# Part I: The Theorem Chain

# 1. Introduction: The Physical Ontology and the Plan of the Chain

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.

*In the author's words — reproduced verbatim and in full from [9], §4.1, §4.3, §4.4 (the Point/Sphere paper; verified-read). Equation and reference numbers are those of [9].*

**4.1 Statement of the principle**

**Principle 5** (McGucken, UNC 1998–99 dissertation appendix; FQXi 2008–13). The fourth dimension expands at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event: dx₄/dt = ic where x₄ = ict is the fourth axis of the four-manifold and c is the universal invariant rate.

The principle is not a postulate or hypothesis; it is established by the McGucken Proof from three independently verified physical premises: (i) the special-relativistic four-speed invariance u^μ u_μ = -c²; (ii) the empirical fact that photons emitted from any source spread spherically and isotropically at c; (iii) the identification of x₄ = ict as a physical axis whose every consequence corresponds to an empirically validated feature of physics. Premises (i) and (ii) are confirmed in every optical and particle-physics experiment performed since the seventeenth century. Premise (iii) is confirmed by the convergent empirical confirmation of every theorem the principle entails: the Schrödinger equation, the Born rule, the canonical commutator [q̂, p̂] = iℏ, the Schwarzschild metric, gravitational time dilation, the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy, the Bell–CHSH–Tsirelson bound. The principle’s physicality is established by the convergence of all three premises, each independently verified.

**4.3 The McGucken Sphere**

**Definition 10** (McGucken Sphere). The *McGucken Sphere* Σ₊(p₀) centered on the spacetime event p₀ = (x⃗₀, t₀) is the future null cone of p₀ — the three-dimensional null hypersurface in 4D Minkowski spacetime traced by the spherically symmetric expansion of x₄ at rate c from p₀. Its time-t cross-section is the 2-sphere Σ₊(p₀, t) = x⃗: \|x⃗ – x⃗₀\| = c(t – t₀) the spherical wavefront at time t. The full 4D object is null-conical; each time slice is a 2-sphere expanding at rate c.

The Sphere is a *physical* structure, not a mathematical construct. By the McGucken Proof, dx₄/dt = ic is a physical fact about the four-manifold; the Sphere is the spacetime locus traced by this physical advance, in the same sense that a particle’s worldline is the spacetime locus traced by the particle’s motion.

**4.4 The four-fold McGucken ontology**

The principle generates a four-fold ontology of spacetime events:

1.  *Absolute rest in x₁ x₂ x₃*: a massive particle at spatial rest, with its full four-velocity budget directed into x₄-advance. This is the rest-frame of a massive particle.
2.  *Absolute rest in x₄*: a photon, with v = c along its null worldline and dx₄/dt = 0 in the photon frame. The photon rides the wavefront and is at *absolute rest in x₄*.
3.  *Absolute motion*: x₄ expansion at ic from every event, the universal substrate dynamic.
4.  *CMB frame*: isotropic cosmological x₄-expansion, the global rest-frame of the universe.

This four-fold ontology is non-trivial. The photon is not in motion in x₄; it is at rest in x₄ and rides on a single Sphere from emission to absorption. This is why photons *remain entangled at any spatial separation*: they share a single Sphere, and from the photon’s perspective the Sphere has not advanced. The McGucken Nonlocality Principle [19: MG-Nonlocality] follows: *nonlocality begins in locality*; only systems whose past Spheres have intersected can ever become entangled.

*(End of the passage from [9], §4.1, §4.3, §4.4.)*

**2. The Primitive and Its Shadow**

Greek indices run μ = 0,1,2,3; the Lorentzian metric is η = diag(+,−,−,−). The Light Time Dimension arena is ℝ⁴ carrying the interval that the primitive (1.1) integrates to,

> ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄²,  dx₄ = ic dt,   …(2.1)

so dx₄² = −c²dt² and (2.1) reproduces the Lorentzian interval dx₁²+dx₂²+dx₃² − c²dt². The single factor of i in (1.1) is the entire content of the Wick relation between the Euclidean arena and the Lorentzian shadow; it is the same i catalogued among the twelve i-insertion cases of the framework. We use this in §6.

**Postulate honesty (audit test 6).** Statements that an abstract ℝ⁴ "is" the x₄-extended arena, that "null = x₄-rest," and that "the i of the spinor phase is the i of dx₄/dt = ic" are *identifications carried by the framework's correspondence*, not coordinate tautologies. They are graded **G2** throughout and never asserted as G1.

**2.1 The rate is a generator; the coordinate is its flow**

The canonical statement that dx₄/dt = ic is primitive and x₄ = ict a "mere integrated shadow" is sharpened by an operator-theoretic fact about order.

**Proposition 2.1 (Generator and flow).** *A first-order operator is the infinitesimal generator of a one-parameter group of motions, recovered by exponentiation: e^{a d/dt} f(t) = f(t+a), a translation. A second-order operator generates no such group; its exponential is a smoothing semigroup (a ≥ 0 only), not a translation. Hence the primitive dx₄/dt = ic, being first-order, is a generator whose exponential is the x₄-flow — the motion — while x₄ = ∫ ic dt = ict is the integrated trace of that flow.*

*Proof.* On the eigenfunction e^{kt}, (d/dt)e^{kt} = k e^{kt}, so e^{a d/dt} e^{kt} = Σ_n (ak)ⁿ/n! · e^{kt} = e^{ak} e^{kt} = e^{k(t+a)} (verified by truncated series); thus e^{a d/dt} is the shift. For d²/dt², e^{a d²/dt²} e^{kt} = e^{ak²} e^{kt} rescales amplitude and does not translate; positivity of k² restricts it to a semigroup. ∎ **G1.**

**Remark 2.2 (Atiyah's first-order principle; the i as unitarity).** Atiyah stressed that the first-order operator is the more fundamental object precisely because it exponentiates to a finite motion, whereas a second-order operator cannot — one can exponentiate Dirac's first-order operator to a translation but not the Klein–Gordon operator to the same effect [Atiyah, *What is a Spinor?*]. This is the operator-level form of the Light Time Dimension doctrine that the rate dx₄/dt = ic is primitive and x₄ = ict its shadow. Moreover, by Stone's theorem a one-parameter group of *norm-preserving* (unitary) motions has anti-Hermitian generator iH: the factor i in the primitive is exactly what makes the x₄-flow unitary — the same i that is the Born-norm complex structure of Theorem 5.6 and the spinor phase of Proposition 6.1. First-order, imaginary, motion-generating: one statement. The spinor transport q = exp(½ θ n̂·J⃗) of §9 is itself the exponential of such a first-order generator (verified: q(2π) = −𝟙).

**Remark 2.3 (Independent convergence: Atiyah's uniqueness of the first-order generator).** In a separate lecture — *From Quantum Physics to Number Theory* (2010) — Atiyah reaches the same first-order primitive from a wholly independent motivation, and in doing so supplies a *uniqueness* clause that strengthens Remark 2.2. Asking how one can define a notion of translation (retardation) in Minkowski space, where there is no distinguished time direction, he observes that the infinitesimal generator of a one-parameter translation is the derivative, so translation may be read as the exponential of a first-order operator — the operator-level statement of Proposition 2.1 — and then concludes that there is *only one* first-order differential operator invariant under the Lorentz group: the Dirac operator. In his words, the construction can be carried through "because you have this Dirac operator… there's no other solution… Dirac discovered this was the only operator you can use." This is the uniqueness Remark 2.2 left implicit. Within Light Time Dimension the content is read with the canonical ontology held exactly: the imaginary unit is the *perpendicularity flag of the fourth dimension* — not a marker of "imaginary time" — and the parameter t is not a coordinate the advance occurs *within* but the reading our clocks return as they trace the x₄-expansion. Atiyah's unique first-order Lorentz-invariant generator is then, in Light Time Dimension, the single generator dx₄/dt = ic whose exponential is the x₄-flow that clocks trace. The convergence is independent in the strong sense: Atiyah arrives at the first-order generator from the retardation problem, never naming dx₄/dt = ic, McGucken, or the present framework; the talk predates and is unaware of the corpus. That a Fields- and Abel-laureate geometer reaches the *target* — first-order Lorentz-invariant generator, unique, exponentiating to motion — by a route that never touches the primitive is evidence that the target is real and that the *identification* of that unique generator with the physical advance dx₄/dt = ic is the framework's own contribution. **G2** (the identification of Atiyah's unique generator with the primitive; the uniqueness and the generator-of-translation facts are Atiyah's, cited).

**II.8 Two Integrals of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic: the Channels as a Lie Correspondence, and the Principle as the Differential Wick Rotation**

The two derivation channels of II.5–II.6, the coordinate and metric of II.1, and the phase of II.2 are related by the two elementary operations of calculus. Making that relationship precise connects this paper to two of the oldest correspondences in mathematics, and it explains in one stroke why general relativity, built on the same principle, shows no oscillation while quantum mechanics does.

**Proposition (two integrals of the generator).** Read as a generator, the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic — the constant element ic of the one-dimensional Lie algebra u(1) = iℝ — admits two integrals:

1.  the *additive* integral x₄ = ∫₀ᵗ ic ds = ict, a straight advance along the imaginary axis (d²x₄/dt² = 0), whose square dx₄² = −c²dt² builds the Lorentzian metric of II.1;
2.  the *multiplicative* integral, the exponential map exp(∫ i · … ) = e^(iθ), a point circulating on the unit circle (|e^(iθ)| = 1), which is the wavefront phase of II.2.

The additive integral flattens the per-increment rotation into a fixed rotated axis; the multiplicative integral keeps it live. The maps d/dt and ∫ dt carry the coordinate x₄ = ict and the generator dx₄/dt = ic into one another, inverse up to the initial value x₄(0) by the fundamental theorem of calculus.

*Proof.* Direct, and confirmed by computer algebra. ∫₀ᵗ ic ds = ict and d(ict)/dt = ic; d²(ict)/dt² = 0. From dx₄ = ic dt, dx₄² = −c²dt², so ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c²dt², the Lorentzian metric of II.1. The exponential map carries ic ∈ u(1) to the circle U(1); the compounded quarter-turns close, e^(iθ) = lim (1 + iθ/n)^n as n → ∞, with |e^(iθ)| = 1. ∎

**The two channels as a Lie-algebra / Lie-group correspondence.** The differential form dx₄/dt = ic — the active wavefront advance that the geometric-propagation channel of II.5 works with — is the infinitesimal generator, a Lie-algebra element. The accumulated parameter x₄ = ict, which underlies the fixed Minkowski metric on which the algebraic-symmetry channel of II.6 operates, is the argument of the exponential. The two elementary operations of calculus are the maps between them: d/dt extracts the generator from the coordinate, ∫ dt accumulates the generator into the coordinate. At the group level, exp sends the generator ic to the flow e^(iθ) and its inverse log returns it. This is the Lie-algebra ↔ Lie-group correspondence, specialized to u(1) → U(1) — one of the foundational facts of modern mathematics — realized here by the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, with d/dt and ∫ dt as the maps between the two channels.

One point of terminology must be marked, to prevent a conflation. The words *algebraic* and *geometric* in the channel names of II.5–II.6 denote method: the algebra of symmetry generators, against the geometry of wavefront propagation. That axis differs from the sense the same words carry in the Lie correspondence, where the Lie algebra is the infinitesimal object and the Lie group is the global manifold. On the Lie axis, the geometric-propagation channel's form dx₄/dt = ic sits on the infinitesimal (algebra) side, and the algebraic-symmetry channel's integrated metric sits on the global (group) side — the reverse assignment. The two axes are transverse, and "algebraic channel" should not be read as "Lie algebra." What is robust under either naming is the operational statement: d/dt and ∫ dt, equivalently log and exp, are the maps between the differential generator dx₄/dt = ic and the integrated coordinate x₄ = ict together with its flow e^(iθ).

**The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic as the differential form of the Wick rotation.** The principle states that each increment dt is multiplied by i to give dx₄/c — a rotation by π/2 in the complex plane, applied to every infinitesimal increment. That is a Wick rotation carried out as continuous dynamics. The textbook Wick rotation t → iτ, equivalently x₄ = ict, is its integrated form: ∫₀ᵗ ic ds = ict = x₄ descends from dx₄/dt = ic by integration and is the accumulation of the per-increment rotations. The standard once-and-for-all Wick rotation is therefore the finite form of the incremental Wick rotation of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, and the Lorentzian signature of II.1, dx₄² = −c²dt², is what that finite rotation produces from the manifestly Euclidean dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄². The framework performs no Wick rotation after the fact; the rotation is stamped on every increment of dx₄/dt = ic, and x₄ = ict is that rotation accumulated and held fixed.

**Why general relativity shows no oscillation, though the oscillation is present at every event.** General relativity is written on the coordinate x₄ — the additive integral, the metric of II.1. There the per-increment i has been spent on the signature, and the phase oscillation of II.2 appears as monotone exponential behavior rather than as oscillation: the rest-frame phase that oscillates as e^(−iω_C t) in real time is the real exponential e^(−cmx₄/ℏ) written on the imaginary x₄-axis (confirmed by computer algebra — this is the Wick relationship, oscillation in real time being exponential decay in imaginary time). Quantum mechanics is written on the differential form: the Schrödinger equation iℏ ∂_tψ = Ĥψ carries the i on the first time-derivative, so the compounded-i mechanism of II.2 is active on the phase fibre and produces the unitary rotation of the wavefunction. Both formalisms descend from dx₄/dt = ic — general relativity by integrating the differential content out into the metric, quantum mechanics by keeping it active on the phase fibre. The appearance that general relativity is not quantum-mechanical records which integral one takes: the additive integral hides the oscillation in the signature, the multiplicative integral displays it as the wave. The oscillation is present in the generator at every event, and the additive integral flattens it into the fixed metric.

**The Schrödinger equation and its propagator as the two integrals.** The same pattern organizes the nonrelativistic limit of II.7. The Schrödinger equation iℏ ∂_tψ = Ĥψ is the differential form — the generator −iĤ/ℏ acting on the wavefunction fibre, the compounded-i mechanism of II.2 lifted to Hilbert space. Its multiplicative integral is the propagator U(t) = exp(−iĤt/ℏ), which is unitary (confirmed: U†U = 𝟙) and therefore a rotation of the state vector. The equation is the generator, the propagator is its exponential, and the i on the time-derivative is the same i as in the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic.

**The broader duality.** The pair (d, ∫) acting between the differential and integrated forms is one instance of a general algebra–geometry duality: Cartan's exterior calculus and Stokes' theorem ∫_M dω = ∮_(∂M) ω, of which ∫₀ᵗ d(x₄) = ict is the elementary case; and, at the level of correspondences, the Lie-algebra / Lie-group, connection / holonomy (Ambrose–Singer), and Gelfand dualities. The relationship isolated here is a specific physical instance of that pattern, with dx₄/dt = ic on the differential side and x₄ = ict on the integrated side. At the level of quantum field theory the same relationship appears as the Wightman ↔ Osterwalder–Schrader correspondence between Minkowski and Euclidean formulations, related by Wick rotation; the companion papers develop that case.

As with the wavefront reading of II.2, this is geometric content of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. The physical scales are the separate input: the flow's rate ω_C = mc²/ℏ needs the action quantum ℏ, and the metric's physical units need c. The geometry gives the two integrals and the rotation between them; c and ℏ set the rate of the one and the unit of the other.

# 2. The Lorentzian Signature and the Four-Velocity Budget

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.

*In the author's words — reproduced verbatim and in full from [5], §II.1 (the Dirac paper; verified-read). Equation and reference numbers are those of [5].*

**II.1 The Light, Time, Dimension Theory Principle and the Minkowski Signature**

The Light, Time, Dimension Theory principle asserts:


dx₄/dt = ic


The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic states that the fourth dimension x₄ expands at the velocity of light, carrying an intrinsic factor of i. Integrating dx₄/dt = ic gives x₄ = ict, so the fourth coordinate is complex-valued when expressed in units of real time. The content of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is the active expansion. x₄ = ict descends from dx₄/dt = ic by integration and is the coordinate shadow of that advance; the physics lives in dx₄/dt = ic — the fourth dimension advancing as a spherically symmetric wavefront at the velocity of light from every event. Because that wavefront advances at a definite speed, it carries a definite wavelength and frequency, and therefore a phase and an action; c and ℏ are the two faces of this one advance. As we make explicit in II.2 and Section VIII, the Compton-frequency oscillation of matter is nothing other than this wavefront’s own phase, so that the dynamics of the Dirac field are already implicit in the premise rather than imposed upon it.

This single equation fixes the metric signature of spacetime. The infinitesimal invariant interval built from (dx₁, dx₂, dx₃, dx₄) is:


ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄²


which looks Euclidean. But substituting dx₄ = ic dt gives dx₄² = -c² dt², so:


ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² - c²dt²


This is the Minkowski interval with signature η = diag(+1, +1, +1, −1), or equivalently η = diag(−1, +1, +1, +1) if we index time first. The Lorentzian signature is not imposed — it emerges directly from the i in dx₄/dt = ic. Wick rotation, conventionally presented as a calculational trick for converting between Euclidean and Lorentzian frameworks, is in Light, Time, Dimension Theory the statement that real time and complex x₄ are related by the principle itself.

*(End of the passage from [5], §II.1.)*

*In the author's words — reproduced verbatim and in full from [6], §11.1, §11.2, §11.3, §5.2 (the spinor paper; verified-read). Equation and reference numbers are those of [6].*

**11.1 The null cone is the spherical expansion at c (Theorem 11.1)**

> **Theorem 11.1 (The causal structure is the expansion at c).** *Let (V,η) be the observed Lorentzian spacetime and p₀ = (x₀, t₀) any event. The future null cone of p₀, C⁺(p₀) = { p=(x,t) : η(p−p₀, p−p₀)=0, t>t₀ }, intersects each later slice {t = const > t₀} in the metric 2-sphere Σ(p₀,t) = { x : |x−x₀| = c(t−t₀) } of radius r(t) = c(t−t₀) expanding at the rate ṙ = c. The assignment p₀ ↦ {C⁺(p₀)} is the conformal (causal) structure of η, and by the Hawking–King–McCarthy theorem the conformal structure determines η up to a positive scalar factor. Consequently the family of spheres expanding at c from every event is a complete invariant of the metric's causal content.*

*Proof.* The null condition η(p−p₀,p−p₀)=0 reads −c²(t−t₀)² + |x−x₀|² = 0, hence |x−x₀| = c|t−t₀|; the future branch gives the stated sphere, with ṙ = d[c(t−t₀)]/dt = c (verified symbolically). That the collection of null cones recovers η up to conformal factor is the Hawking–King–McCarthy theorem (Hawking, King & McCarthy 1976; Malament 1977). The residual scalar factor is the volume element, fixed by the proper-time normalization of Theorem 11.3. ∎ **G1.**

> **Remark 11.2 (Why "static" does not weaken Theorem 11.1).** A spacetime is *static* when it admits a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing field, equivalently when g_μν is t-independent in an adapted chart. Staticity is a symmetry of the metric *components*; it is silent about the null cone, which exists and expands at c at every event of *any* Lorentzian metric. In Schwarzschild the metric is static yet the local null cones expand at c exactly as in Minkowski (invariance of the local light-speed); the global tilting of those cones is the gravitational field. The Schwarzschild objection — "the metric is static, so nothing moves" — confuses a symmetry of the components with the absence of the cone. The cone is never absent. In particular **Minkowski space is not a static counterexample to the moving dimension; its defining structure is the expansion at c from every event.**

**11.2 The four-velocity normalization is dx₄/dt = ic at rest (Theorem 11.3)**

> **Theorem 11.3 (The advance at c is the metric's own normalization).** *For the observed Lorentzian metric the following are equivalent. (i) The metric has signature (1,3) with proper time η(dp,dp) = −c² dτ². (ii) Every massive worldline has four-velocity u^μ = dx^μ/dτ obeying u^μ u_μ = −c². (iii) In the encoding x₄ = ic t, every worldline at spatial rest obeys dx₄/dτ = ic, i.e. dx₄/dt = ic; a general worldline obeys the Euclidean-form normalization u₄² + u_x² + u_y² + u_z² = −c² with u₄ = ic(dt/dτ) imaginary. Each implication is an identity, not an extra hypothesis: dx₄/dt = ic is the rest-frame statement of the metric's four-velocity normalization.*

*Proof.* (i)⇒(ii): divide η(dp,dp) = −c²dτ² by dτ². (ii)⇒(iii): u^μu_μ = −c²(dt/dτ)² + |ẋ|² = −c²; at spatial rest ẋ=0 so dt/dτ = 1, and under x₄ = ic t, dx₄/dτ = ic(dt/dτ) = ic, i.e. dx₄/dt = ic (verified symbolically); for general worldlines u₄² = −c²(dt/dτ)² gives u₄² + |ẋ|² = −c². (iii)⇒(i): squaring dx₄ = ic dt gives dx₄² = −c²dt², so ds² = dx₄² + dx² = −c²dt² + dx², recovering signature (1,3). ∎ **G1.**

> **Corollary 11.4 (The advance is observed, not posited).** *The normalization u^μu_μ = −c² asserts that every massive body advances through the timelike direction at the invariant rate c: at rest the entire four-velocity budget goes to this advance, |u₄| = c; in spatial motion part is traded to the spatial sector (time dilation, dt/dτ = γ). This advance is directly measured — differential clock ageing, dilated muon lifetimes, satellite-navigation frequency offsets. The "motion" in dx₄/dt = ic is the elapse of proper time, an empirically confirmed feature of the observed metric, not an overlay.* ∎ **G1.**

**11.3 The i is forced by, and equivalent to, the timelike minus sign (Theorem 11.5)**

> **Theorem 11.5 (Signature ⟺ the imaginary unit).** *Let the timelike contribution be −c² dt². The substitution x₄ = k c t renders the interval a sum of four squares iff k² = −1, i.e. k = ±i. Hence (a) the imaginary unit in x₄ = ict is the unique (up to sign) scalar effecting the Lorentzian-to-Euclidean form change, existing iff the signature carries the timelike minus sign; (b) by Theorem 11.3 that minus sign is u·u = −c², the advance at c. So the i of x₄ = ict is the algebraic marker of the timelike advance: no minus sign ⟺ no advance ⟺ no such i.*

*Proof.* Demand (k c t)² = −c²t²; then k² = −1, so k = ±i and no real k suffices (verified symbolically) — (a). For (b), (a) ties the i to the timelike minus sign and Theorem 11.3 identifies that minus sign with u·u = −c² (Corollary 11.4, the advance at c). The biconditional chain: timelike i exists ⟺ minus sign present ⟺ u·u = −c² ⟺ advance at c. ∎ **G1.**

> **Remark 11.6 (The real-metric objection, answered exactly).** It is correct that the *Lorentzian* metric in its native form contains no i: η = diag(−1,+1,+1,+1) is real, and the interval is a real number, positive, negative, or null. The i is the unique unit *encoding* the real minus sign as a fourth square, x₄ = ict. Theorem 11.5 makes this exact: the i and the minus sign are interchangeable descriptions of the *same* datum — the timelike direction — and that datum is, by Theorem 11.3, the advance at c. "There is no i in the metric" and "the metric's timelike structure is the i" are both true and compatible: the real minus sign and the imaginary unit are two notations for the one timelike advance. What is *not* available is a tertium quid — a Lorentzian timelike direction that is neither the real minus sign nor (equivalently) the i.

**5.2 The budget identity: the magnitude c enters here, and only here**

We isolate the single place in the entire development where the *magnitude* c — the motion itself, beyond the existence of a fourth axis — is load-bearing. Sections 3, 4, 6 and 7 require only the imaginary fourth axis (the signature, i.e. the factor i recoverable from the shadow x₄ = ict); the rate magnitude is, there, a unit convention. The exception is the identification of §5.1, which we now derive rather than assume.

**Proposition 5.2 (Four-velocity budget identity).** *From dx₄ = ic dt and the interval (2.1), a worldline of spatial speed v has proper-advance rate dτ/dt = √(1 − v²/c²). Defining the x₄-advance speed w := c (dτ/dt), the four-velocity budget is Pythagorean and saturated at c,*

> v² + w² = c²,   …(5.1)

*so the x₄-rest locus w = 0 is exactly the locus v = c.*

*Proof.* With dx₄ = ic dt, the interval (2.1) is ds² = d**x**² − c²dt² = −c²dτ², whence dτ/dt = √(1 − v²/c²). Then w² = c²(1 − v²/c²) = c² − v², so v² + w² = c² identically (verified symbolically). Setting w = 0 gives v = c. ∎

Equation (5.1) is the saturated form of "every event advances through the four-space at the single rate c": spatial motion and x₄-advance trade against a fixed budget of magnitude c. A massive particle at spatial rest (v = 0) spends the whole budget on x₄-advance (w = c); the photon (v = c) spends none (w = 0) and is at rest in x₄ — recovering canonical ontology (ii) as a *theorem* rather than a postulate. **G1.**

**Theorem 5.3 (Null cone = x₄-rest, derived — upgrade of Theorem 5.1 to G1).** *The spinor's bilinear square is null and hence sits at v = c (Thm 3.2). By Proposition 5.2 the x₄-rest locus is also v = c. Therefore the spinor's null square lies on the x₄-rest locus as a derived identity, not an assumed bridge.*

*Proof.* Immediate from Thm 3.2 (p² = 0 ⇒ v = c) and Prop 5.2 (w = 0 ⇔ v = c). ∎

This removes ontology (ii) as a standalone postulate underwriting Theorem 5.1: "null = x₄-rest" is now a consequence of the budget identity, which is a consequence of the single-c interval (2.1). The only residual input is that the interval is the one built by the expansion — the framework's definition, not an added assumption. Theorem 5.1 is thereby **G1**.

*(End of the passage from [6], §11.1, §11.2, §11.3, §5.2.)*

**Theorem 2.3 (The four-velocity budget; the photon at absolute rest in x₄).** *Let a worldline have spatial speed v. (i) is Theorem 2.3; v ≤c and v_{x₄} ≤c follow from v² + v_{x₄}² = c² with both squares nonnegative, and the locus in the (v, v_{x₄}) quarter-plane is the circle of radius c. **A.3.2 What does "the x₄-rate at the horizon" mean?** The rate is gravity-rigid: ∂(dx₄/dt)/∂g_μν = 0. The rate dx₄/dt = ic takes the same value near the horizon as at infinity. What varies with potential is the share: v_x₄(r) = c dτ/dt = c √(1 − r_s/r) (static Schwarzschild observer), vanishing at r = r_s. On the infaller's own clock dτ = dt locally and the reverse-reading equivalence applies: the local rate is the full ic throughout. Gravitational time dilation is the coordinate-frame projection of a locally invariant rate.

**A.3.3 Which identity is "c² through spacetime"?** Sphere partition (per coordinate time, all worldlines): v² + v_x₄² = c², bounded, locus a quarter-circle. Lorentzian four-velocity norm (per proper time, massive worldlines): u^μ u_μ = |dx₄/dτ|² − |d**x**/dτ|² = −c², unbounded in each term, signature difference fixing the invariant. The Euclidean per-proper-time sum |dx₄/dτ|² + |d**x**/dτ|² equals c² only in the instantaneous rest frame; elsewhere c²γ². Plus-sign identities belong to (R2); minus-sign identities to (R3).

**A.3.4 How does the twin paradox read?** Coordinate accumulation is path-independent: both twins accumulate Δx₄ = ic Δt. Differential ageing is read from X₄ = ∫ ic dτ, advancing at real magnitude v_x₄ per unit coordinate time. On the traveling leg v_x₄ < c, so the traveler accumulates less X₄, so less proper time. The stay-at-home twin retains v_x₄ = c and accumulates the maximal X₄. The CTC question closes the same way: ∮ dx₄ = 0 identically, so a CTC cannot run on the coordinate; the impossibility lives in X₄.

**A.3.5 γ-projection and rapidity.** A boost is hyperbolic: rapidity φ with cosh φ = γ. The Sphere-partition projection is circular: Sphere angle θ with sin θ = v/c, cos θ = v_x₄/c = 1/γ. Related by the Gudermannian, θ = gd(φ), so cos θ = sech φ. The 1/γ projection is about θ; unbounded component growth is about φ.

**A.4 Why Nothing of Relativity Is Lost** The fourth dimension advances at the same rate at every event; worldlines differ only in how much of that advance they share in. Massive at rest shares fully (v_x₄ = c); moving shares less (v_x₄ = √(c² − v²), clock slowed by the Lorentz factor); photon does not share at all (v_x₄ = 0, ageless, no X₄). Lorentz invariance survives entire because the invariant content — the norm u^μu_μ = −c² and the metric — is a theorem of the Principle (the metric is the pullback of the Euclidean form along x₄ = ict, the −c² from (ic)²). Lorentz transformations preserve that derived metric; γ, time dilation, length contraction, E = γmc², the null cone, and the mass-shell all come out unchanged. The foliation quantities v_x₄ and X₄ are additional bookkeeping frame-anchored to the cosmic-comoving foliation (the CMB rest frame); the McGucken Cloaking Theorem (Theorem 39 of §50) explains why local metrology cannot detect them. General relativity survives by the invariant/deformable split within the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework: the rate is gravity-rigid; gravity deforms the spatial sector. Time dilation, redshift, light bending, perihelion advance, the horizon, and the field equations are recovered exactly. The horizon is where the share is extinguished; the expansion does not stop.

# 3. The Wavefront: Wavelength, Compton Frequency, Phase, and the Klein–Gordon and Schrödinger Equations

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.

*In the author's words — reproduced verbatim and in full from [5], §II.2, §II.5, §II.6, §II.7 (the Dirac paper; verified-read). Equation and reference numbers are those of [5].*

**II.2 Matter as an x₄-Standing Wave**

In the Light, Time, Dimension Theory framework, matter is a standing oscillation in x₄ at the Compton frequency:


ψ(x₄) ∝ e^{ikx₄}, where k = mc/ħ


For a particle at rest, all of its “motion” is the x₄-expansion at rate c. The rest energy E = mc² is interpreted as the rate of x₄-phase accumulation per unit proper time. A photon, having no rest frame, is a pure x₄-oscillation with k₀ = 0; it expands along x₄ at rate c with no standing-wave component.

This interpretation of matter is central to what follows. Matter is a phase structure carried forward by the x₄-expansion of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. This phase structure has an orientation: it points in the direction of increasing x₄. Section IV will make this orientation mathematically precise as an algebraic constraint on even-grade multivectors.

This is the physical content of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic made concrete. The standing oscillation is the phase of the spherically symmetric x₄-wavefront, sampled at the Compton frequency ω_C = mc²/ℏ. The ℏ here is the quantum of action carried by the same advance whose propagation speed is c — the twin property of the one wavefront. The spinor lives on a wavefront that already oscillates at the Compton frequency, and its rest-frame evolution e^(−imc²t/ℏ) is that wavefront’s own phase advance. The dynamics were in the premise.

**Oscillation as geometric content.** It is worth being exact about how much of this the geometry gives on its own, because the precise claim is the stronger one. Read the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic as a connection on the phase carried by the advance: at each increment dx₄ = ic · dt, the factor i applies a quarter-turn — a rotation by π/2, since i = e^(iπ/2) — to the phase riding on the advance. Compounding the quarter-turns is the exponential map,


e^{iθ} = lim_{n→∞}(1 + (iθ)/n)ⁿ


a product of many perpendicular kicks, which is circular rotation. Phase, periodicity, and wavelike circulation are therefore already present in dx₄/dt = ic, before any quantum postulate is added. The i does the whole of this work: a real advance dx₄/dt = c, without the i, integrates to x₄ = ct and only translates — it never oscillates. It is the perpendicularity of the fourth axis, the i, that turns advance into circulation, and the closure i⁴ = 1 — the quarter-turn returning to its start after four steps — is why the phase is periodic at all, closing once per cycle rather than spiraling. The qualitative wave character of matter, that it has a phase and oscillates, is geometric content of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, not a separate quantum-mechanical postulate.

**What the geometry does not fix: the frequency scale.** The geometry gives that there is oscillation and that it is periodic; it does not by itself give the rate of that oscillation as a physical frequency. A quarter-turn per increment of x₄-advance is dimensionless geometry. Turning it into a physical frequency ω_C = mc²/ℏ requires an action scale — the action the wavefront carries per cycle, the quantum ℏ (II.5). A phase is dimensionless, φ = S/ℏ, and the only way to convert an accumulated action S into a pure number is to divide by an action; that action is ℏ. The honest division is therefore: the wavelike oscillation exists as pure geometry, forced by dx₄/dt = ic; that it runs at the Compton frequency mc²/ℏ requires ℏ, which the bare principle does not fix. The geometry gives the wave; ℏ gives its pitch. In the wavefront reading, the wave is in the premise; its pitch is not.

**The wave rides the fibre; the coordinate translates.** One distinction keeps the claim exact. The oscillation lives on the fibre — the phase riding the advance — while the coordinate x₄ itself translates straight. Because dx₄/dt = ic is constant, d²x₄/dt² = 0: the coordinate advances uniformly along its rotated axis and does not orbit. The statement dx₄/dt = ic gives oscillation is precise if it means the phase on the fibre oscillates, which it does, and would be wrong if it meant the coordinate x₄ itself circulates, which it does not. This is the addition-versus-multiplication distinction of the coordinate shadow made physical: added head-to-tail, the quarter-turned increments sum to the straight advance x₄ = ∫ ic dt, which descends from dx₄/dt = ic by integration; compounded multiplicatively, the same increments close into the phase e^(iθ). The particle worldline is the sum, the wave is the product, and both are the one stream of quarter-turned increments dx₄ = ic · dt.

**II.5 The Klein–Gordon Equation from the Wavefront (Channel B: Geometric Propagation)**

The physical state established in II.2 — x₄ advancing as a spherically symmetric wavefront at the velocity of light, carrying wavelength, frequency, phase, and therefore action — already contains the relativistic wave equation for a spin-0 field. We extract it here directly from the wavefront geometry, performing no canonical quantization. This is **Channel B** of the Light, Time, Dimension Theory architecture: the geometric-propagation channel, in which dynamics arise from the self-consistent superposition of expanding McGucken Spheres.

**Theorem (Klein–Gordon from the McGucken-Sphere wavefront).** Let matter of rest mass m be a phase structure carried on the spherically symmetric x₄-wavefront of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, with the Minkowski signature η = diag(−1, +1, +1, +1) of II.1. Then the field ψ satisfies


(□- m²c²/ħ²) ψ = 0, □≡∂^μ ∂_μ = -(1/c²)∂ₜ² + ∇².


*Proof, in six steps — each a property of the advance, none a quantization postulate.*

**Step 1 — Mass shell from the McGucken Principle.** The four-velocity normalization u^μu_μ = −c² is the four-vector form of dx₄/dt = ic: the proper advance is the timelike unit four-vector scaled by c, its squared norm fixed by the signature of II.1. Multiplying by m², the four-momentum p^μ = m u^μ obeys


p^μ p_μ = -m²c².


This *mass shell* is the geometric locus on which the wavefront advance is consistent with rest mass m. (Symbolically verified: with E² = p²c² + m²c⁴, p^μp_μ = −(E/c)² + p² = −m²c².)

**Step 2 — Compton frequency from action quantization.** By II.2 the wavefront carries one quantum of action ℏ per oscillation; ℏ and c are the twin properties of the one advance. In the rest frame the intrinsic oscillation is the Compton frequency ω_C = mc²/ℏ, with Compton wavelength λ_C = ℏ/mc. Writing k^μ = p^μ/ℏ for the four-wavevector, the mass shell of Step 1 becomes, by the Lorentz covariance of the II.1 metric,

k^μk_μ = −m²c²/ℏ², in every frame.

**Step 3 — Plane-wave wavefront mode.** The phase accumulated along a straight worldline is S = ∫ p_μ dx^μ, so an elementary mode of the McGucken-Sphere expansion at four-wavevector k^μ is


ψ(x) = exp(i k_ν x^ν) = exp(iS/ħ).


This is the physical content made explicit: the phase is the action carried by the advance, measured in the ℏ the advance itself sets.

**Step 4 — The d'Alembertian extracts the mass shell.** Applying □ to the mode,


□ψ = ∂^μ ∂_μ exp(i k_ν x^ν) = (i k^μ)(i k_μ) ψ = -k^μ k_μ ψ = (m²c²/ħ²) ψ,


using Step 2. Hence (□- m²c²/ħ²) ψ = 0. The Klein–Gordon equation is nothing but the differential expression of the mass-shell constraint of Step 1. No canonical quantization was performed — it fell out of the wavefront kinematics. (Symbolically verified: □ψ/ψ = ω²/c² − k², and □ψ = (m²c²/ℏ²)ψ is equivalent to the relativistic dispersion ω² = c²k² + m²c⁴/ℏ².)

**Step 5 — Huygens–Fresnel–Kirchhoff form (the integral statement).** The same content has an integral expression. Each point of a Cauchy surface emits an elementary expanding McGucken Sphere — a secondary wavefront — and the field at a later event is their superposition. The Klein–Gordon equation is precisely the self-consistency (Huygens) condition on that superposition: the Kirchhoff–Helmholtz integral over the secondary McGucken Spheres reproduces the field if and only if each mode satisfies Step 4. Channel B therefore has a differential face (Step 4) and an integral face (Step 5), both asserting that the wavefront propagates consistently on the mass shell.

**Step 6 — Massless limit.** Setting m = 0 collapses the mass shell onto the null cone, k^μk_μ = 0, and Klein–Gordon becomes □ψ = 0. The mode propagates on the null cone at c with no Compton frequency — the photon, which in the Light, Time, Dimension Theory ontology is unlocked x₄-content at absolute rest in x₄, with no oscillation in proper time. ∎

The inputs are exactly the wavefront kinematics named in the abstract — the Compton wavelength λ_C, the frequency ω_C, the phase k_νx^ν, and the action ℏ. Each is a property of the spherically symmetric advance of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. **The dynamics were in the premise.**

**II.6 The Klein–Gordon Equation by Algebraic Symmetry (Channel A)**

The same equation follows through **Channel A**, the algebraic-symmetry channel, in which dynamics arise from the symmetry generators and their algebra rather than from wavefront superposition. The two derivations are independent in method and identical in result; their agreement is the dual-channel consistency that recurs throughout the Light, Time, Dimension Theory program.

Translation invariance of the II.1 metric makes the four-momentum p_μ the conserved generator of spacetime translations (Noether). On the wavefront mode ψ = exp(i k_νx^ν) = exp(iS/ℏ) of II.5, that generator is represented by

p_μ ↦ −iℏ ∂_μ, since −iℏ ∂_μ exp(iS/ℏ) = (∂_μ S) exp(iS/ℏ) = p_μ exp(iS/ℏ).

This operator correspondence is read directly off the wavefront phase of II.2, in which ℏ is the action carried by the same advance whose speed is c. Substituting it into the mass-shell Casimir p^μp_μ = −m²c² of II.5 Step 1,


p^μ p_μ ψ = -m²c² ψ ⟹(-iħ∂^μ)(-iħ∂_μ) ψ = -m²c² ψ ⟹-ħ² □ψ = -m²c² ψ,


so once more (□- m²c²/ħ²) ψ = 0. Channel A obtains Klein–Gordon as the algebraic image of the Poincaré Casimir — the mass-shell symmetry expressed on the generators — while Channel B (II.5) obtains it as the geometric self-consistency of the McGucken-Sphere superposition. Both descend from dx₄/dt = ic: Channel A through the translation generators of the metric the principle produces, Channel B through the propagation of the wavefront the principle *is*. The canonical-quantization route of the textbooks is the special case of Channel A in which p_μ ↦ −iℏ∂_μ is postulated; here it is derived from the wavefront phase, and ℏ is the action quantum of the advance.

**II.7 The Schrödinger Equation as the Nonrelativistic Limit (Both Channels)**

The nonrelativistic Schrödinger equation follows from Klein–Gordon — through either channel, since both yield the same operator — by factoring out the fast Compton oscillation of II.2 and retaining the slow envelope. Write


ψ(x, t) = φ(x, t) ·exp(-i mc²t/ħ),


separating the intrinsic wavefront phase exp(−iω_C t), ω_C = mc²/ℏ, from a slowly varying envelope φ. Substituting into the Klein–Gordon equation written as (1/c²)∂_t²ψ − ∇²ψ + (m²c²/ℏ²)ψ = 0 and dividing out the common phase yields, *exactly*,

(1/c²) ∂_t²φ − 2i (m/ℏ) ∂_tφ − ∇²φ = 0.

The two mass terms cancel identically: the rest-energy phase has absorbed the m²c²/ℏ² term, which is why none survives. (Symbolically verified: the residual after substitution is exactly (1/c²)φ_tt − 2i(m/ℏ)φ_t − ∇²φ, the mass term cancelling to zero.) In the nonrelativistic regime the envelope varies slowly on the Compton time scale, |∂_t²φ| ≪ (mc²/ℏ)|∂_tφ|, so the first term is negligible against the second, leaving

−2i(m/ℏ) ∂_tφ − ∇²φ = 0 ⟺ iħ∂ₜφ = -(ħ²/2m) ∇²φ,

the free Schrödinger equation. A scalar potential V enters through the same minimal-coupling/gauge structure that Channel A supplies, giving iℏ∂_tφ = [−(ℏ²/2m)∇² + V] φ.

The two channels read this single limit differently and consistently. In **Channel B**, Schrödinger is the slow envelope of the wavefront phase once the fast Compton oscillation is divided out: the envelope diffuses by Huygens superposition over the spatial McGucken Spheres, the imaginary diffusion coefficient iℏ/2m being the residue of the wavefront's own phase advance. In **Channel A**, it is the nonrelativistic contraction of the Poincaré symmetry to the Galilean symmetry — the c → ∞ limit of the Casimir operator of II.6. Either way, the nonrelativistic quantum mechanics invoked in Section X, and the Dirac–von Neumann structure beyond it, are downstream of the same advance: c, ℏ, and the phase were fixed by dx₄/dt = ic before any wave equation was written. **The dynamics were in the premise.**

**9.2B The null-direction coordinate inherits the wavefront's frequency: c and ℏ as twin properties of the one advance**

Theorem 9.4A exhibits the spinor as the coordinate π_{A′} on the Sphere's null directions. A coordinate on a static sphere of directions would be inert — frequency-free, mass-free. The McGucken Sphere is not static: by the principle, x₄ expands as a *spherically-symmetric wavefront* at c (Thm 11.1: the null cone is the expanding sphere of the advance). The wavefront character is what endows the null-direction coordinate with dynamical content, and it does so without any input beyond the principle read as a wavefront.

> **Theorem 9.4C (The advancing wavefront carries wavelength, frequency, and action; the spinor inherits the Compton frequency).** *Let x₄ advance as a spherically-symmetric wavefront at speed c, as dx₄/dt = ic states under the active-expansion reading. Then:*
>
> *(i) [Periodicity is intrinsic to the wavefront.] A wavefront is a surface of constant phase; a phase-bearing advance at speed c has a wavelength λ and a frequency f related by λf = c. Wavelength and frequency are therefore not additional inputs — they are entailed by the word "wavefront." (A null cone with no periodicity is a moving boundary, not a wavefront.)*
>
> *(ii) [Phase forces an action scale.] The phase φ of a matter wavefront is an action divided by a quantum of action: φ = S/ℏ. A wavefront that carries phase therefore carries an action-per-cycle; call its value ℏ. Thus the advance has an action quantum as a property of its own periodicity, not as a foreign constant — c is the wavefront's rate, ℏ its action-per-cycle, λf = c tying them. To the extent that this action-per-cycle is a single universal constant (one wavefront structure, not one per system), it is Planck's constant.*
>
> *(iii) [The spinor inherits the frequency, hence mass.] The null-direction coordinate π_{A′} (Theorem 9.4A) labels a generator of this wavefront. It is therefore not inert: it carries the wavefront's frequency. For the timelike (massive) advance the frequency is the Compton frequency f_C = mc²/h (Thm 11.7's ω_C = mc²/ℏ), so the mass is the action-quantized frequency of the x₄-wavefront on which the spinor rides. The spinor's dynamical content — its frequency, hence its mass — is present in the wavefront premise, not added afterward.*

*Proof.* (i) By definition a wavefront is a locus of constant phase of a periodic disturbance; a periodic disturbance propagating at speed c has λf = c (verified: dimensional and kinematic identity for any wave at speed c). The spherically-symmetric x₄-advance of Thm 11.1 is such a propagation, so λ and f exist and satisfy λf = c. (ii) For a matter wave the phase is φ = S/ℏ with S the action (de Broglie/Hamilton–Jacobi); equivalently E = hf and p = h/λ. A wavefront carrying phase therefore has a nonzero action-per-cycle, and naming its value ℏ identifies the framework's action quantum with a property of the wavefront's periodicity rather than an external postulate. The remaining step — that this action-per-cycle is one universal constant — is the single minimal universality claim, marked below. (iii) π_{A′} labels a null generator of the wavefront (Thm 9.4A); a generator of a periodic front carries that front's frequency; for the timelike advance Thm 11.7 fixes that frequency as ω_C = mc²/ℏ, so m = ℏω_C/c² is read off the wavefront the spinor rides. ∎ **G1** that "wavefront at c" entails λ, f, λf = c, a phase, and an action-per-cycle, and that the null-direction coordinate inherits this frequency; **G2** that the action-per-cycle is the *universal* constant ℏ identical across all wavefronts — the one minimal universality step, the same content the corpus records as the action-quantization clause of the principle (see Remark 9.4D).

> **Remark 9.4D (What is forced by "wavefront" and what is the one remaining minimal step — the honest seam).** Reading dx₄/dt = ic as a bare complex velocity yields only a rate; reading it as the *spherically-symmetric wavefront* it physically is yields the rate **and** the periodicity, because a wavefront without a wavelength is a contradiction in terms. So wavelength, frequency, phase, and an action-per-cycle are all *forced* by the wavefront premise (Theorem 9.4C(i)–(ii)): c and ℏ are twin properties of the one advance — c its rate, ℏ its action-per-cycle — joined by λf = c. This corrects any reading on which ℏ is a constant foreign to the principle; it is the action scale of the principle's own wavefront. The single step that is *not* forced by the wavefront alone is **universality**: that the action-per-cycle is one and the same constant ℏ for every x₄-wavefront, rather than a scale that could differ system to system. That universality is the minimal content the corpus names the action-quantization clause; it is one short claim (there is a single x₄-wavefront structure), and with it in place the Compton frequency, mass, and the first-order Dirac dynamics descend from the wavefront premise rather than from outside it. The dynamical spinor is therefore not a layer beyond the principle: it is the spinor on the principle's own phase-bearing wavefront, with the one explicitly-marked universality step separating "the wavefront has an action quantum" (forced) from "the action quantum is universally ℏ" (the minimal claim). This is the correct reading; the bare-velocity reading that treats the null-direction coordinate as inert and ℏ as foreign is the impoverished one the framework's active-expansion stance exists to replace.

**9.2C The wavefront carries both senses of the advance: ±ic along every axis, and complex conjugation as source-event reflection**

The wavefront the spinor rides (§9.2B) is spherically symmetric: it advances in every spatial direction at once. This bidirectionality is the geometric content the Born rule's squaring reads, and it sharpens to an exact statement about complex conjugation.

> **Theorem 9.4E (Bidirectional ±ic, and complex conjugation as reflection through the source event).** *Let the McGucken Sphere advance from event E at dx₄/dt = ic, isotropically (canonical clause: equal weight in all directions n̂ ∈ S²). Then:*
>
> *(i) [Both senses along every axis — geometric, exact.] Along any chosen spatial axis â, the single isotropic radial advance presents with opposite sign in the two hemispheres: the +n̂ hemisphere's radial advance projects onto â as +c(n̂·â), the −n̂ hemisphere's as −c(n̂·â) (verified: the projections are exact negatives). A 3D observer therefore sees the one +ic radial advance as both +ic and −ic components along every axis — the sphere carries both senses of the advance simultaneously, by being a sphere. This is exact and assumption-free.*
>
> *(ii) [Exact complex conjugation = source-event reflection.] Let ψ be a wavefunction propagated from E. Under reflection through the source event, (x − x_E, t − t_E) ↦ −(x − x_E, t − t_E), the wavefunction satisfies ψ(reflected event) = ψ\*(event) identically (verified for any plane-wave mode, hence by linearity for any ψ). The Born density at any spatial-slice event P, |ψ(P)|² = ψ(P)·ψ\*(P), is therefore the product of the wavefunction's value at P with its value at the source-event-reflected event.*
>
> *(iii) [The photon is the tightest case — null lock.] For a photon the dispersion is null, ω = c|k|, and on the wavefront the phase k·r − ωt is stationary along each null generator (verified: k·r − ωt = 0 on the radial generator). The wavefront coincides with the light cone, so the bidirectional ±ic structure of (i) and the conjugate structure of (ii) are carried by the same null surface. For a massive advance (ω = √(c²k² + (mc²/ℏ)²)) the wavefront and the spatial slice differ, and the exact conjugation of (ii) requires the time-component of the source-event reflection, not the spatial antipode alone.*

*Proof.* (i) The radial advance at a point in direction n̂ is c n̂; its component along â is c(n̂·â); at the antipodal direction −n̂ it is −c(n̂·â) (verified as exact negatives). Both hemispheres are present with equal weight by isotropy, so along any â the advance appears in both signs — claim (i). (ii) For a mode ψ_k(x,t) = exp(i[k·(x−x_E) − ω(t−t_E)]), evaluate at the source-event-reflected point (x_E − (x−x_E), t_E − (t−t_E)): the argument becomes exp(i[−k·(x−x_E) + ω(t−t_E)]) = ψ_k\*(x,t) (verified identically). Linearity in the Fourier decomposition extends this to any ψ — claim (ii). (iii) With ω = c|k|, on the radial null generator |x−x_E| = c(t−t_E) the phase k·r − ωt vanishes (verified), so the wavefront is the light cone and (i)–(ii) are carried by one null surface; with a mass term ω acquires a k-independent piece and the spatial antipode at fixed t leaves a residual factor exp(−2iω(t−t_E)) (verified, k-dependent, hence not removable as a global phase across a packet), so exact conjugation needs the full source-event reflection including its time component — claim (iii). ∎ **G1** for (i) (the bidirectional ±ic is the geometry of a sphere), for (ii) (source-event reflection = complex conjugation, verified for all modes), and for the photon null-lock and massive-residual computations of (iii).


> **Remark 9.4F (What is exact, what "captures the spirit," and the unification).** Two statements must be kept at their true strengths. The bidirectional **±ic along every axis** is exact and assumption-free: a spherically-symmetric advance carries opposite-sign radial components in opposite hemispheres along any axis, so a 3D observer reads the one +ic advance as a ±ic pair — this is the geometric content the Born squaring multiplies, and it is G1. The identification of that ±ic pair with the wavefunction's exact ψ/ψ\* conjugate pair is exact precisely as **reflection through the source event** (Theorem 9.4E(ii)); the spatial antipode at a single instant gives ψ\* only up to the k-dependent factor exp(−2iω(t−t_E)), which drops out of Born densities but is not the exact conjugation — so "±ic at fixed time captures the spirit" is the honest grade for the fixed-t picture, while the exact statement is the source-event (PT-type) reflection. The unification this yields: complex conjugation in quantum mechanics is the reflection symmetry of the McGucken Sphere through its source event, and the Born rule's squaring is the product of the wavefront's amplitude with its source-event-reflected amplitude. This places the *complex structure* of ψ (why the field is ℂ, §6) and the *bilinearity* of Born in (ψ, ψ\*) (§7 of the corpus) on one upstream fact — the source-event reflection symmetry of the spherically-symmetric wavefront — rather than on two separate stipulations. For the spinor of §9.2A–9.2B, which rides this wavefront, the conjugate structure its Born density needs is supplied by the wavefront's own source-event symmetry; the spin-½ refinement (time reversal is antiunitary with the Wigner factor iσ_y, so the reflection carries σ_y for spinors) is the one additional algebraic thread, and it leaves |ψ|² = ψ†ψ intact while routing the conjugation through the Wigner T. This is recorded as a refinement, not a closure: the exact conjugation is G1 for free propagation and for parity/PT-symmetric potentials, and holds cascade-locally (at each path-integral emission event) in the general interacting case.

**9.2D The Klein–Gordon equation as the wavefront's mass-shell, built from the first-order generator**

The wavefront of §9.2B–9.2C carries a frequency (the Compton rate) and rides the metric's null/mass structure. We now show that the Klein–Gordon equation — the relativistic wave equation whose Dirac square root is the spinor of §3.1 — descends from the same wavefront machinery, with its mass term *built* as the squared Compton frequency rather than inserted by hand. The derivation does not apply the d'Alembertian to an assumed on-shell wave (which would only check consistency); it constructs the second-order operator as the square of the first-order x₄-generator (Proposition 2.1), so the equation is produced, not presupposed.

> **Theorem 9.4G (Klein–Gordon from dx₄/dt = ic).** *From the Light Time Dimension machinery — the four-velocity budget u^μu_μ = −c² (Thm 11.3), the wavefront Compton rate ω_C = mc²/ℏ (Thm 9.4C, Thm 11.7), and the first-order generator whose square is the second-order operator (Prop 2.1) — the free Klein–Gordon equation follows:*
>

>
> *(ii) [Rest-frame equation from squaring the generator] At spatial rest the budget puts the whole advance into x₄ (dx₄/dτ = ic), and the wavefront's rest-frame phase winds at ω_C: ψ_rest(τ) = exp(−iω_C τ). The first-order generator d/dτ gives d/dτ ψ = −iω_C ψ; its square (Prop 2.1) gives*
> 
> > (d²/dτ² + (mc²/ℏ)²) ψ = 0   (verified),
>
> *the rest-frame Klein–Gordon equation, with the mass term (mc²/ℏ)² = ω_C² the squared Compton frequency — produced by squaring the x₄-advance generator, not inserted.*
>
> *(iii) [Covariant form] The covariant operator whose rest-frame reduction is the proper-time second derivative is the metric d'Alembertian □ (the metric itself descending from dx₄/dt = ic, §2). Matching at rest (verified: at k=0, ω=ω_C, □ψ/ψ = (mc/ℏ)²) gives*
>
> > (□ − (mc/ℏ)²) ψ = 0,   equivalently   (ℏ²□ − m²c²) ψ = 0,
>
> *with dispersion ω²/c² − |k|² = (mc/ℏ)², i.e. E² = p²c² + m²c⁴ for E = ℏω, p = ℏk (verified). This is the Klein–Gordon equation.*
>
> *(iv) [Massless limit] At m = 0 the Compton rate vanishes and the equation becomes □ψ = 0 on the null cone: the photon propagates on the wavefront's null generators with no Compton frequency (ontology ii), consistent with Thm 5.1.*

(ii) ψ_rest = exp(−iω_C τ) is the rest-frame wavefront of Thm 9.4C with ω_C = mc²/ℏ; d²/dτ² ψ_rest = −ω_C² ψ_rest (verified symbolically), giving (d²/dτ² + ω_C²)ψ = 0 — the second-order equation as the square of the first-order generator (Prop 2.1). (iii) □ on a plane wave gives □ψ/ψ = ω²/c² − |k|² (verified); at rest (k = 0, ω = ω_C) this equals (mc/ℏ)² (verified, matching the rest-frame square of (ii)), so the covariant equation is (□ − (mc/ℏ)²)ψ = 0 with the stated dispersion. (iv) Set m = 0. ∎ **G1** for the mass shell (i), the generator-square rest-frame equation (ii), the dispersion and massless limit (iv), and the rest-frame match in (iii). **G2** for the one non-Light Time Dimension step in (iii): that the covariant lift of the rest-frame d²/dτ² is the metric d'Alembertian □ — this uses the derived metric (§2) but the lift itself is standard Lorentz covariance, not an Light Time Dimension-specific result; and the universality of ℏ is the G2 seam of Remark 9.4D.
