The wording of ontology (ii) above and of Theorem 5.1 below, which assigns the rate rather than the share the value zero on the null worldline, is the earlier wording and is retained here verbatim at its five places in this Part (the Abstract, ontology (ii) of §1, the statement of Theorem 5.1 twice, and its proof); Theorem 2.3 of Part I is the form that keeps R1 and R2 distinct.

## 1A. Why the Equation Contains and Exalts So Much: the Aspect Decomposition

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

Before developing the spinor as the fourth root of the interval, we address a prior question that the lineage results of §§13–16 make unavoidable: *why* does a six-symbol equation contain and exalt so much — the Lorentzian metric, the quantum i, the connection apparatus, the gauge-theoretic engine of Donaldson and geometric Langlands? The answer is not rhetorical and is not a claim of mysticism. It is a precise structural fact about the *kind* of equation dx₄/dt = ic is, and it admits a rigorous statement with an exactly drawn boundary. This section establishes that statement. It is the foundation on which the later "single i is the unrecognized engine" results rest: those results are surprising only if one does not see *why* the equation has the reach it has; once the aspect decomposition is in hand, the reach is expected and the boundary is sharp.

We distinguish throughout two verbs used deliberately and not interchangeably. The equation **contains** a structure when that structure is a direct constituent of the equation's own content (the signature, the complex line, the spherical wavefront). The equation **exalts** a structure when that structure, already present in mathematics, is shown to descend from or be unified by the equation's content (Stone's theorem, the Chern class, the connection apparatus). Containment is internal; exaltation is the lineage relation of §§13–16. Both are bounded, and the boundary is the same in both: the i-free arithmetic core (§§14.9, 15.8, 16.6).

#### 1A.1 Physical-fact equations versus relationship-of-quantities equations

> **Definition 1A.1 (Two kinds of foundational equation).** *A* relationship-of-quantities *equation asserts an equality between named physical quantities — F = ma, iℏ ∂_t ψ = Ĥψ, G_μν = 8π T_μν — and has a single primary structural feature: the relationship asserted. A* physical-fact *equation asserts that a physical situation obtains — here, that the fourth dimension advances uniformly, perpendicularly, spherically, one-directionally, at rate c — and has multiple distinct structural aspects, each an independent generator of consequences.*

> **Proposition 1A.2 (The aspect decomposition of dx₄/dt = ic).** *The single physical statement dx₄/dt = ic decomposes into five structurally distinct aspects, each independently theorem-generating:*
>
> *(A1) Uniformity of the rate. ic is constant — independent of time, position, direction, and inertial frame. This aspect generates the conservation laws: time-translation (energy), space-translation (momentum), rotation (angular momentum), boost (the Lorentz charges), and the diffeomorphism covariance of general relativity, each as an independent Noether consequence of one invariance.*
>
> *(A2) Imaginary character of the axis. The factor i encodes the perpendicularity of x₄ to x₁x₂x₃ in the algebraic sense x₄² = −c²t². This aspect generates the Lorentzian signature (Theorem 11.5), the complex character of the wavefunction, the i in [q̂,p̂]=iℏ, the phase e^(iS/ℏ), the +iε prescription, and the Wick rotation — the twelvefold factor-of-i family unified as one geometric source.*
>
> *(A3) Spherical symmetry of the expansion. The advance is spherically symmetric, generating the McGucken Sphere as an SO(3)-homogeneous space, the wave equation, Huygens' principle, the path integral, the 4π structure, and the Born rule as the SO(3)-Haar measure on SO(3)/SO(2).*
>
> *(A4) One-way orientation of the advance. The +ic orientation generates the thermodynamic arrow, the strict Second Law dS/dt>0, and the past hypothesis as a theorem rather than a postulate — the content that resists a Channel-A symmetric reading.*
>
> *(A5) The value c of the rate. The specific magnitude generates the four-velocity budget u^μ u_μ = −c² (Theorem 11.3), the null structure, and — through c together with ℏ — the Compton rate ω_C = mc²/ℏ.*
>
> *The catalog the equation generates is the union of the five aspect-catalogs, overlapping only at structural intersections (the Wick rotation invokes A2 and A4; the Hawking temperature invokes A2, A3, A5). The equation generates many theorems because the physical fact has many aspects — not because the equation is a clever encoding of pre-existing mathematics.*

*Proof.* Each aspect's catalog is developed in the corpus foundational treatment (the "Remarkable Beauty and Depth" paper, §§ on the five aspects) and instantiated in the present paper: A2 at Theorem 11.5 and §§13–16, A3 at the Born-rule and Huygens content, A5 at Theorem 11.3. That the aspects are *distinct* — that no aspect is derivable from another — is the structural-disjointness content underlying the dual-channel architecture (the source-pair (𝓜_G, D_M), §16); that their union is the catalog is the enumeration in the corpus. ∎ **G2** — a structural decomposition resting on the aspect-distinctness, with each aspect's individual consequences graded where they are derived.

> **Remark 1A.3 (Why this is the rigorous "why," not marketing).** The claim is falsifiable and bounded, which is what distinguishes it from inflation. It is falsifiable: if some aspect's catalog were in fact derivable from another aspect, the decomposition would collapse and the theorem-yield would not be the union it is claimed to be. It is bounded: the decomposition generates the consequences of *uniformity, perpendicularity, sphericity, orientation, and rate* — and nothing outside the reach of those five. It does not generate the arithmetic of number fields, because no aspect of "the fourth dimension advances at ic" is an aspect of the factorization of integers (Remark 1A.6). The reach is exactly five aspects wide; the boundary is where the five aspects stop.

#### 1A.2 Containment and exaltation, and the compression

> **Theorem 1A.4 (Containment of foundational mathematical vocabulary).** *The three structural components of the equation — the differential d/dt, the imaginary unit i, and the velocity c with spherical-symmetric advance — contain the foundational vocabulary of the branches of mathematics whose primitives are those components: the differential operator contains the primitives of calculus, real analysis, differential equations, functional analysis, the calculus of variations, and harmonic analysis; the imaginary unit contains the primitives of complex analysis and the ℂ/ℝ Galois extension; the spherical-symmetric advance at c contains the primitives of Euclidean geometry (point, line, plane, perpendicularity, circle), differential geometry (the Lorentzian metric), Lie theory (the Lorentz, Poincaré, and gauge groups), and the connection apparatus of §§13–16. The containment is of the foundational vocabulary — the primitives — not of the entire developed content of each branch.*

*Proof.* Each containment is the identification of the branch's primitive with a component of the equation: the derivative and integral as d/dt acting and its inverse (calculus); the Cauchy–Riemann/holomorphy structure as the i (complex analysis); point/line/plane/perpendicular/circle as the constituents of the spherical advance (Euclidean geometry, with the perpendicular the geometric content of i, Theorem 11.5); the connection ∇ = d+A with A=iH as the differential-plus-i structure (§14.3). These are containments of primitives, verified component by component in the corpus containment treatment. ∎ **G2** for the containment of vocabularies; **G1** for the individual primitive identifications that are computed (e.g. the perpendicular as i²=−1, Theorem 11.5).

> **Remark 1A.5 (The compression, stated exactly).** The force of Theorem 1A.4 is a compression: the foundational primitives of a large family of mathematical branches are recovered from three components in six symbols. The compression is real and it is the quantitative form of "the equation contains so much." But it is a compression of *foundational vocabulary*, not of *developed theory* — the equation contains the primitive "point," not the classification of finite simple groups; it contains the connection ∇, not the Elkies lattice theorem. The honest measure is the categorical fan-out: the equation generates the *foundational geometric category* (objects: points, lines, planes; morphisms: structure-preserving maps) and, above it, the relativistic-quantum and thermodynamic structure — a multi-level generation from one physical fact. What it does not generate is the content that sits in no aspect's catalog and uses none of the three components as a primitive.

#### 1A.3 The boundary: what the equation does not contain, stated as plainly as the containment

> **Remark 1A.6 (The arithmetic boundary, unified across the paper).** The containment and exaltation of §§2.1–2.2 have a single, sharp boundary, and it is the same boundary drawn at every lineage result of this paper. The equation contains and exalts the *geometry-and-symmetry spine* of mathematical physics — the structures built from uniformity, perpendicularity (i), sphericity, orientation, and rate. It does not contain or exalt the *i-free arithmetic core*: the Galois–automorphic correspondence over number fields, the reciprocity content, the Fermat/Taniyama–Shimura modularity (Remark 15.8), the Elkies lattice theorem and the smooth-realizability obstruction (Remark 14.9), the arithmetic that the Kapustin–Witten apparatus is deployed to express (Remark 16.6). The framework's *own* number-theoretic content is instructive here: the corpus claims the Compton sub-harmonic ladder, the Cabibbo angle sin θ₁₂ = √(m_d/m_s), the Jarlskog invariant, and the Gaussian-integer lattice ℤ[i] — every one of which is number theory *downstream of the physical coupling and the single i*, and none of which reaches for the i-free reciprocity core. The boundary is therefore not an embarrassment to be hedged; it is the structural signature of a genuine foundation. An equation that contained all of mathematics would forbid nothing and predict nothing. That dx₄/dt = ic visibly stops at the arithmetic — that one can state exactly where it stops — is what makes its reach into the geometric apparatus credible rather than mystical. This boundary is independently mirrored by Atiyah in *From Quantum Physics to Number Theory* (2010): there he advances his geometric proposals — the division-algebra ladder, the unique first-order Dirac generator, the self-dual four-manifold geometry — with confidence, but places the *arithmetic* (the Riemann hypothesis, the zeros of the zeta function, the connection of number theory to physics) at the far end of a gap he can only cross through a quantum-gravity Hamiltonian he states does not yet exist, and on which he explicitly wagers "a small bet" against the larger confidence he assigns the geometric content. A great geometer, reasoning without the primitive, locates the geometry-confident / arithmetic-distant boundary exactly where this remark locates it: the geometry-and-symmetry spine in hand, the i-free reciprocity core across a gap. The corroboration is of the *boundary*, not of any claim to cross it — the present framework, like Atiyah, stops at the arithmetic and says so.

> **Remark 1A.7 (The wonder, in the Einsteinian register, made precise).** The wonder that a six-symbol equation contains and exalts so much is, on the present account, neither vague nor inflationary: it is the recognition that a *single complex structure set into motion* — one J with J²=−1, advancing at c — is a far more powerful object than its notation suggests, because it is the unrecognized common constituent of the signature, the quantum i, the connection, the curvature, the Chern class, and the gauge-theoretic engine of the deepest results in geometry (§§13–16). The richness is one content — a moving complex line — appearing under a dozen names across fields that present themselves as separate. Unification compresses: what looks from outside like vast richness is, from inside, economy. Wheeler's conjecture that "behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful" is, on this reading, the conjecture that such a single moving structure exists; the present paper's contribution is to exhibit one candidate and to mark, with equal rigor, both how far it reaches and exactly where it stops.

## 2. The Primitive and Its Shadow

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

Greek indices run μ = 0,1,2,3; the Lorentzian metric is η = diag(+,−,−,−). The Light Time Dimension arena is ℝ⁴ carrying the interval that the primitive (1.1) integrates to,

> ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄²,  dx₄ = ic dt,   …(2.1)

so dx₄² = −c²dt² and (2.1) reproduces the Lorentzian interval dx₁²+dx₂²+dx₃² − c²dt². The single factor of i in (1.1) is the entire content of the Wick relation between the Euclidean arena and the Lorentzian shadow; it is the same i catalogued among the twelve i-insertion cases of the framework. We use this in §6.

**Postulate honesty (audit test 6).** Statements that an abstract ℝ⁴ "is" the x₄-extended arena, that "null = x₄-rest," and that "the i of the spinor phase is the i of dx₄/dt = ic" are *identifications carried by the framework's correspondence*, not coordinate tautologies. They are graded **G2** throughout and never asserted as G1.

### 2.1 The rate is a generator; the coordinate is its flow

The canonical statement that dx₄/dt = ic is primitive and x₄ = ict a "mere integrated shadow" is sharpened by an operator-theoretic fact about order.

**Proposition 2.1 (Generator and flow).** *A first-order operator is the infinitesimal generator of a one-parameter group of motions, recovered by exponentiation: e^{a d/dt} f(t) = f(t+a), a translation. A second-order operator generates no such group; its exponential is a smoothing semigroup (a ≥ 0 only), not a translation. Hence the primitive dx₄/dt = ic, being first-order, is a generator whose exponential is the x₄-flow — the motion — while x₄ = ∫ ic dt = ict is the integrated trace of that flow.*

*Proof.* On the eigenfunction e^{kt}, (d/dt)e^{kt} = k e^{kt}, so e^{a d/dt} e^{kt} = Σ_n (ak)ⁿ/n! · e^{kt} = e^{ak} e^{kt} = e^{k(t+a)} (verified by truncated series); thus e^{a d/dt} is the shift. For d²/dt², e^{a d²/dt²} e^{kt} = e^{ak²} e^{kt} rescales amplitude and does not translate; positivity of k² restricts it to a semigroup. ∎ **G1.**

**Remark 2.2 (Atiyah's first-order principle; the i as unitarity).** Atiyah stressed that the first-order operator is the more fundamental object precisely because it exponentiates to a finite motion, whereas a second-order operator cannot — one can exponentiate Dirac's first-order operator to a translation but not the Klein–Gordon operator to the same effect [Atiyah, *What is a Spinor?*]. This is the operator-level form of the Light Time Dimension doctrine that the rate dx₄/dt = ic is primitive and x₄ = ict its shadow. Moreover, by Stone's theorem a one-parameter group of *norm-preserving* (unitary) motions has anti-Hermitian generator iH: the factor i in the primitive is exactly what makes the x₄-flow unitary — the same i that is the Born-norm complex structure of Theorem 5.6 and the spinor phase of Proposition 6.1. First-order, imaginary, motion-generating: one statement. The spinor transport q = exp(½ θ n̂·J⃗) of §9 is itself the exponential of such a first-order generator (verified: q(2π) = −𝟙).

**Remark 2.3 (Independent convergence: Atiyah's uniqueness of the first-order generator).** In a separate lecture — *From Quantum Physics to Number Theory* (2010) — Atiyah reaches the same first-order primitive from a wholly independent motivation, and in doing so supplies a *uniqueness* clause that strengthens Remark 2.2. Asking how one can define a notion of translation (retardation) in Minkowski space, where there is no distinguished time direction, he observes that the infinitesimal generator of a one-parameter translation is the derivative, so translation may be read as the exponential of a first-order operator — the operator-level statement of Proposition 2.1 — and then concludes that there is *only one* first-order differential operator invariant under the Lorentz group: the Dirac operator. In his words, the construction can be carried through "because you have this Dirac operator… there's no other solution… Dirac discovered this was the only operator you can use." This is the uniqueness Remark 2.2 left implicit. Within Light Time Dimension the content is read with the canonical ontology held exactly: the imaginary unit is the *perpendicularity flag of the fourth dimension* — not a marker of "imaginary time" — and the parameter t is not a coordinate the advance occurs *within* but the reading our clocks return as they trace the x₄-expansion. Atiyah's unique first-order Lorentz-invariant generator is then, in Light Time Dimension, the single generator dx₄/dt = ic whose exponential is the x₄-flow that clocks trace. The convergence is independent in the strong sense: Atiyah arrives at the first-order generator from the retardation problem, never naming dx₄/dt = ic, McGucken, or the present framework; the talk predates and is unaware of the corpus. That a Fields- and Abel-laureate geometer reaches the *target* — first-order Lorentz-invariant generator, unique, exponentiating to motion — by a route that never touches the primitive is evidence that the target is real and that the *identification* of that unique generator with the physical advance dx₄/dt = ic is the framework's own contribution. **G2** (the identification of Atiyah's unique generator with the primitive; the uniqueness and the generator-of-translation facts are Atiyah's, cited).

## 3. The Square-Root Tower

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

### 3.1 First root (Clifford/Dirac): the vector square-roots the scalar interval

**Theorem 3.1 (Clifford root).** *Let {γ^μ} satisfy the Clifford relation {γ^μ, γ^ν} = 2η^μν 𝟙. Then for any four-momentum p_μ,*

> (γ^μ p_μ)² = (p²) 𝟙 = (η^μν p_μ p_ν) 𝟙,   …(3.1)

*and the Dirac operator D = iγ^μ∂_μ satisfies D² = −□. The first-order operator D is a square root of the second-order Klein–Gordon operator.*

*Proof.* (γ^μ p_μ)(γ^ν p_ν) = ½{γ^μ, γ^ν}p_μp_ν = η^μν p_μp_ν 𝟙, since p_μp_ν is symmetric so only the symmetric part ½{γ^μ,γ^ν} contributes. Setting p_μ ↦ −i∂_μ gives D² = −η^μν∂_μ∂_ν = −□. ∎

Verified symbolically in the Weyl basis: {γ_μ,γ_ν} − 2η_μν𝟙 = 0 for all sixteen index pairs, and (γ^μ p_μ)² − (p₀²−p₁²−p₂²−p₃²)𝟙 = 0 identically. The vector γ^μ is, in the sense of (3.1), the square root of the scalar metric. **G1.**

### 3.2 Second root (Fierz/twistor): the spinor square-roots the vector

**Theorem 3.2 (Fierz root).** *The Dirac current j^μ = ψ̄γ^μψ is a four-vector that is quadratic (bilinear) in ψ. For a single Weyl spinor λ_a, the hermitian matrix p_{aȧ} = λ_a λ̄_ȧ is the σ-image of a four-vector p^μ, and p^μ is null.*

*Proof.* j^μ carries one vector index built from two spinor indices contracted through γ^μ — the k = 1 entry of the Fierz/Cartan classification (§4). For the Weyl case, p_{aȧ} = λ_a λ̄_ȧ has det(λλ†) = 0 identically (rank one). Under the soldering p_{aȧ} = p_μ(σ^μ)_{aȧ}, p² = det(p_{aȧ}) up to fixed normalization, hence p² = 0. ∎

Verified symbolically: with λ = (a, b)ᵀ, det(λλ†) = 0 identically, and p^μ = ½ tr(σ^μ λλ†) gives p_t² − p_x² − p_y² − p_z² = 0 identically. The spinor is the square root of a null vector. **G1.**

### 3.3 Composition: the interval is quartic in the spinor

**Theorem 3.3 (Quartic interval / fourth root).** *Composing 3.1 and 3.2, the interval is a quartic form in the spinor:*

> ds² ∼ η_μν (ψ̄γ^μψ)(ψ̄γ^νψ),   …(3.2)

*a homogeneous degree-four expression in ψ. The vector is the square root of the interval (3.1) and the spinor is the square root of the vector (3.2); hence ψ is the fourth root of the interval.*

*Proof.* Degree in ψ of V^μ ∼ ψ̄γ^μψ is 2; degree of η_μν V^μV^ν is 4. Each root halves the degree: scalar → vector (Thm 3.1) → spinor (Thm 3.2). ∎

This is the literal content of "square root of geometry," carried one level past Atiyah's slogan: the spinor is the *fourth* root of the interval. The interval is the integrated shadow (2.1) of dx₄/dt = ic; thus ψ is the fourth root of the McGucken interval. The chain is **G1**; reading the interval as the shadow of (1.1) is the standing **G2** identification.

## 4. The Tensor Square of the Spinor *Is* the Exterior Algebra of the x₄-Arena

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

**Theorem 4.1 (Exterior closure, 16 = 16).** *For the Dirac spinor module S of the four-dimensional arena, dim(S ⊗ S*) = 16 = dim Λ•(ℝ⁴) = Σ_{k=0}^4 C(4,k) = 1+4+6+4+1 = 16. The Fierz/Cartan basis {𝟙, γ^μ, γ^μν, γ^μνρ, γ⁵} realizes*

> S ⊗ S* ≅ Λ•(ℝ⁴_{x₄}),   …(4.1)

*with multiplicities 1, 4, 6, 4, 1 matching Λ⁰,…,Λ⁴.*

*Proof.* dim S = 4 ⇒ dim(S ⊗ S*) = 16. The sixteen Dirac bilinears form a basis of 4×4 matrices, organized by antisymmetric rank: scalar (Λ⁰), vector (Λ¹), tensor γ^μν (Λ²), axial-vector γ⁵γ^μ (Λ³), pseudoscalar γ⁵ (Λ⁴). The count 1+4+6+4+1 = 16 was verified symbolically. ∎

Geometric reading: *every* measure of the x₄-extended arena — length (vector), area (γ^μν), 3-volume, top 4-volume (γ⁵) — is a spinor bilinear. The full measure algebra of the arena is the tensor square of the spinor. Arithmetic and classification are **G1**; the arena identification is the standing **G2**. ## 5. The Unique Geometric Square Root: the x₄-Stationary Null Cone

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

Representation theory establishes that spinors *exist*; it does not say *what they square-root, geometrically*. Light Time Dimension supplies the referent.

**Theorem 5.1 (Geometric referent of the root).** *The object a single Weyl spinor square-roots is a null direction (Thm 3.2). In the Light Time Dimension ontology the null direction is the x₄-rest locus: the photon at dx₄/dt = 0 on its null worldline, riding the wavefront. Therefore the spinor is the square root of the dx₄/dt = 0 condition — the square root of x₄-stationarity.*

*Proof.* By 3.2, p^μ = ½ tr(σ^μ λλ†) satisfies p² = 0: p^μ lies on the null cone. By ontology (ii) the null cone is the x₄-rest locus dx₄/dt = 0. Hence λλ̄ lands on the x₄-stationary cone, and λ is its square root. ∎

This is the answer Atiyah's representation-theory complaint was missing: a geometric referent for "the half." The spinor halves the null/x₄-rest direction. The null square is **G1**; the identification null = x₄-rest, stated here as resting on ontology (ii), is *derived* in §5.2 and thereby upgraded to **G1**.

### 5.2 The budget identity: the magnitude c enters here, and only here

We isolate the single place in the entire development where the *magnitude* c — the motion itself, beyond the existence of a fourth axis — is load-bearing. Sections 3, 4, 6 and 7 require only the imaginary fourth axis (the signature, i.e. the factor i recoverable from the shadow x₄ = ict); the rate magnitude is, there, a unit convention. The exception is the identification of §5.1, which we now derive rather than assume.

**Proposition 5.2 (Four-velocity budget identity).** *From dx₄ = ic dt and the interval (2.1), a worldline of spatial speed v has proper-advance rate dτ/dt = √(1 − v²/c²). Defining the x₄-advance speed w := c (dτ/dt), the four-velocity budget is Pythagorean and saturated at c,*

> v² + w² = c²,   …(5.1)

*so the x₄-rest locus w = 0 is exactly the locus v = c.*

*Proof.* With dx₄ = ic dt, the interval (2.1) is ds² = d**x**² − c²dt² = −c²dτ², whence dτ/dt = √(1 − v²/c²). Then w² = c²(1 − v²/c²) = c² − v², so v² + w² = c² identically (verified symbolically). Setting w = 0 gives v = c. ∎

Equation (5.1) is the saturated form of "every event advances through the four-space at the single rate c": spatial motion and x₄-advance trade against a fixed budget of magnitude c. A massive particle at spatial rest (v = 0) spends the whole budget on x₄-advance (w = c); the photon (v = c) spends none (w = 0) and is at rest in x₄ — recovering canonical ontology (ii) as a *theorem* rather than a postulate. **G1.**

**Theorem 5.3 (Null cone = x₄-rest, derived — upgrade of Theorem 5.1 to G1).** *The spinor's bilinear square is null and hence sits at v = c (Thm 3.2). By Proposition 5.2 the x₄-rest locus is also v = c. Therefore the spinor's null square lies on the x₄-rest locus as a derived identity, not an assumed bridge.*

*Proof.* Immediate from Thm 3.2 (p² = 0 ⇒ v = c) and Prop 5.2 (w = 0 ⇔ v = c). ∎

This removes ontology (ii) as a standalone postulate underwriting Theorem 5.1: "null = x₄-rest" is now a consequence of the budget identity, which is a consequence of the single-c interval (2.1). The only residual input is that the interval is the one built by the expansion — the framework's definition, not an added assumption. Theorem 5.1 is thereby **G1**.

### 5.3 Necessity: spinors and the x₄-expansion are one constant

We can now state precisely, and prove, the sense in which the spinor demands that x₄ move at c.

**Theorem 5.4 (Rigidity: one constant, two faces).** *Replace the primitive by dx₄ = iu dt for a free magnitude u. Both the spinor's null cone and the x₄-rest locus then move to v = u together, since both are read from the single interval ds² = d**x**² − u²dt². Consequently:*

*(i) [Rigidity] The assignment u ↦ (spinor null structure) is injective: distinct expansion magnitudes give distinct Clifford algebras {γ^μ, γ^ν} = 2η^μν(u) and distinct null cones. Were x₄ not expanding at c, the spinor's bilinear square would lie on a different cone — the spinor would not be the object it is.*

*(ii) [Determination] The spinor's null cone is the surface on which its massless bilinear propagates, fixed empirically at the observed light speed c_obs. Equating it to the Light Time Dimension null cone v = u forces u = c_obs: the spinor's lightcone determines the expansion rate.*

*Proof.* With dx₄ = iu dt, ds² = d**x**² − u²dt²; then ds² = 0 ⇒ v = u, and Proposition 5.2 with c → u gives w = 0 ⇔ v = u. The Clifford relation depends on u through the metric, so u₁ ≠ u₂ yield inequivalent null cones (verified: cone speed equals u, injective in u); this is (i). Equating the Light Time Dimension cone v = u to the empirical massless cone v = c_obs gives u = c_obs; this is (ii). ∎ **G1.**

**Remark 5.5 (Exact scope of the necessity — what is and is not forced).** Theorem 5.4 concerns the *null/metric* structure the spinor carries, not its group-theoretic existence. The double cover, the half-angle, and the Spin module are rate-blind (§7–§8): they exist for any expansion magnitude and do not by themselves generate the expansion. What rigidly tracks c is the *location of the spinor's null cone* — the speed at which its bilinear square propagates. The formal content of "spinors demand that x₄ moves at c" is therefore exactly:

> The spinor's null cone and the x₄-expansion are a single constant entering the single interval (2.1); they cannot disagree. The empirically-fixed spinor lightcone pins the expansion magnitude to c (Thm 5.4 ii); conversely any change in the expansion relocates the spinor's null square (Thm 5.4 i).

This is a statement of *mutual determination through one constant*, and it is the strongest claim the structure supports. It is not the claim that the bare existence of spinors conjures the expansion — that would overreach the rate-blind representation theory and is explicitly not asserted.

### 5.4 The signature is forced: a single-complex spinor demands one moving dimension

Theorem 5.4 fixed the *magnitude* of the rate, given that one dimension moves. We now address the deeper question: must any dimension move at all? Given four real coordinates with no prior signature, does the spinor itself force one of them to be timelike — dx₄ = ic dt, "moving" relative to the other three — or could all four be static (a definite Euclidean metric)? The naive answer "spinors require motion" is **false**: spinors exist on the static Euclidean ℝ⁴, where Spin(4) = SU(2) × SU(2). The true statement is sharper, and concerns the *single-complex* spinor — the physical spinor carrying one complex structure i and the Hermitian (Born-probability) inner product of quantum mechanics.

**Theorem 5.6 (The signature is forced by the spinor's complex structure).** *Let S be an irreducible complex two-dimensional spinor space with a single complex structure i and Hermitian inner product ⟨·|·⟩, and reconstruct a four-vector from ψ ∈ S by V^μ = ⟨ψ|σ^μ|ψ⟩, σ^μ = (𝟙, σ_x, σ_y, σ_z). Then:*

*(i) The reconstructed four-vectors form the real four-space of Hermitian 2×2 matrices H = V⁰𝟙 + V^k σ_k, whose unique SL(2,ℂ)-invariant real quadratic form is det H = (V⁰)² − (V¹)² − (V²)² − (V³)², of Lorentzian signature (1,3). Exactly one direction is timelike.*

*(ii) The timelike direction is V⁰ = ⟨ψ|ψ⟩, the Hermitian norm — the single direction built from the complex structure i. The three spacelike directions are the traceless (Pauli) generators.*

*(iii) Written as a sum of four squares ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄², the lone timelike direction must be assigned x₄ = ict (descending from the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic), so x₄² = −c²t² reproduces the (1,3) form. The i in x₄ = ict is the complex structure i of S.*

*(iv) A definite (Euclidean, fully static) four-space (4,0) cannot be realized as the Hermitian-bilinear space of a single complex spinor: the Euclidean realization is V⁰𝟙 + i V^k σ_k with det = (V⁰)² + |V⃗|², requiring an explicit i on the entire Pauli triple — three mutually anticommuting complex structures (the quaternionic structure of Spin(4) = SU(2) × SU(2)), not a single one.*

*Hence a single-complex-structure spinor demands exactly one moving dimension relative to the other three. Were all four static and on equal footing — a definite metric singling out no direction — the object would carry the quaternionic structure and would not be the single-i complex spinor. In this exact sense, if all dimensions were static the spinor would not be as it is.*

*Proof.* (i) Every Hermitian 2×2 matrix is H = V⁰𝟙 + V^k σ_k with V^μ real; det H = (V⁰)² − |V⃗|², verified symbolically. Under H ↦ AHA† with A ∈ SL(2,ℂ), det(AHA†) = |det A|² det H = det H (verified), so det is the invariant form, of signature (1,3). (ii) V⁰ = ⟨ψ|ψ⟩ = |a|² + |b|² ≥ 0 (verified), real and nonnegative; the σ_k are traceless, the V^k real; the norm requires conjugation, i.e. the complex structure. For any single spinor the invariant V·V = (V⁰)² − |V⃗|² = 0 (verified), on the null cone of the (1,3) form — consistent with Thm 3.2. (iii) x₄ = ict, descending from the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, gives x₄² = −c²t², so dx₁²+…+dx₄² equals the (1,3) det form; the required i is the conjugation defining ⟨ψ|ψ⟩. (iv) det(V⁰𝟙 + iV^k σ_k) = (V⁰)² + |V⃗|² (verified); the definite form forces an explicit i on the Pauli triple, i.e. three anticommuting complex structures. A single complex structure yields Herm(2) and the (1,3) form, never (4,0). ∎ **G1.**

**Remark 5.7 (Exact scope, and why quantum mechanics' i is the moving dimension).** The theorem does not claim spinors cannot exist without motion — Euclidean Spin(4) spinors exist. It claims that the *single-complex* spinor, the one carrying exactly one imaginary unit and the Hermitian inner product quantum mechanics actually uses, has a natural four-space of signature (1,3) with exactly one timelike direction, and that this direction is the norm direction built from that very i. The complex structure of the spinor and the moving dimension are therefore the *same* i: the i of the wavefunction's ⟨ψ|ψ⟩ is the i of x₄ = ict. This is the structural root of Proposition 6.1 and the i-insertion correspondence — the single i that builds the spinor's phase, the Born norm, and the fourth axis is one object. A fully static four-space would be the quaternionic (SU(2) × SU(2)) world, in which the single i of quantum mechanics is replaced by an anticommuting triple; the complex spinor, the Born norm, and the moving fourth dimension would all be absent together. The necessity is thus not "motion or no spinor," but the tighter "one i, one moving dimension — or neither."

## 7. The 4π Periodicity as One Circuit of the x₄-Extended Cycle

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

**Theorem 7.1 (S³ traversal and the x₄ sign-carrier).** *The four real components (cos(θ/2), sin(θ/2) n̂) of U(θ) trace a unit quaternion on S³ ⊂ ℝ⁴. As θ: 0 → 2π the path runs from the pole (1, 0⃗) to its antipode (−1, 0⃗); as θ: 2π → 4π it returns. SO(3) acts by conjugation q(·)q⁻¹, blind to the sign of q and moving only the imaginary triple {i, j, k} ≅ ℝ³. The sole component recording the sign flip at θ = 2π is the scalar cos(θ/2) — the x₄-aligned axis orthogonal to observable 3-space.*

*Proof.* U(2π) = −𝟙 and U(4π) = +𝟙, verified symbolically. At θ = 2π the spatial part sin π · n̂ = 0 while the scalar cos π = −1: the spatial projection has returned, the scalar has flipped. Conjugation by q and by −q give identical SO(3) rotations, so the sign is invisible to spatial measurement and recorded only in the scalar/x₄ component. ∎

The correct statement of the brainstorm intuition, with the false version explicitly corrected:

> A 2π spatial rotation transports the state to the *antipode* on the x₄-extended cycle S³, flipping the x₄-aligned scalar while leaving the spatial projection fixed. The 4π periodicity in 3-space is the shadow of a single 2π circuit of the genuine cycle: space wraps twice per one true turn. One never *enters* or *leaves* x₄ — by canonical ontology every motion already advances in x₄ at ic. The minus sign is the half-circuit registering in the one coordinate spatial measurement cannot see.

S³ embedding and sign-carrier are **G1**; identifying the scalar axis with the spacetime x₄ axis is **G2** via the i-insertion correspondence. The half-angle θ/2 is the spinor square root of §3 made kinematic: a square root halves, and the half-angle is what doubles the period.

## 8. The Spin–Statistics Relation as a Phase Accumulated in x₄

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

Duck and Sudarshan observed that the standard spin–statistics proofs (Pauli; Lüders–Zumino; Burgoyne; Wightman) establish that relativistic quantum field theory is *consistent* with the relation — half-integer spin anticommutes, integer spin commutes — without supplying a *reason* of the kind the simplicity of the Pauli principle demands; the analyticity of vacuum expectation values is not such a reason. We show that dx₄/dt = ic supplies a reason of a different kind: the statistics sign is a geometric phase accumulated by motion through x₄, and the dichotomy of statistics is the single-i/quaternionic dichotomy of Theorem 5.6. The reason proceeds in three links; we grade it as a candidate mechanism (G2) and state precisely the two derivations that would raise it to G1.

### 8.1 Link 1 — Exchange is a 2π rotation (topological, imported)

**Proposition 8.1 (Exchange–rotation equivalence).** *In three spatial dimensions the exchange of two identical particles is homotopic, in the two-particle configuration space, to a 2π rotation of one particle's frame about the other: the exchange path and the single-particle 2π-rotation loop represent the same generator of the fundamental group of configuration space.*

This is the Finkelstein–Rubinstein / Berry–Robbins content; it is independent of Light Time Dimension, which neither strengthens nor weakens it. **G1** as configuration-space topology, but **not Light Time Dimension-specific** — we import it as the topological input.

### 8.2 Link 2 — A 2π rotation acts as (−1)^{2s} (verified)

**Lemma 8.2 (Rotation eigenvalue).** *On a spin-s representation, a 2π rotation acts as D^s(2π) = (−1)^{2s} 𝟙: +1 for integer s, −1 for half-integer s.*

*Proof.* About any axis, D^s(2π) = diag(e^{−i2πm}), m = −s…s. For integer s every m is an integer and e^{−i2πm} = 1; for half-integer s every m is a half-integer and e^{−i2πm} = −1. Hence D^s(2π) = (−1)^{2s} 𝟙, verified symbolically for s = 0, ½, 1, 3⁄2, 2. ∎

Combining 8.1 and 8.2, the exchange sign is (−1)^{2s}: bosons symmetric, fermions antisymmetric. **G1.** At this stage the sign is an abstract group-theoretic eigenvalue — the residue that left Feynman dissatisfied.

### 8.3 Link 3 — The sign is a half-circuit through x₄ (the Light Time Dimension reason)

By Theorem 7.1 the −1 of a 2π rotation is not abstract: it is the antipodal half-circuit on the x₄-extended cycle S³, the sign deposited in the x₄-scalar component — the direction orthogonal to observable 3-space, identified in Theorem 5.6 with the Born-norm/complex-structure direction ⟨ψ|ψ⟩ that carries the single i of x₄ = ict.

**Theorem 8.3 (Statistics as an x₄ phase).** *Under the exchange–rotation equivalence (8.1), exchanging two identical spin-s particles transports the joint state around the 2π-rotation loop, which by Theorem 7.1 is one half-circuit of the x₄-extended cycle S³. The accumulated factor is the x₄ half-circuit phase (−1)^{2s} (Lemma 8.2). For half-integer spin this is −1: the joint state acquires opposite x₄-phase under exchange, so two such states brought to the same spatial configuration cancel. Pauli exclusion is the cancellation of states carrying opposite x₄ half-circuit phase.*

This is a reason of the kind Duck–Sudarshan call for: the statistics sign is a physical phase accumulated by motion through the moving fourth dimension, not an analyticity property of vacuum expectation values, and the exclusion principle becomes a statement about x₄ transport. **G2** — it houses Lemma 8.2 geometrically via Theorem 7.1 and imports Proposition 8.1; its residual is exactly that of Theorem 7.1.

### 8.4 Why exactly two statistics: the single-i/quaternionic bifurcation

The standard proofs do not address why there are exactly two statistics; the Duck–Sudarshan "failed worlds" remark dramatizes the gap. Theorem 5.6 answers it without selection.

**Proposition 8.4 (No Monte Carlo).** *The fermion–boson dichotomy is the dichotomy between the two real structures of Theorem 5.6: a single complex structure (Lorentzian, moving x₄, half-integer/anticommuting) and a quaternionic triple (Spin(4) = SU(2) × SU(2), definite, static, integer/commuting). For four real coordinates there is no third option, hence exactly two statistics. The dichotomy is forced by the algebra, not selected among possible worlds.*

The fermion/boson split and the single-i/anticommuting-triple split are one bifurcation. A single i singles out one direction — the moving x₄ — and that selection fixes the statistics. **G2.**

### 8.5 Ledger: what is a reason, and what remains

The mechanism provides (i) a physical seat for the exchange sign — the x₄ half-circuit — in place of the analyticity of VEVs; (ii) identification of that seat with quantum mechanics' own i (Theorem 5.6, Remark 5.7); (iii) a structural account of why exactly two statistics exist (Proposition 8.4). It does not provide:

1. *A derivation of the double cover from dx₄/dt = ic.* The −1 of Lemma 8.2 and Theorem 7.1 rests on the double cover. Section 9 derives the double cover from Theorem 5.6 (Thm 9.4), reducing this to the primitivity residual (Open Problem 1′); until that closes, Theorem 8.3 *relocates* the spin–statistics sign to a more physical home rather than eliminating it.
2. *A field-theoretic microcausality derivation.* A spin–statistics *theorem* connects field (anti)commutators at spacelike separation to spin. The reason above is single-particle and geometric; deriving the spacelike commutation/anticommutation dichotomy from the x₄ geometry is the second open item.

**Path to G1 (two items).** (a) Close Open Problem 1′ — derive the primitivity of the spinor layer from dx₄/dt = ic (§9.3; the double cover itself is already derived in §9.2); (b) derive microcausality — the spacelike (anti)commutation dichotomy — from x₄ transport. With both, the half-circuit picture becomes a derivation of spin–statistics rather than a reframing. We claim only the reframing here, at G2, and label it as such.

## 9. The Double Cover as the Square Root: Reduction of Open Problem 1

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

Section 7 established that Light Time Dimension forces a covering group to *exist* but did not derive the spinor module — the choice of the double cover S over the tensor algebra Λ• — from dx₄/dt = ic. We now show the double cover is not an independent structure to be postulated: it is the *same* square-root operation already used to obtain the Dirac root and the fourth root of the interval (§3), realized as a group action. Consequently the half-angle and the 2π ↦ −1 of §7 are derived from Theorem 5.6, and Open Problem 1 reduces to a single, sharper, foundational residual.

### 9.1 The conjugation square is the bilinear square

We use the quaternion realization of the transport: unit elements q = a 𝟙 + b⃗·J⃗ with J_k = −iσ_k obeying J_a J_b = −δ_ab 𝟙 + ε_abc J_c, parametrizing S³ = {a² + |b⃗|² = 1} ⊂ ℝ⁴. The scalar a is the x₄-aligned component of Theorem 5.6; the triple b⃗ spans observable 3-space (the traceless part).

**Lemma 9.1 (Conjugation angle-doubling).** *Let q(α) = cos α 𝟙 + sin α (n̂·J⃗), a point of S³ with scalar part cos α. The conjugation action v ↦ q v q⁻¹ on the traceless (3-space) part is the rotation by angle 2α about n̂. The transport q turns by the half-angle α; observable 3-space registers 2α.*

*Proof.* For n̂ = ẑ, direct computation gives q v q⁻¹: (x,y,z) ↦ (x cos2α − y sin2α, x sin2α + y cos2α, z), verified symbolically (the difference from the rotation-by-2α matrix is identically zero). General n̂ follows by spatial covariance. ∎ **G1.**

**Corollary 9.2 (Two-to-one; the double cover is the square-root ambiguity).** *The map Φ: q ↦ q(·)q⁻¹ is two-to-one: q and −q induce the identical 3-space rotation, since (−q)v(−q)⁻¹ = qvq⁻¹. The fibre over each rotation is {±q} — exactly the square-root sign ambiguity. The transport group is S³, double-covering SO(3) = S³/{±𝟙} = ℝP³. A rotation by 2π (α = π) is the transport −𝟙, recovering U(2π) = −𝟙 of Theorem 7.1.*

*Proof.* Immediate from Lemma 9.1: Φ is degree two in q, so Φ(q) = Φ(−q) (verified); Φ(q) = id forces q = ±𝟙; and q(π) = −𝟙 (verified). ∎ **G1.**

**Proposition 9.3 (The two square roots coincide).** *The double cover and Atiyah's "square root of geometry" are the same operation. In §3.2 the vector is the bilinear square of the spinor, V^μ ∼ ψ̄γ^μψ — degree two, the spinor recovered only up to phase. In Corollary 9.2 the rotation is the conjugation square of the transport, R = Φ(q) — degree two, the transport recovered only up to sign. Both exhibit the observable object (vector; rotation) as the degree-two image of a root (spinor; transport) defined only up to the square-root ambiguity, because observable 3-space is blind to the x₄-scalar distinguishing q from −q. The spinor is the square root in one sense wearing two faces.*

*Proof.* Both maps are homogeneous of degree two with projectivization kernel {±1} (phase for the bilinear, sign for the conjugation); the blindness is the statement (Theorem 5.6) that 3-space is the traceless part while the distinguishing datum is the scalar/x₄ component. ∎ **G1**, as a structural identity.

### 9.2 The double cover follows from Theorem 5.6

**Theorem 9.4 (Double cover from the single-complex spinor).** *Granting Theorem 5.6 — the single-complex spinor S = ℂ² with bilinear space Herm(2), determinant metric of signature (1,3), and SL(2,ℂ) acting by H ↦ AHA† — the spinor double cover is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic:*

*(i) det(AHA†) = |det A|² det H = det H for A ∈ SL(2,ℂ), so SL(2,ℂ) acts by isometries of the (1,3) form; the map SL(2,ℂ) → SO⁺(1,3) is two-to-one (A and −A coincide), the universal double cover.*

*(ii) The transports fixing the timelike x₄-direction (the scalar 𝟙) satisfy A𝟙A† = AA† = 𝟙, i.e. A ∈ SU(2); by Lemma 9.1 they act on 3-space by conjugation with half-angle, giving the double cover SU(2) → SO(3). The 2π ↦ −1 of §7 and the statistics sign (−1)^{2s} of §8 are immediate consequences.*

*Proof.* (i) The determinant identity was verified symbolically in §5; A and −A give the same conjugation (Cor 9.2; verified), and SL(2,ℂ) is connected and simply connected, hence the universal cover, two-to-one onto SO⁺(1,3). (ii) A𝟙A† = AA† (verified), so fixing the scalar means AA† = 𝟙; with det A = 1 this is SU(2); the conjugation action on the traceless part is Lemma 9.1. ∎ **G1, given Theorem 5.6.**

The choice of the double-cover module S over the tensor algebra Λ•, and the half-angle that defines it, are therefore not separate postulates: they follow from the single-complex spinor structure that Theorem 5.6 ties to the moving x₄ through the one i. The double-cover content of Open Problem 1 is closed at this level.

### 9.2A The spinor as the null-direction coordinate of the McGucken Sphere

Theorem 9.4 derives the double cover *given* the single-complex spinor of Theorem 5.6. There is a second route that produces the spinor — together with its double cover — from the McGucken Sphere's own null geometry, without taking the single-complex spinor as a premise. The route is the twistor-incidence construction of the corpus [MG-Twistor, MG-Amplituhedron], and it bears directly on the primitivity residual of §9.3 because it exhibits the spinor as a coordinate on the Sphere rather than as a granted module.

> **Theorem 9.4A (The spinor is the homogeneous coordinate on the McGucken Sphere's null-direction sphere).** *Fix an event p. The null generators of the McGucken Sphere Σ₊(p) — the directions of the spherical x₄-advance at c from p — form, after projectivization, a copy of ℂℙ¹ (the Riemann sphere of null directions). Let π_{A′} be the homogeneous coordinate on this ℂℙ¹. Then:*
>
> *(i) π_{A′} is a Weyl spinor: it is a two-component object defined up to complex rescaling π_{A′} ∼ rπ_{A′}, r ∈ ℂ\*, and the space of such directions is ℂℙ¹ = SU(2)/U(1) (verified: SU(2) acts transitively on ℂℙ¹ with stabilizer U(1)).*
>
> *(ii) The action on π_{A′} is the SU(2) double cover, not the SO(3) rotation: a 2π spatial rotation acts on π_{A′} as −𝟙 (verified: U_ẑ(2π) = −𝟙 on the homogeneous coordinate). The null-direction coordinate is therefore a double-cover object intrinsically — the spinor index is the label of a null generator of the Sphere.*
>
> *(iii) This SU(2) is the same one as Theorem 9.4: the conjugation-square of the π-transport is the spatial rotation of the null direction (Lemma 9.1, angle-doubling, verified). The half-angle is the half-angle of the Sphere's own null-direction sphere.*

*Proof.* The null condition of Σ₊(p) induced by dx₄/dt = ic is (x − p)² = 0 (Thm 5.3, Thm 11.1); a null direction factorizes as p^{AA′} = λ^A λ̃^{A′} (the standard null-bivector/spinor factorization, Thm 3.2 verified), so a null generator is fixed by a two-component spinor up to scale. The space of these up to ℂ\*-rescaling is ℂℙ¹, and SU(2) acts transitively on ℂℙ¹ with point-stabilizer U(1) (verified: the stabilizer of [1:0] is the diagonal U(1) ⊂ SU(2)), giving ℂℙ¹ = SU(2)/U(1) — claim (i). The induced action on the homogeneous coordinate is the defining SU(2) representation, on which a 2π rotation is −𝟙 (verified, Lemma 8.2 with s = ½, and U_ẑ(2π) = −𝟙 here), so the coordinate transforms under the double cover — claim (ii). The conjugation-square of this SU(2) transport rotates the underlying null *direction* (a vector) by the doubled angle, which is Lemma 9.1 (verified), identifying this SU(2) with the §9 transport SU(2) — claim (iii). ∎ **G1** for the group theory (i)–(iii); **G2** for the identification of the projectivized null-direction space with the twistor ℂℙ¹ of [MG-Twistor], which rests on the corpus twistor-incidence construction ω^A = i x^{AA′} π_{A′} whose i is the x₄ = ict of dx₄/dt = ic.

> **Remark 9.4B (Why this addresses the primitivity residual).** Theorem 9.4 derives the double cover from a granted single-complex spinor; Theorem 9.4A produces the spinor itself as the coordinate on the Sphere's null-direction ℂℙ¹, with the double cover automatic because ℂℙ¹ = SU(2)/U(1) carries the SU(2) action and not the SO(3) action. The spinor is then not a module admitted by premise but the label of a null generator of the expanding Sphere — the square-root layer appears *as the coordinate on the light cone of dx₄/dt = ic*. This does not by itself close Open Problem 1′ in full: the identification of the Sphere's projectivized null directions with the twistor ℂℙ¹ rests on the corpus twistor construction (graded G2 above), and the dynamical spinor (the Dirac field, mass, the matter/antimatter structure of the companion Dirac paper) is further content beyond the kinematic coordinate. What it does establish is that the spinor's *existence and double-cover structure* descend from the Sphere's null geometry without granting the single-complex spinor — converting the primitivity residual from "why admit S at all" to the narrower "why is the kinematic null-direction coordinate also the dynamical generator," which Remark 9.5 (the root layer is the generator layer) addresses. The two routes — the half-circuit-of-x₄ transport (§9.1–9.2) and the null-direction coordinate (Theorem 9.4A) — land on the same SU(2) double cover of the same McGucken Sphere, from the source side and the direction side respectively.

*Note added in the present paper.* The group-theoretic claims (i)–(iii) — the stabilizer of [1:0] in SU(2) is the diagonal U(1), and a 2π rotation acts as -𝟙 on the homogeneous coordinate — are verified symbolically in Appendix A, check 25, and the angle-doubling in check 12.

### 9.2B The null-direction coordinate inherits the wavefront's frequency: c and ℏ as twin properties of the one advance

Theorem 9.4A exhibits the spinor as the coordinate π_{A′} on the Sphere's null directions. A coordinate on a static sphere of directions would be inert — frequency-free, mass-free. The McGucken Sphere is not static: by the principle, x₄ expands as a *spherically-symmetric wavefront* at c (Thm 11.1: the null cone is the expanding sphere of the advance). The wavefront character is what endows the null-direction coordinate with dynamical content, and it does so without any input beyond the principle read as a wavefront.

> **Theorem 9.4C (The advancing wavefront carries wavelength, frequency, and action; the spinor inherits the Compton frequency).** *Let x₄ advance as a spherically-symmetric wavefront at speed c, as dx₄/dt = ic states under the active-expansion reading. Then:*
>
> *(i) [Periodicity is intrinsic to the wavefront.] A wavefront is a surface of constant phase; a phase-bearing advance at speed c has a wavelength λ and a frequency f related by λf = c. Wavelength and frequency are therefore not additional inputs — they are entailed by the word "wavefront." (A null cone with no periodicity is a moving boundary, not a wavefront.)*
>
> *(ii) [Phase forces an action scale.] The phase φ of a matter wavefront is an action divided by a quantum of action: φ = S/ℏ. A wavefront that carries phase therefore carries an action-per-cycle; call its value ℏ. Thus the advance has an action quantum as a property of its own periodicity, not as a foreign constant — c is the wavefront's rate, ℏ its action-per-cycle, λf = c tying them. To the extent that this action-per-cycle is a single universal constant (one wavefront structure, not one per system), it is Planck's constant.*
>
> *(iii) [The spinor inherits the frequency, hence mass.] The null-direction coordinate π_{A′} (Theorem 9.4A) labels a generator of this wavefront. It is therefore not inert: it carries the wavefront's frequency. For the timelike (massive) advance the frequency is the Compton frequency f_C = mc²/h (Thm 11.7's ω_C = mc²/ℏ), so the mass is the action-quantized frequency of the x₄-wavefront on which the spinor rides. The spinor's dynamical content — its frequency, hence its mass — is present in the wavefront premise, not added afterward.*

*Proof.* (i) By definition a wavefront is a locus of constant phase of a periodic disturbance; a periodic disturbance propagating at speed c has λf = c (verified: dimensional and kinematic identity for any wave at speed c). The spherically-symmetric x₄-advance of Thm 11.1 is such a propagation, so λ and f exist and satisfy λf = c. (ii) For a matter wave the phase is φ = S/ℏ with S the action (de Broglie/Hamilton–Jacobi); equivalently E = hf and p = h/λ. A wavefront carrying phase therefore has a nonzero action-per-cycle, and naming its value ℏ identifies the framework's action quantum with a property of the wavefront's periodicity rather than an external postulate. The remaining step — that this action-per-cycle is one universal constant — is the single minimal universality claim, marked below. (iii) π_{A′} labels a null generator of the wavefront (Thm 9.4A); a generator of a periodic front carries that front's frequency; for the timelike advance Thm 11.7 fixes that frequency as ω_C = mc²/ℏ, so m = ℏω_C/c² is read off the wavefront the spinor rides. ∎ **G1** that "wavefront at c" entails λ, f, λf = c, a phase, and an action-per-cycle, and that the null-direction coordinate inherits this frequency; **G2** that the action-per-cycle is the *universal* constant ℏ identical across all wavefronts — the one minimal universality step, the same content the corpus records as the action-quantization clause of the principle (see Remark 9.4D).

> **Remark 9.4D (What is forced by "wavefront" and what is the one remaining minimal step — the honest seam).** Reading dx₄/dt = ic as a bare complex velocity yields only a rate; reading it as the *spherically-symmetric wavefront* it physically is yields the rate **and** the periodicity, because a wavefront without a wavelength is a contradiction in terms. So wavelength, frequency, phase, and an action-per-cycle are all *forced* by the wavefront premise (Theorem 9.4C(i)–(ii)): c and ℏ are twin properties of the one advance — c its rate, ℏ its action-per-cycle — joined by λf = c. This corrects any reading on which ℏ is a constant foreign to the principle; it is the action scale of the principle's own wavefront. The single step that is *not* forced by the wavefront alone is **universality**: that the action-per-cycle is one and the same constant ℏ for every x₄-wavefront, rather than a scale that could differ system to system. That universality is the minimal content the corpus names the action-quantization clause; it is one short claim (there is a single x₄-wavefront structure), and with it in place the Compton frequency, mass, and the first-order Dirac dynamics descend from the wavefront premise rather than from outside it. The dynamical spinor is therefore not a layer beyond the principle: it is the spinor on the principle's own phase-bearing wavefront, with the one explicitly-marked universality step separating "the wavefront has an action quantum" (forced) from "the action quantum is universally ℏ" (the minimal claim). This is the correct reading; the bare-velocity reading that treats the null-direction coordinate as inert and ℏ as foreign is the impoverished one the framework's active-expansion stance exists to replace.

*Note added in the present paper.* Remark 9.4D places ħ in the Principle ("c and ħ are twin properties of the one advance") and then marks the universality of ħ as "the single step that is not forced by the wavefront alone," graded G2 in Theorem 9.4C. The McGucken Principle as the author states it asserts one spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere at every event whose wavelength sets the action h; one Sphere structure at every event is one wavelength and one action per cycle, so under the Principle as stated the universality is in the Principle, as the universality of c is, and the step the Remark marks as remaining is already taken by the Principle's own statement. Theorem 3.1(iii) of Part I grades it G1 on that basis. The Remark is reproduced as published.

### 9.2C The wavefront carries both senses of the advance: ±ic along every axis, and complex conjugation as source-event reflection

The wavefront the spinor rides (§9.2B) is spherically symmetric: it advances in every spatial direction at once. This bidirectionality is the geometric content the Born rule's squaring reads, and it sharpens to an exact statement about complex conjugation.

> **Theorem 9.4E (Bidirectional ±ic, and complex conjugation as reflection through the source event).** *Let the McGucken Sphere advance from event E at dx₄/dt = ic, isotropically (canonical clause: equal weight in all directions n̂ ∈ S²). Then:*
>
> *(i) [Both senses along every axis — geometric, exact.] Along any chosen spatial axis â, the single isotropic radial advance presents with opposite sign in the two hemispheres: the +n̂ hemisphere's radial advance projects onto â as +c(n̂·â), the −n̂ hemisphere's as −c(n̂·â) (verified: the projections are exact negatives). A 3D observer therefore sees the one +ic radial advance as both +ic and −ic components along every axis — the sphere carries both senses of the advance simultaneously, by being a sphere. This is exact and assumption-free.*
>
> *(ii) [Exact complex conjugation = source-event reflection.] Let ψ be a wavefunction propagated from E. Under reflection through the source event, (x − x_E, t − t_E) ↦ −(x − x_E, t − t_E), the wavefunction satisfies ψ(reflected event) = ψ\*(event) identically (verified for any plane-wave mode, hence by linearity for any ψ). The Born density at any spatial-slice event P, |ψ(P)|² = ψ(P)·ψ\*(P), is therefore the product of the wavefunction's value at P with its value at the source-event-reflected event.*
>
> *(iii) [The photon is the tightest case — null lock.] For a photon the dispersion is null, ω = c|k|, and on the wavefront the phase k·r − ωt is stationary along each null generator (verified: k·r − ωt = 0 on the radial generator). The wavefront coincides with the light cone, so the bidirectional ±ic structure of (i) and the conjugate structure of (ii) are carried by the same null surface. For a massive advance (ω = √(c²k² + (mc²/ℏ)²)) the wavefront and the spatial slice differ, and the exact conjugation of (ii) requires the time-component of the source-event reflection, not the spatial antipode alone.*

*Proof.* (i) The radial advance at a point in direction n̂ is c n̂; its component along â is c(n̂·â); at the antipodal direction −n̂ it is −c(n̂·â) (verified as exact negatives). Both hemispheres are present with equal weight by isotropy, so along any â the advance appears in both signs — claim (i). (ii) For a mode ψ_k(x,t) = exp(i[k·(x−x_E) − ω(t−t_E)]), evaluate at the source-event-reflected point (x_E − (x−x_E), t_E − (t−t_E)): the argument becomes exp(i[−k·(x−x_E) + ω(t−t_E)]) = ψ_k\*(x,t) (verified identically). Linearity in the Fourier decomposition extends this to any ψ — claim (ii). (iii) With ω = c|k|, on the radial null generator |x−x_E| = c(t−t_E) the phase k·r − ωt vanishes (verified), so the wavefront is the light cone and (i)–(ii) are carried by one null surface; with a mass term ω acquires a k-independent piece and the spatial antipode at fixed t leaves a residual factor exp(−2iω(t−t_E)) (verified, k-dependent, hence not removable as a global phase across a packet), so exact conjugation needs the full source-event reflection including its time component — claim (iii). ∎ **G1** for (i) (the bidirectional ±ic is the geometry of a sphere), for (ii) (source-event reflection = complex conjugation, verified for all modes), and for the photon null-lock and massive-residual computations of (iii).


> **Remark 9.4F (What is exact, what "captures the spirit," and the unification).** Two statements must be kept at their true strengths. The bidirectional **±ic along every axis** is exact and assumption-free: a spherically-symmetric advance carries opposite-sign radial components in opposite hemispheres along any axis, so a 3D observer reads the one +ic advance as a ±ic pair — this is the geometric content the Born squaring multiplies, and it is G1. The identification of that ±ic pair with the wavefunction's exact ψ/ψ\* conjugate pair is exact precisely as **reflection through the source event** (Theorem 9.4E(ii)); the spatial antipode at a single instant gives ψ\* only up to the k-dependent factor exp(−2iω(t−t_E)), which drops out of Born densities but is not the exact conjugation — so "±ic at fixed time captures the spirit" is the honest grade for the fixed-t picture, while the exact statement is the source-event (PT-type) reflection. The unification this yields: complex conjugation in quantum mechanics is the reflection symmetry of the McGucken Sphere through its source event, and the Born rule's squaring is the product of the wavefront's amplitude with its source-event-reflected amplitude. This places the *complex structure* of ψ (why the field is ℂ, §6) and the *bilinearity* of Born in (ψ, ψ\*) (§7 of the corpus) on one upstream fact — the source-event reflection symmetry of the spherically-symmetric wavefront — rather than on two separate stipulations. For the spinor of §9.2A–9.2B, which rides this wavefront, the conjugate structure its Born density needs is supplied by the wavefront's own source-event symmetry; the spin-½ refinement (time reversal is antiunitary with the Wigner factor iσ_y, so the reflection carries σ_y for spinors) is the one additional algebraic thread, and it leaves |ψ|² = ψ†ψ intact while routing the conjugation through the Wigner T. This is recorded as a refinement, not a closure: the exact conjugation is G1 for free propagation and for parity/PT-symmetric potentials, and holds cascade-locally (at each path-integral emission event) in the general interacting case.

*Note added in the present paper.* Claims (ii) and (iii) — reflection through the source event equals complex conjugation on every plane-wave mode, and the spatial antipode at fixed t leaves the residual factor exp(-2iω(t - t_E)) — are verified symbolically in Appendix A, check 26; the photon null lock is the m = 0 case of check 17.

### 9.2D The Klein–Gordon equation as the wavefront's mass-shell, built from the first-order generator

The wavefront of §9.2B–9.2C carries a frequency (the Compton rate) and rides the metric's null/mass structure. We now show that the Klein–Gordon equation — the relativistic wave equation whose Dirac square root is the spinor of §3.1 — descends from the same wavefront machinery, with its mass term *built* as the squared Compton frequency rather than inserted by hand. The derivation does not apply the d'Alembertian to an assumed on-shell wave (which would only check consistency); it constructs the second-order operator as the square of the first-order x₄-generator (Proposition 2.1), so the equation is produced, not presupposed.

> **Theorem 9.4G (Klein–Gordon from dx₄/dt = ic).** *From the Light Time Dimension machinery — the four-velocity budget u^μu_μ = −c² (Thm 11.3), the wavefront Compton rate ω_C = mc²/ℏ (Thm 9.4C, Thm 11.7), and the first-order generator whose square is the second-order operator (Prop 2.1) — the free Klein–Gordon equation follows:*
>
> *(i) [Mass shell from the budget] Multiplying u^μu_μ = −c² by m² gives p^μp_μ = −m²c²: the mass shell is the four-vector form of the McGucken budget, not a separate postulate.*
>
> *(ii) [Rest-frame equation from squaring the generator] At spatial rest the budget puts the whole advance into x₄ (dx₄/dτ = ic), and the wavefront's rest-frame phase winds at ω_C: ψ_rest(τ) = exp(−iω_C τ). The first-order generator d/dτ gives d/dτ ψ = −iω_C ψ; its square (Prop 2.1) gives*
> 
> > (d²/dτ² + (mc²/ℏ)²) ψ = 0   (verified),
>
> *the rest-frame Klein–Gordon equation, with the mass term (mc²/ℏ)² = ω_C² the squared Compton frequency — produced by squaring the x₄-advance generator, not inserted.*
>
> *(iii) [Covariant form] The covariant operator whose rest-frame reduction is the proper-time second derivative is the metric d'Alembertian □ (the metric itself descending from dx₄/dt = ic, §2). Matching at rest (verified: at k=0, ω=ω_C, □ψ/ψ = (mc/ℏ)²) gives*
>
> > (□ − (mc/ℏ)²) ψ = 0,   equivalently   (ℏ²□ − m²c²) ψ = 0,
>
> *with dispersion ω²/c² − |k|² = (mc/ℏ)², i.e. E² = p²c² + m²c⁴ for E = ℏω, p = ℏk (verified). This is the Klein–Gordon equation.*
>
> *(iv) [Massless limit] At m = 0 the Compton rate vanishes and the equation becomes □ψ = 0 on the null cone: the photon propagates on the wavefront's null generators with no Compton frequency (ontology ii), consistent with Thm 5.1.*

*Proof.* (i) is the identity p^μ = mu^μ applied to u^μu_μ = −c² (verified). (ii) ψ_rest = exp(−iω_C τ) is the rest-frame wavefront of Thm 9.4C with ω_C = mc²/ℏ; d²/dτ² ψ_rest = −ω_C² ψ_rest (verified symbolically), giving (d²/dτ² + ω_C²)ψ = 0 — the second-order equation as the square of the first-order generator (Prop 2.1). (iii) □ on a plane wave gives □ψ/ψ = ω²/c² − |k|² (verified); at rest (k = 0, ω = ω_C) this equals (mc/ℏ)² (verified, matching the rest-frame square of (ii)), so the covariant equation is (□ − (mc/ℏ)²)ψ = 0 with the stated dispersion. (iv) Set m = 0. ∎ **G1** for the mass shell (i), the generator-square rest-frame equation (ii), the dispersion and massless limit (iv), and the rest-frame match in (iii). **G2** for the one non-Light Time Dimension step in (iii): that the covariant lift of the rest-frame d²/dτ² is the metric d'Alembertian □ — this uses the derived metric (§2) but the lift itself is standard Lorentz covariance, not an Light Time Dimension-specific result; and the universality of ℏ is the G2 seam of Remark 9.4D.

> **Remark 9.4H (Why the mass term is derived, not imported — and the Huygens integral form).** The content of Theorem 9.4G that is more than a consistency check is part (ii): the second-order operator and its mass term are *constructed* by squaring the first-order x₄-generator (Prop 2.1), so m²c²/ℏ² appears as the squared Compton frequency ω_C² of the x₄-advance, not as a constant placed into □ by hand. Applying □ to an assumed on-shell plane wave would only verify the mass shell it was built from; the derivational step is that the generator is first-order (the rate dx₄/dt = ic) and the wave equation is its square. The same content has an integral (Huygens) form: by the spherical-wavefront character (Thm 9.4C), the McGucken Spheres emitted from each point of a Cauchy surface are the elementary secondary wavefronts, and the Klein–Gordon equation is the self-consistency (Huygens–Fresnel–Kirchhoff) condition on their superposition — the differential and integral expressions of one wavefront fact. This places Klein–Gordon upstream of the Dirac square root of §3.1: the spinor square-roots the very operator here derived, so the §3 tower and this section meet — Dirac's "square root of Klein–Gordon" square-roots a Klein–Gordon equation that is itself the squared first-order x₄-generator. The nonrelativistic Schrödinger equation follows by the standard slow-envelope reduction (factoring exp(−imc²t/ℏ) and dropping ∂_t²), placing nonrelativistic quantum mechanics downstream of the same wavefront.

*Note added in the present paper.* The rest-frame generator-square equation of (ii), the dispersion relation of (iii), and the massless limit (iv) are verified symbolically in Appendix A, checks 17 and 18 (the plane-wave d'Alembertian and the exact Schrödinger envelope reduction), and the mass shell of (i) is check 15 multiplied by m².

### 9.2E The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic as a connection: phase and wavelike oscillation as geometric content

The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is a connection. Its advance moves the base point along x₄; its imaginary unit applies a quarter-turn to whatever rides on the advance. Reading the increment this way makes the wave character of matter a geometric consequence of the principle: the phase, its periodicity, and the oscillation itself descend from the fact that the advance is quarter-turned, before any quantum postulate is added.

> **Theorem 9.4I (Phase and oscillation from the McGucken Principle).** *Write the increment of the McGucken Principle as dx₄ = ic·dt. Then:*
>
> *(i) [Quarter-turn increment] ic = c·e^{iπ/2} (verified): the advance proceeds at magnitude c in the direction one quarter-turn from real space. The imaginary unit is the quarter-turn operator itself, carried by every increment.*
>
> *(ii) [Base translates, fibre rotates] The same increment acts on two objects. On the base coordinate it is a fixed displacement, x₄ ↦ x₄ + ic·dt, summing to the straight advance x₄ = ict with d²x₄/dt² = 0 (verified): the coordinate translates and does not orbit. On a phase ψ riding the advance it acts multiplicatively, ψ ↦ (1 + i·rate·dt)ψ; at ψ = 1 the increment dψ ∝ i is perpendicular to ψ (verified): each increment turns the phase by a quarter-turn. Translation of the base and rotation of the fibre are one increment acting on two objects.*
>
> *(iii) [Compounded increments are oscillation] The fibre rotation compounds by the exponential map: lim_{n→∞}(1 + iθ/n)^n = e^{iθ} (verified), a periodic circulation with d²/dt²(e^{iωt}) = −ω²e^{iωt} (verified, centripetal). The phase riding the x₄-advance therefore oscillates. The closure i⁴ = 1 (verified) makes the oscillation periodic — it returns each period rather than spiraling.*
>
> *(iv) [The imaginary unit is what makes it wave] A real advance of the same magnitude, dx₄/dt = c with no imaginary unit, gives the monotone e^{ct} with d²/dt²(e^{ct}) = +c²e^{ct} (verified): growth, no oscillation. The wave character comes from the quarter-turn i — the perpendicularity of the fourth axis — not from the magnitude c. Perpendicularity of the fourth axis is already wavelike behavior.*

*Proof.* (i) ic = c·e^{iπ/2} is the polar form of the imaginary unit scaled by c (verified). (ii) On the coordinate, integrating the constant increment gives x₄ = ict, a straight line, d²x₄/dt² = 0 (verified); on a phase, the increment is multiplication by 1 + i·rate·dt, whose action at ψ = 1 is dψ ∝ i, perpendicular to ψ (verified) — a quarter-turn. (iii) The product of n perpendicular kicks is (1 + iθ/n)^n → e^{iθ} (verified), periodic with centripetal second derivative −ω² (verified) and closure i⁴ = 1 (verified). (iv) Replacing i by 1 gives e^{ct}, monotone, second derivative +c² (verified), with no oscillation; the oscillation is therefore attributable to the imaginary unit. ∎ **G1** for (i)–(iv): the quarter-turn increment, the base/fibre split, the compounding to periodic oscillation, and the contrast establishing that the imaginary unit is the source of the wave character.

> **Remark 9.4J (What the geometry gives, and where the frequency needs the action quantum).** Theorem 9.4I establishes the wave *character* — phase, periodicity, oscillation — as geometric content of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic: matter has a phase and oscillates because the fourth-axis advance is quarter-turned, and compounded quarter-turns are e^{iθ}. This is a physical consequence of the principle prior to any quantum postulate. What the geometry alone does not fix is the *rate*. The quarter-turn is "per unit of the advance," a dimensionless geometric statement; identifying the physical oscillation rate as the Compton frequency ω_C = mc²/ℏ requires the action-per-cycle of the wavefront, the action quantum ℏ of Theorem 9.4C. So the wave exists by geometry (G1), and its pitch is set by ℏ (G1 given the action quantum, with the universality of ℏ the G2 seam of Remark 9.4D). The three offices of the single imaginary unit meet here: it sets the advance perpendicular to real space (the Wick relation as identity, §11.5), it drives the phase in a periodic circulation (this theorem), and it is the complex structure of the Born norm and the spinor half-angle (Theorem 5.6, Proposition 6.1) — one imaginary unit, one quarter-turn, carried by every increment of the McGucken Principle. The oscillation lives on the fibre that rides the advance; the base coordinate x₄ translates straight (ii). The wave is in what rides the advance, not in the advance's own trajectory.

### 9.2F Derivative and integral as the two channels: the McGucken Principle as the differential form of the Wick rotation

The two forms of the McGucken Principle — the differential dx₄/dt = ic and the integrated x₄ = ict — are related by differentiation and integration, and this relation is a specific instance of the Lie algebra / Lie group correspondence. The differential form carries the active oscillation (§9.2E); the integrated form is the static coordinate on which the metric is built. The map between them is the elementary calculus of d/dt and ∫dt.

> **Theorem 9.4K (The two forms as Lie generator and group parameter; the McGucken Principle as the differential form of the Wick rotation).**
>
> *(i) [Lie reading] The generator dx₄/dt = ic is the Lie-algebra element ic ∈ u(1)⊗ℝ, the infinitesimal generator of the one-parameter phase subgroup exp(i·(rate)·t) (verified: d/dθ exp(iθ)|₀ = i). The coordinate x₄ = ict is the accumulated group parameter, the argument of the exponential. Differentiation d/dt returns the generator from the coordinate; integration ∫dt returns the coordinate from the generator; the two are inverse up to the initial value x₄(0) (fundamental theorem of calculus, verified). The differential form is the generator; the integrated form is the group parameter.*
>
> *(ii) [Wick reading] The integrated coordinate is imaginary time: x₄ = ict gives x₄/c = it (verified). The fourth axis is the time axis rotated by the quarter-turn i — the Wick rotation, carried structurally by the McGucken Principle rather than performed afterward. Because ∫ic dt = ict is linear, the accumulation of identical i-increments equals one global axis rotation: the standard once-and-for-all Wick rotation t ↦ iτ is the integrated form of the per-increment i of the McGucken Principle. The Wick rotation applied to the Schrödinger equation returns the heat equation ∂_τψ = −(Ĥ/ℏ)ψ (verified), the static Euclidean form.*
>
> *(iii) [Two forms, two visibilities] General relativity works on the coordinate x₄ = ict through the metric (§11), the integrated form, in which the derivative content is flattened into a fixed signature and no oscillation is manifest. Quantum mechanics works on the differential form through the generator dψ/dt = −(i/ℏ)Ĥψ (verified: the generator is i times a Hermitian operator, §9.2E, Remark 2.2), in which the per-increment i drives the phase and oscillation is manifest. Both forms descend from the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic: general relativity by integrating the derivative content into the metric, quantum mechanics by keeping it active on the phase fibre. The oscillation is latent in the coordinate — recovered by differentiating a phase written on x₄ — so its absence from the general-relativistic equations is a fact about which form is used, with the oscillation present at every point of the integrated form (§9.2E(iv), verified: differentiating x₄ = ict returns ic).*

*Proof.* (i) The one-parameter subgroup exp(iθ) has generator d/dθ exp(iθ)|₀ = i (verified), so ic is the u(1) generator scaled by c; ∫₀ᵗ ic ds = ict and d/dt(ict) = ic (verified) are inverse up to x₄(0). (ii) x₄/c = it (verified); the substitution t ↦ iτ in the Schrödinger generator gives ∂_τψ = −(Ĥ/ℏ)ψ (verified). (iii) The generator dψ/dt = −(i/ℏ)Ĥψ has the imaginary unit on every increment (verified, §9.2E); the metric form carries x₄ = ict with the imaginary unit spent on the signature (§11.5); differentiating x₄ = ict returns ic (verified), so the oscillation is recoverable. ∎ **G1** for the calculus facts (the inverse d/∫ maps, x₄/c = it, the Wick-to-heat reduction, the generator as i times Hermitian). **G2** for the identification of the Algebraic and Geometric channel contents with the Lie group parameter and Lie algebra generator respectively — a correspondence with standard Lie theory, stated as an identification and not a derivation.

> **Remark 9.4L (One imaginary unit, two rotations — the axis and the fibre kept distinct).** The imaginary unit of the McGucken Principle performs two rotations that must be kept separate. The **axis** rotation is the Wick rotation: x₄ = ict makes the fourth axis imaginary time (x₄/c = it), which fixes the Lorentzian signature (§11.5). The **fibre** rotation is the phase circulation: the generator applies a quarter-turn to the phase riding the advance at every increment (§9.2E), which is the quantum oscillation. Both are the single imaginary unit of Theorem 5.6, and this is the unification — but they act on different objects (the base axis versus the phase fibre) and are different rotations. The McGucken Principle is the differential form of the Wick rotation in the axis sense (the integrated x₄ = ict is imaginary time); the per-increment phase rotation of a fibre is the quantum oscillation, a distinct action of the same unit. Two further identifications belong here as statements, not derivations: at the level of quantum field theory the differential/integrated pair is the Wightman/Osterwalder–Schrader relationship (Minkowski axioms and Euclidean axioms related by Wick rotation), and at the level of exterior calculus the pair (d, ∫) is the Stokes adjunction. These place the channel relationship within the Lie-theoretic and Cartan–de Rham algebra–geometry correspondences of standard mathematics; the identifications are recorded here and graded G2, the specific physical instance being the content the McGucken Principle supplies.
