### 9.2G Two stances on the one advance: conservation laws (Noether) and interference (Huygens) as the two channel readings

The two forms of the McGucken Principle (§9.2F) correspond to two observer stances on the same advance, and the two stances read the two most foundational results of classical mathematical physics: Noether's theorem and Huygens' principle. This is a reading of standard physics through the dual channels, offered at the grades below.

> **Theorem 9.4M (The two channel stances; Noether and Huygens as their readings).**
>
> *(i) [Stationary stance — the invariants pass through] An observer at rest with respect to x₄ = ict watches the spherically symmetric advance pass through at c, carrying the wavefront invariants of Theorem 9.4C: the Compton frequency ω_C = mc²/ℏ, the Compton wavelength λ_C = h/mc, and one quantum of action ΔS = h per cycle (verified: E = ℏω_C = mc²). Noether's theorem applied to the symmetries of this advance gives the conservation laws — time-translation invariance to energy, space-translation to momentum, the SO(3) symmetry of the spherical advance to angular momentum, U(1) phase invariance of the Compton clock to charge. This stance reads discrete spectra, conservation laws, and unitary evolution.*
>
> *(ii) [Co-moving stance — riding the wavefront] An observer riding the expanding McGucken Sphere reads the wavefront's spreading. Huygens' principle — every point of a wavefront is a secondary source — is the statement that the McGucken Sphere emitted from every event is an elementary secondary wavefront (Theorem 9.4C, the Huygens–Fresnel form of Remark 9.4H). The superposition of these Spheres gives interference; the wavefront amplitude ψ gives the Born density |ψ|² over a spatial slice (Theorem 9.4E); the Wick-rotated evolution is the heat kernel (Theorem 9.4K), whose spreading is wavepacket dispersion. This stance reads interference, wavepacket spreading, and probability distributions.*
>
> *(iii) [Same advance, two readings] The stationary and co-moving stances are two readings of the one advance dx₄/dt = ic, related by the Wick reparametrization of §9.2F. Noether's conservation content and Huygens' wavefront content are the two stances' primary readings of the same substrate; both hold of the same events.*

*Proof.* (i) The wavefront invariants ω_C, λ_C, ΔS = h are Theorem 9.4C (with the ℏ-dependence marked there); E = ℏω_C = mc² (verified). Noether's theorem (cited, G1-documentary) maps the listed symmetries to the listed conservation laws. (ii) Huygens' every-point-a-source is the McGucken Sphere from every event (Theorem 9.4C); interference is Sphere superposition; the Born density is Theorem 9.4E; the heat-kernel evolution is Theorem 9.4K. (iii) The two forms are related by the Wick reparametrization (Theorem 9.4K), so the two stances read one advance. ∎ **G1** (documentary) for Noether's theorem and Huygens' principle as cited results, and **G1**-given-ℏ for the identification of the read invariants with the wavefront invariants ω_C, λ_C, ΔS = h (Theorem 9.4C). **G2** for the identification of the Algebraic and Geometric channel stances with the stationary and co-moving observers, and for the reading of Noether's and Huygens' results as the two stances' primary content — a structural interpretation, not a derivation.

> **Remark 9.4N (Scope, and what is not claimed).** The two-stance reading organizes standard physics: the conservation laws the stationary observer measures and the interference the co-moving observer measures both hold of the same events, one from each channel. It is an interpretation at the grades stated, and three limits are marked. First, Noether's theorem and Huygens' principle are cited standard results, not derived here; the framework's content is their identification with the two channel stances (G2). Second, the invariants the stationary stance reads carry ℏ (ω_C = mc²/ℏ, ΔS = h), so this stance's quantitative content is G1-given-ℏ, with the universality of ℏ the G2 seam of Remark 9.4D. Third, a diffusive (Brownian) reading of the co-moving stance would reproduce a diffusion coefficient of the form ℏ/2m; because that coefficient carries ℏ, such a reading is consistent with a stochastic-mechanics description given the same action quantum, not an independent derivation of it. The reading is offered as a structural organization of known physics through the dual channels; it does not claim to resolve the interpretation of quantum measurement, and the unitary and probabilistic descriptions are recorded as the two stances' readings without a claim that one supersedes the other.

### 9.3 The sharpened residual

What Theorem 9.4 does *not* establish — and what we do not claim — is that dx₄/dt = ic forces the spinor layer to be *primitive*. Theorem 5.6 takes the single-complex spinor as premise and shows it forces (1,3) and, via §9.2, the double cover; the converse — that the principle compels S to exist as fundamental rather than as a structure emergent from the vector/tensor layer — is not proved. The original Open Problem 1 ("derive that the relevant representation is S rather than Λ•") therefore splits:

> **Closed (G1, given Theorem 5.6).** The double cover, the half-angle, and 2π ↦ −1, once the single-complex spinor is admitted.

> **Open Problem 1′ (primitivity, in Atiyah's terms).** Atiyah's sharpest form of the question is: *what is a spinor when there is no complex structure?* — for spinors exist without one (Euclidean Spin(2n)). By Theorem 5.6 and Remark 5.7, "no complex structure" is the quaternionic, static, SU(2) × SU(2) sector — geometry with no moving dimension. The single complex structure and the one moving dimension appear together. Atiyah's question therefore becomes, in Light Time Dimension: *what is geometry with no moving dimension, and why does admitting one complex structure — one moving x₄ — make the spinor the primitive root layer (§9.1) rather than the emergent square (vector/tensor) layer?* Equivalently: derive from dx₄/dt = ic that the square-root layer is fundamental.

Atiyah himself named the program this requires: just as the depth of √−1 lay not in its algebra but in complex *analysis*, the depth of the spinor will lie in a *spinor analysis* — a calculus standing to the spinor as complex analysis stands to √−1 — which he called the first stage of understanding the square root of geometry [Atiyah, *What is a Spinor?*]. In Light Time Dimension this is the calculus in which the half-circuit transport (§9.1), the first-order generator of x₄-motion (Proposition 2.1), is the primitive object.

**Remark 9.5 (The root layer is the generator layer).** Proposition 2.1 fixes what "the square-root layer is primitive" means: the root layer is the *generator* (first-order) layer and the squared layer the *flow/observable* (second-order) layer. The transport q = exp(½ θ n̂·J⃗) is the exponential of a first-order generator; the rotation q(·)q⁻¹ is its degree-two image (§9.1); the Dirac operator D is the first-order root of □ (§3.1). Atiyah's principle — first-order is fundamental because it exponentiates to motion — is thus the operator-theoretic statement of Open Problem 1′: to make the spinor primitive is to make the first-order generator layer primitive and the second-order metric layer its exponential. The one first-order generator is dx₄/dt = ic. *(G3 lead.)* In the same passage Atiyah attaches to his first-order advanced operator a shift set by the Compton wavelength and a second constant he reads as a cosmological constant; that a single first-order generator should couple the quantum and cosmological scales is the shape of dx₄/dt = ic itself, and is recorded here as a target, not a result.

This is the genuine Atiyah-depth question, now isolated: not "what is the half-angle" (Lemma 9.1) nor "why a double cover" (Theorem 9.4), but "why is geometry founded on its square root." Proposition 9.3 reframes it favorably — the square-root layer is the same one already used for the Dirac and interval roots of §3, so admitting it is no extra cost beyond what this paper's central result already assumes. With Open Problem 1′ closed, the spin–statistics mechanism of §8 (Theorem 8.3) would upgrade from G2 to a derivation, and the central-charge problem c = 6Q₁Q₅ would inherit the same square-root layer.

## 10. The Static Four-Space Carries No Physics: the Moving x₄ Injects Relativity, Quantum Mechanics, and Their Symmetries

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

Theorem 5.6 split the four-space into two real structures: the moving single-complex sector of signature (1,3), and the static quaternionic sector of signature (4,0). The most exotic geometry known in dimension four — Donaldson's smooth four-manifold theory, with its diagonalization theorem for definite intersection forms, its gauge-theoretic invariants, and the uncountably many exotic smooth structures on ℝ⁴ (Donaldson 1983; Freedman 1982; Witten 1994) — lives *entirely* in the static sector: these are theorems of Riemannian, definite, motionless four-manifolds. We prove here that this static sector contains *neither* relativity, *nor* quantum mechanics, *nor* the symmetries either requires, and that the single i of dx₄/dt = ic is exactly the operation that injects all three at once. The exotic topology of dimension four is a static gift; the physics is not in it until the i.

### 10.1 The static four-space and its structures

**Proposition 10.1 (Static structures and symmetry).** *In the definite (Euclidean) four-space: (i) the Hodge star on Λ² satisfies ⋆² = +1, splitting the six-dimensional 2-forms into three self-dual and three anti-self-dual, a middle-degree self-pairing unique to n = 4; (ii) the self-dual 2-forms are the symmetric square of a chiral spinor, Λ²₊ ≅ Sym²(S⁺), dim = 3 = 3 — a spinor square; (iii) the isometry group is a subgroup of the compact SO(4), with double cover Spin(4) = SU(2)_L × SU(2)_R, two independent chiral factors.*

*Proof.* (i) ⋆² = (−1)^{k(n−k)} Euclidean; (k,n) = (2,4) ⇒ +1 (verified), eigenspaces of dimension 3. (ii) dim Sym²(ℂ²) = 3 = dim Λ²₊ (verified). (iii) Definite metric ⇒ isometry group orthogonal and compact; identity component SO(4), double-covered by SU(2) × SU(2). ∎ **G1.**

### 10.2 The static sector hosts no physics

**Theorem 10.2 (Absence of relativity, quantum mechanics, and their symmetries).** *In the definite (4,0) sector:*

*(i) [no relativity] The metric is positive-definite: every pair of distinct points has Δs² > 0, so there is no timelike direction, no null cone (the only null vector is 0), no causal order, no finite invariant speed. The isometry group is the compact SO(4), with no boosts and no invariant cone — not the noncompact Lorentz group SO⁺(1,3) relativity requires.*

*(ii) [no quantum mechanics] By Theorem 5.6 the sector carries the quaternionic triple (Spin(4) = SU(2) × SU(2), three anticommuting complex structures), not a single complex structure. With no single i there is no complex amplitude, no Born norm ⟨ψ|ψ⟩ singled out as timelike, and — by Stone's theorem, which requires a single anti-Hermitian generator iH (Prop 2.1, Remark 2.2) — no unitary one-parameter evolution e^{−iHt}, hence no Schrödinger dynamics.*

*(iii) [no Dirac spinor] The Weyl modules S⁺, S⁻ are independent (pseudoreal) representations of the two independent SU(2) factors, not related by complex conjugation. The physical Dirac spinor requires S⁻ = conj(S⁺), which a single complex structure supplies and the quaternionic sector does not. The static sector cannot carry the physical Dirac spinor.*

*Proof.* (i) Positive-definiteness gives Δs² > 0 for distinct points; no signature split, no cone; Isom₀ = SO(4), compact, no noncompact one-parameter subgroups (boosts). (ii) Theorem 5.6(iv): the definite form requires the explicit i on the full quaternion triple, three anticommuting structures, not one; a unitary one-parameter group needs the single iH (Remark 2.2), absent here. (iii) Spin(4) = SU(2)_L × SU(2)_R with S⁺, S⁻ the two independent fundamentals; conjugation relating them is a feature of the Lorentzian real form SL(2,ℂ), not of the compact product. ∎ **G1.**

### 10.3 The single i injects the physics

**Theorem 10.3 (The i as the injection of physics).** *The single i of dx₄/dt = ic — the Wick rotation x₄ = ict — carries the static (4,0) sector to the moving (1,3) sector, introducing simultaneously:*

*(i) [relativity] SO(4) → SO⁺(1,3): the compact rotation group becomes the noncompact Lorentz group; ⋆² on Λ² flips +1 → −1; the null cone appears (the locus the spinor squares to, Thm 5.3); the finite invariant speed c is the rate in the primitive.*

*(ii) [quantum mechanics] SU(2) × SU(2) → SL(2,ℂ) with S⁻ = conj(S⁺): the quaternionic triple collapses to a single complex structure; the Born norm ⟨ψ|ψ⟩ becomes the distinguished timelike direction (Thm 5.6); unitary evolution e^{−iHt} becomes available, its anti-Hermitian generator the first-order x₄-generator (Prop 2.1).*

*(iii) [the symmetries] The physical symmetry groups — Lorentz/Poincaré and the unitary group of quantum mechanics — are exactly the images under the i of the static SO(4) and Spin(4). They are absent from the static sector and produced by the rotation.*

*Proof.* Each transition is the analytic continuation t → it (the Wick rotation) applied to Proposition 10.1: the signature change (4,0) → (1,3) (Thm 5.6 iii), the ⋆² flip +1 → −1 (verified), and the group continuation Spin(4) = SU(2) × SU(2) → SL(2,ℂ) = Spin⁺(1,3) in which the two compact factors become complex conjugates. The single i is the McGucken primitive's i (§2, Thm 5.6, Prop 6.1). ∎ **G1** for the signature/group transitions; the identification of the rotating i with the physical expansion dx₄/dt = ic is the standing **G2**.

The three injections, side by side:

| Structure | Static (4,0) — Donaldson | Moving (1,3) — physical, via i |
|---|---|---|
| Signature | +,+,+,+ (definite) | +,+,+,− (Lorentzian) |
| ⋆² on Λ² | +1 (real SD/ASD split) | −1 (SD/ASD complex) |
| Cone | none (only null vector is 0) | light cone; speed c |
| Isometry | compact SO(4) | Lorentz SO⁺(1,3) |
| Cover | SU(2)_L × SU(2)_R | SL(2,ℂ), S⁻ = conj(S⁺) |
| Complex structure | quaternionic triple | single i (Born norm) |
| Evolution | none | unitary e^{−iHt} |
| Spinor | Euclidean S⁺, S⁻ (Donaldson) | physical Dirac spinor |

The exotic four-manifold topology belongs to the left column and survives unchanged under no operation; everything physics requires belongs to the right column and is absent from the left. The arrow between the columns is the single i — the moving x₄.

### 10.4 Historical placement, and the exotic-ℝ⁴ gap

**Remark 10.4 (What was known, and what was not).** The result is group-and-signature mathematics (G1) plus the standing i ↔ x₄ identification (G2); the following is a historical assessment, not a theorem, stated without flattery. The Euclidean (definite-signature) character of Donaldson's and Seiberg–Witten's four-manifold theory is *universally understood*, not overlooked: Atiyah's own instanton work (the ADHM construction, self-dual Yang–Mills) is explicitly Euclidean; Witten's topological field theory realized the Donaldson invariants as a topological twist of 𝒩 = 2 supersymmetric Yang–Mills; Seiberg–Witten theory descends from 𝒩 = 2 physics. The relationship to physics through the Wick rotation and the topological twist was contemplated intensively and produced major results. What is *standard* is the framing of the Euclidean sector as the Wick-rotated calculational shadow of Lorentzian physics — Euclidean-as-tool, Lorentzian-as-primary, the i an analytic-continuation device, not a physical process. What is *not* standard is the active inversion offered here: the static sector is a substrate carrying no physics, and the i is the physical expansion dx₄/dt = ic that injects relativity, quantum mechanics, and the symmetries. The specific articulation — that Donaldson's four-space hosts no Lorentz group, no single i, no Born rule, and cannot carry the physical Dirac spinor of his advisor Atiyah without the i — is, to our knowledge, not a stated result, though every underlying piece (Euclidean vs Lorentzian spinor structures, the Wick rotation) is entirely standard. A niche literature (Brans; Asselmeyer-Maluga) has asked whether exotic smoothness carries physical relevance, largely inconclusively. The honest conclusion mirrors §3.10 of the companion null-hypersurface analysis: the gap did not go unnoticed — the Euclidean/Lorentzian distinction is foundational — but the "Euclidean-as-tool" framing made the active question appear already answered and foreclosed the reading made here.

**Remark 10.5 (What the framework does not claim about exotic ℝ⁴).** Theorem 10.2 concerns the *physics-bearing structure* (signature, symmetry group, complex structure, spinor type) of the static sector, not its *smooth-structure exotica*. The existence of uncountably many smooth structures on ℝ⁴ is a differential-topological fact about diffeomorphism types; the present framework neither derives it nor is contradicted by it. The injection of physics by the i (Theorem 10.3) acts on signature and symmetry, not on smooth structure; whether the exotic smooth structures carry consequence under the moving x₄ is left open, a question for the spinor analysis of §9.3, not a claim of this section. **G3** (open).

### 10.6 Donaldson's theorem: an i-free statement reached only through the imported i

The deepest result of the static sector — Donaldson's theorem (Donaldson 1983), the one that revealed exotic ℝ⁴ — sharpens the thesis of this section in a precise and initially surprising way. The *statement* of the theorem contains no i, no metric, and no signature. Its *only known proof* runs entirely on the imported i — the Euclidean signature that is the spent form of the Wick rotation. We make both halves exact, because the distinction is the whole point and conflating them would be overreach in either direction.

**The statement is metric-free.** Donaldson's theorem concerns the intersection form of a closed, simply-connected, smooth four-manifold X: the unimodular symmetric bilinear pairing

Q_X : H²(X;ℤ) × H²(X;ℤ) → ℤ, (α,β) ↦ ⟨α ⌣ β, [X]⟩,

defined by the cup product and Poincaré duality.

**Theorem 10.6 (Donaldson 1983; stated, not reproved).** *If X is a closed, simply-connected, smooth four-manifold whose intersection form Q_X is definite, then Q_X is diagonalizable over ℤ: Q_X ≅ diag(±1, …, ±1).*

The intersection form is a homotopy invariant — defined with no reference to any Riemannian or Lorentzian metric, no Hodge star, no signature, no i. A four-manifold carries Q_X whether or not it is ever given a metric of any signature, and "diagonalizable over ℤ" is a statement in the arithmetic of unimodular lattices. **Theorem 10.6 is therefore an i-free statement**, and the present framework does not pretend otherwise; to claim the topological conclusion "contains" dx₄/dt = ic would be exactly the category error Remark 10.4 warns against.

**The proof is i-saturated at every load-bearing step.** Donaldson's route to this metric-free truth — the only route known in 1983, and the one that won the Fields Medal — is the moduli space of anti-self-dual instantons, and every structural feature the proof depends on is the imported Euclidean i. Fix the orientation so Q_X is negative definite (so b⁺ = 0), and take the SU(2) bundle with c₂ = 1.

**Proposition 10.7 (Each pillar of the proof is the imported i).** *In the instanton proof of Theorem 10.6:*

*(i) The equation solved exists only in Euclidean signature.* The anti-self-duality equation F = −⋆F is a *real* constraint precisely because ⋆² = +1 on Λ² in signature (4,0) (Proposition 10.1(i)); in Lorentzian signature ⋆² = −1 and the real self-dual/anti-self-dual split does not exist (Theorem 10.3(i)). The object Donaldson solves for is unavailable until the i has rotated (1,3) to (4,0).

*(ii) The moduli space is finite-dimensional only because the operator is elliptic.* The linearized deformation operator of the ASD equation is elliptic in Euclidean signature, and its Atiyah–Singer index gives the moduli-space dimension dim ℳ = 8c₂ − 3(1 + b⁺) = 8 − 3 = 5. (The full Atiyah–Hitchin–Singer formula is dim ℳ = 8c₂ − 3(1 − b₁ + b⁺); Donaldson's hypothesis that X is simply-connected sets b₁ = 0, which is what reduces it to 8c₂ − 3(1 + b⁺). The reduction therefore depends on the simply-connectivity assumption, not on the signature.) Ellipticity is a Euclidean-signature property; the physical Lorentzian Yang–Mills operator is hyperbolic — an evolution equation with no finite-dimensional solution count. The number "5" is a gift of the imported i.

*(iii) The moduli space is compactifiable only by Uhlenbeck compactness.* Finite-action instantons and the Uhlenbeck compactness that makes ℳ a compact cobordism-with-ends are facts of the Euclidean Yang–Mills functional. They have no Lorentzian counterpart.

*Proof.* Each clause is a standard fact of gauge theory on Riemannian four-manifolds (Donaldson–Kronheimer 1990; Freed–Uhlenbeck 1984), here only re-read: in each case the property holds in signature (4,0) and fails in (1,3), and the passage between them is the single i of Theorem 10.3, i.e. the Wick rotation t → iτ that is the integrated content of dx₄/dt = ic. ∎ **G1** that each pillar requires Euclidean signature; **G2** that this Euclidean i is the physical i of dx₄/dt = ic.

**The engine.** With these three Euclidean inputs, the proof runs: ℳ is a 5-dimensional oriented manifold whose non-compact ends consist of (a) a collar diffeomorphic to X itself, from instantons concentrating at points of X (Taubes gluing), and (b) a cone on ℂP² at each *reducible* connection, the reducibles being in bijection with the ± pairs of lattice vectors α ∈ H²(X;ℤ) of square α² = −1. Excising the ends presents ℳ as a compact oriented cobordism between X and a disjoint union of copies of ℂP², one per reducible; cobordism invariance then forces the count of square-(−1) vectors to be exactly that of the diagonal lattice, which forces Q_X to be diagonal. The metric-free conclusion is reached entirely through the metric-dependent, Euclidean-signature, imported-i machinery.

**Why the imported i is the instrument of his fame, not an incidental.** This is the part that is more than a slogan. Freedman (1982) had already classified *topological* simply-connected four-manifolds by their intersection form, with no gauge theory and no metric — and his topological methods are structurally blind to smooth structure: a homeomorphism invariant cannot see a diffeomorphism difference. The thing Donaldson saw that no purely topological method could see — that definite smooth forms must be standard, hence that Freedman's exotic definite forms (e.g. E₈) bound *no* smooth manifold, hence the existence of exotic ℝ⁴ — became visible *only* through the instanton lens, i.e. only through the imported Euclidean i. The one new thing dimension four had to show, the smooth structure invisible to topology, was seen through the moving dimension's i, frozen into a Riemannian metric and never named as such.

**Remark 10.8 (The exact claim, and its grade).** The honest statement is three-layered. *(a)* Theorem 10.6 itself is i-free topology — **not** a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic, and not claimed to be (Remarks 10.4, 10.5). *(b)* Every pillar of its only known proof — the existence of the ASD equation via ⋆² = +1, the finite moduli dimension via ellipticity, the compactness via Uhlenbeck — requires Euclidean signature: **G1**, standard and uncontroversial. *(c)* That Euclidean signature is the spent form of the single physical i of dx₄/dt = ic, so the proof is structurally parasitic on the unacknowledged moving dimension, and the smooth-structure vision it bought was accessible only through it: **G2**, resting on the single-i identification of Theorem 5.6 and Theorem 10.3. The framework's contribution is not to re-derive Donaldson's topology — it cannot and does not — but to name what his proof silently runs on: the i he wrote as "Riemannian" and never returned.

## 11. The Observed Lorentzian Metric Forces the Advance at c: Four Theorems and Their Exact Grades

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

The preceding sections derived the spinor, the signature, and the injection of physics from dx₄/dt = ic taken as the primitive. This section confronts the converse directly, at the highest available rigor, because it is the question on which the physical status of the framework turns: *does the spacetime metric we actually observe — the one carrying relativity and quantum mechanics — force the moving dimension, or merely permit it?* We prove four theorems. Three are G1; the fourth is G1 in its operative half and G2 in its identificatory half. Together they establish the strongest claim the mathematics supports and fix the exact boundary past which the claim becomes false.

The central correction is this. One is tempted to argue that the Lorentzian metric is a *static* tensor — a time-independent g_μν, as in Schwarzschild — so that no "motion" is required. That is a category error, and Minkowski space refutes it: the causal structure of *any* Lorentzian metric is its family of null cones, and each null cone *is* a sphere expanding at c. "Static" constrains the metric *components* in a chosen chart; it does not abolish the expansion of the null cone, which is the metric's causal content at every event.

Throughout, V ≅ ℝ^{1,3} is the observed spacetime with metric η of signature (1,3) (η = diag(−1,+1,+1,+1) on (t,x,y,z)). All four results are coordinate-invariant; the coordinate x₄ = ict appears only as the encoding whose status is what we adjudicate.

### 11.1 The null cone is the spherical expansion at c (Theorem 11.1)

> **Theorem 11.1 (The causal structure is the expansion at c).** *Let (V,η) be the observed Lorentzian spacetime and p₀ = (x₀, t₀) any event. The future null cone of p₀, C⁺(p₀) = { p=(x,t) : η(p−p₀, p−p₀)=0, t>t₀ }, intersects each later slice {t = const > t₀} in the metric 2-sphere Σ(p₀,t) = { x : |x−x₀| = c(t−t₀) } of radius r(t) = c(t−t₀) expanding at the rate ṙ = c. The assignment p₀ ↦ {C⁺(p₀)} is the conformal (causal) structure of η, and by the Hawking–King–McCarthy theorem the conformal structure determines η up to a positive scalar factor. Consequently the family of spheres expanding at c from every event is a complete invariant of the metric's causal content.*

*Proof.* The null condition η(p−p₀,p−p₀)=0 reads −c²(t−t₀)² + |x−x₀|² = 0, hence |x−x₀| = c|t−t₀|; the future branch gives the stated sphere, with ṙ = d[c(t−t₀)]/dt = c (verified symbolically). That the collection of null cones recovers η up to conformal factor is the Hawking–King–McCarthy theorem (Hawking, King & McCarthy 1976; Malament 1977). The residual scalar factor is the volume element, fixed by the proper-time normalization of Theorem 11.3. ∎ **G1.**

> **Remark 11.2 (Why "static" does not weaken Theorem 11.1).** A spacetime is *static* when it admits a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing field, equivalently when g_μν is t-independent in an adapted chart. Staticity is a symmetry of the metric *components*; it is silent about the null cone, which exists and expands at c at every event of *any* Lorentzian metric. In Schwarzschild the metric is static yet the local null cones expand at c exactly as in Minkowski (invariance of the local light-speed); the global tilting of those cones is the gravitational field. The Schwarzschild objection — "the metric is static, so nothing moves" — confuses a symmetry of the components with the absence of the cone. The cone is never absent. In particular **Minkowski space is not a static counterexample to the moving dimension; its defining structure is the expansion at c from every event.**

### 11.2 The four-velocity normalization is dx₄/dt = ic at rest (Theorem 11.3)

> **Theorem 11.3 (The advance at c is the metric's own normalization).** *For the observed Lorentzian metric the following are equivalent. (i) The metric has signature (1,3) with proper time η(dp,dp) = −c² dτ². (ii) Every massive worldline has four-velocity u^μ = dx^μ/dτ obeying u^μ u_μ = −c². (iii) In the encoding x₄ = ic t, every worldline at spatial rest obeys dx₄/dτ = ic, i.e. dx₄/dt = ic; a general worldline obeys the Euclidean-form normalization u₄² + u_x² + u_y² + u_z² = −c² with u₄ = ic(dt/dτ) imaginary. Each implication is an identity, not an extra hypothesis: dx₄/dt = ic is the rest-frame statement of the metric's four-velocity normalization.*

*Proof.* (i)⇒(ii): divide η(dp,dp) = −c²dτ² by dτ². (ii)⇒(iii): u^μu_μ = −c²(dt/dτ)² + |ẋ|² = −c²; at spatial rest ẋ=0 so dt/dτ = 1, and under x₄ = ic t, dx₄/dτ = ic(dt/dτ) = ic, i.e. dx₄/dt = ic (verified symbolically); for general worldlines u₄² = −c²(dt/dτ)² gives u₄² + |ẋ|² = −c². (iii)⇒(i): squaring dx₄ = ic dt gives dx₄² = −c²dt², so ds² = dx₄² + dx² = −c²dt² + dx², recovering signature (1,3). ∎ **G1.**

> **Corollary 11.4 (The advance is observed, not posited).** *The normalization u^μu_μ = −c² asserts that every massive body advances through the timelike direction at the invariant rate c: at rest the entire four-velocity budget goes to this advance, |u₄| = c; in spatial motion part is traded to the spatial sector (time dilation, dt/dτ = γ). This advance is directly measured — differential clock ageing, dilated muon lifetimes, satellite-navigation frequency offsets. The "motion" in dx₄/dt = ic is the elapse of proper time, an empirically confirmed feature of the observed metric, not an overlay.* ∎ **G1.**

*Note added in the present paper.* Theorem 11.3 states that "dx₄/dt = ic is the rest-frame statement of the metric's four-velocity normalization," and §11.5 and §13.1 below repeat the equivalence ("equivalently u^μ u_μ = -c²"; "the four-velocity normalization u^μ u_μ = -c², i.e. with dx₄/dt = ic"). Read as an equivalence of the Principle with Minkowski's norm, this is the reading the author has withdrawn: u^μ u_μ = -c² is a scalar constraint carrying no McGucken Sphere, no orientation +ic, and no measure, and the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic — the fourth dimension expanding at the velocity of light as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h — is the physical statement of which the norm is the magnitude-only shadow (Part I, Theorem 2.3 and the paragraph after it; Part IV, [9] §5.1). What Theorem 11.3 proves at G1 is the one-way statement that the observed metric's normalization is consistent with, and at rest reduces to, the magnitude c of the advance; the converse direction, from the norm to the Sphere, is what the McGucken Sphere adds and the norm lacks. The text is reproduced as published.

### 11.3 The i is forced by, and equivalent to, the timelike minus sign (Theorem 11.5)

> **Theorem 11.5 (Signature ⟺ the imaginary unit).** *Let the timelike contribution be −c² dt². The substitution x₄ = k c t renders the interval a sum of four squares iff k² = −1, i.e. k = ±i. Hence (a) the imaginary unit in x₄ = ict is the unique (up to sign) scalar effecting the Lorentzian-to-Euclidean form change, existing iff the signature carries the timelike minus sign; (b) by Theorem 11.3 that minus sign is u·u = −c², the advance at c. So the i of x₄ = ict is the algebraic marker of the timelike advance: no minus sign ⟺ no advance ⟺ no such i.*

*Proof.* Demand (k c t)² = −c²t²; then k² = −1, so k = ±i and no real k suffices (verified symbolically) — (a). For (b), (a) ties the i to the timelike minus sign and Theorem 11.3 identifies that minus sign with u·u = −c² (Corollary 11.4, the advance at c). The biconditional chain: timelike i exists ⟺ minus sign present ⟺ u·u = −c² ⟺ advance at c. ∎ **G1.**

> **Remark 11.6 (The real-metric objection, answered exactly).** It is correct that the *Lorentzian* metric in its native form contains no i: η = diag(−1,+1,+1,+1) is real, and the interval is a real number, positive, negative, or null. The i is the unique unit *encoding* the real minus sign as a fourth square, x₄ = ict. Theorem 11.5 makes this exact: the i and the minus sign are interchangeable descriptions of the *same* datum — the timelike direction — and that datum is, by Theorem 11.3, the advance at c. "There is no i in the metric" and "the metric's timelike structure is the i" are both true and compatible: the real minus sign and the imaginary unit are two notations for the one timelike advance. What is *not* available is a tertium quid — a Lorentzian timelike direction that is neither the real minus sign nor (equivalently) the i.

### 11.4 The observed quantum i is the generator of an advance (Theorem 11.7)

The metric i of §11.3 is one face of the single complex structure of Theorem 5.6. Its quantum face is independently observed, and its observation is again the observation of an advance.

> **Theorem 11.7 (The observed i of quantum theory is an evolution generator).** *Let U(t) = e^{−iHt/ℏ} be the time-evolution group of an observed quantum system with self-adjoint H. Then (a) [Stone] U(t) is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with anti-Hermitian generator −iH/ℏ, dU/dt = (−i/ℏ)H U; the i converts the observable H into the generator of the flow, and with no advance (t=0) one has U(0)=𝟙 — the i generates nothing observable; it is manifest only as the generator of the advance t ↦ U(t). (b) [Compton rate] A free particle at rest advances in phase at ω_C = mc²/ℏ, a measured rate, the quantum-phase reading of the proper-time advance of Theorem 11.3 (e^{−iω_C τ}). (c) [Empirical necessity] Real-Hilbert-space quantum theory is falsified at multi-σ by the Renou–Li–Chen protocol and its confirmations; the i is an empirically necessary feature of the observed state space.*

*Proof.* (a) is Stone's theorem (Stone 1932; Reed–Simon I, Thm VIII.8): one-parameter unitary groups correspond to self-adjoint generators via U(t)=e^{itA}, here A = −H/ℏ; the differential relation shows the i acts only through the t-flow (verified symbolically). (b) is E = ℏω with E = mc² at rest, identified with proper-time advance via Theorem 11.3. (c) is Renou et al. (2021) with Li et al. (2022) and Chen et al. (2022). ∎ **G1** for (a)–(c); the identification of this evolution-generating i with the metric i of Theorem 11.5 is the single-complex-structure content of Theorem 5.6, **G2**.

### 11.5 Synthesis: what is proved, and the exact boundary where it stops

The two claims at issue: **(C1)** the observed Lorentzian metric requires a moving dimension such as dx₄/dt = ic; **(C2)** the i observed in relativity and quantum mechanics can exist only with a moving dimension.

> **Theorem 11.8 (The advance is forced; the word "dimension" is the residual).** *(a) [G1] The metric forces, at every event, a null cone that is a sphere expanding at c (Theorem 11.1), equivalently u^μu_μ = −c² stating that every massive body advances through the timelike direction at c (Theorem 11.3, Corollary 11.4); coordinate-invariant, directly measured, not abolished by staticity (Remark 11.2). (b) [G1] The i of x₄ = ict is the unique scalar interchangeable with the timelike minus sign, hence with that advance (Theorem 11.5); the observed quantum i is the generator of the evolution whose rest-frame rate is ω_C (Theorem 11.7) — in both faces the observed i is the marker/generator of the forced advance. (c) [G2] That this advance is literally a fourth spatial-type dimension x₄ in motion, rather than "proper time elapsing," is the identification x₄ = ict ↔ dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem 5.6, Proposition 2.1); the two descriptions share all invariant content, the surplus in "dimension" is interpretive.* ∎

> **Theorem 11.9 (The exact boundary: necessity holds for the observed structure, fails for the abstract algebra).** *(a) [Affirmative] The observed Lorentzian metric forces the advance at c (G1); identifying it with the moving dimension is G2. To this extent (C1) is established. (b) [Bounding counterexample] A real 4-space with a single complex structure J, J² = −𝟙, exists as a static algebraic object — multiplication by i on ℂ² sits motionless; such an i has no advance, so the strict reading of (C2) is false for the abstract algebraic i. (c) [Reconciliation] But that abstract J is exactly the physics-free static sector of Theorem 10.2: no signature in motion, no Born evolution, no Compton phase, until a dynamics is attached. The moment the i is the observed one — the metric's timelike normalization (Theorem 11.3) or the quantum evolution generator (Theorem 11.7) — it is the marker/generator of the advance and (C2) holds. The observed i requires the advance (G1) and is the moving dimension's i (G2); the merely algebraic i does not, and is the inert J of the static sector.*

*Proof.* (a) restates Theorem 11.8. (b): (ℂ², i) realizes J = i·𝟙, J² = −𝟙, no time parameter — a static single complex structure, so an i qua algebra entails no motion. (c): by Theorem 10.2 the static complex-structure data carry no physics until the injection of Theorem 10.3; by Theorems 11.5 and 11.7 the observed metric-i and quantum-i are marker and generator of the advance. ∎ **G1** for the boundary; the cross-boundary identification (observed i = moving-dimension i) is **G2**.

> **Remark 11.10 (The honest maximal claim).** The spacetime metric we observe — the one carrying relativity and quantum mechanics — cannot be had without an advance at the invariant rate c through its timelike direction; this advance is its null-cone expansion and its proper-time normalization simultaneously (Theorems 11.1, 11.3); the imaginary unit of relativity and of quantum mechanics is the marker and generator of that advance (Theorems 11.5, 11.7); and the only thing separating this from "the metric requires the moving dimension dx₄/dt = ic" is whether the forced advance is named a "dimension in motion" or "proper time elapsing" — the same invariant content under two names (Theorem 11.8(c)). The claim is not refuted by static Schwarzschild (whose cones still expand at c, Remark 11.2), nor by the reality of η (the real minus sign *is* the i, Theorem 11.5), nor by a static complex structure (the physics-free sector, Theorem 11.9): each is the static *arena*, and the advance at c is the content it carries. What cannot be claimed, on pain of the counterexample in Theorem 11.9(b), is that a *bare algebraic* i requires motion; the necessity holds for the *observed* i, which is the only i relativity and quantum mechanics actually exhibit.

## 12. Quaternionic Quantum Mechanics Cannot Avoid the Single i: the Hilbert Space Already Carries dx₄/dt = ic

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

Quaternionic quantum mechanics (Adler 1995) replaces the complex Hilbert space by a module over ℍ, with amplitudes r₀ + r₁i + r₂j + r₃k carrying *three* anticommuting imaginary units. Its stated aspiration is to make the richer division algebra — and the internal SU(2) it contains — fundamental, with ordinary complex QM recovered as an effective limit. This section proves the aspiration is foreclosed at the first axiom: the moment one adopts a Hilbert space with a probability-conserving inner product, the single complex structure i of §11 is entailed, and with it (Theorem 11.5) the timelike structure dx₄/dt = ic. The three quaternionic units are then either inert (they drop out of every observable) or obstructive (they cannot carry the Lorentzian signature). Quaternionic QM is thus a hostile witness for the framework: a rigorous attempt to ground physics in the static three-unit sector, whose own structure forces out the single moving i and the nonlocality §11 and the companion null-hypersurface analysis attribute to the moving dimension.

> **Lemma 12.1 (Probability conservation forces an anti-self-adjoint generator).** *On any Hilbert space (real, complex, or quaternionic) with inner product ⟨·|·⟩ and Born probabilities |⟨ψ|φ⟩|², a strongly continuous evolution U(t) = e^{tA} preserves all probabilities for all t iff its generator is anti-self-adjoint, A† = −A.*

*Proof.* d/dt ⟨Uψ|Uψ⟩ = ⟨Uψ|(A† + A)|Uψ⟩; this vanishes for all ψ,t iff A† + A = 0. ∎ **G1.**

> **Lemma 12.2 (A quaternionic one-parameter flow selects a single complex structure).** *On a quaternionic module the anti-self-adjoint generator of Lemma 12.1 is, at each point, a single imaginary quaternion A = a i + b j + c k. It satisfies A² = −(a²+b²+c²)𝟙, so J := A/|A| obeys J² = −𝟙: the evolution e^{tA} runs along the single complex-structure axis J, and the two quaternionic directions orthogonal to J do not enter the flow. By Stone's theorem (Theorem 11.7) a strongly continuous observable evolution has exactly one such generator; hence a single complex structure is selected.*

*Proof.* For A = a i + b j + c k with i,j,k the standard anticommuting units, A² = −(a²+b²+c²)𝟙 (verified symbolically), the cross terms cancelling by {i,j}={j,k}={i,k}=0. Thus A generates a U(1) whose complexification is ℝ⊕ℝJ, a single complex line; components along the two units perpendicular to J are constant under the flow. ∎ **G1.**

> **Theorem 12.3 (Adopting Hilbert space + Born rule is adopting the single i, hence dx₄/dt = ic).** *Any quantum theory built on a Hilbert space with a probability-conserving evolution — quaternionic QM included — necessarily contains the single complex structure i as the generator of its evolution (Lemmas 12.1, 12.2, Stone). By Theorem 11.5 that single i is interchangeable with the timelike minus sign of the metric, and by Theorem 11.3 with the four-velocity normalization u^μu_μ = −c², i.e. with dx₄/dt = ic. Therefore the moving-dimension structure is entailed by the Hilbert-space/Born-rule machinery. Writing down a Hilbert space with conserved probabilities is writing down the single i of dx₄/dt = ic.*

*Proof.* Lemma 12.1 forces an anti-self-adjoint generator; Lemma 12.2 with Stone forces it to select a single complex structure J, J²=−𝟙; this J is the unit converting the self-adjoint Hamiltonian to the generator, A = −iH/ℏ, i.e. the quantum i. Theorem 11.5 identifies that i with the timelike minus sign and Theorem 11.3 with u^μu_μ = −c², equivalently dx₄/dt=ic at rest. Each step is forced. ∎ **G1** for the entailment of the single i from Born-conserving evolution; **G2** for the identification of that i with the moving dimension (Theorem 5.6, §11).

> **Corollary 12.4 (The two forced reappearances in Adler's theory).** *(a) [Single i] By Theorem 12.3, every observable evolution in quaternionic QM collapses to a single complex structure; this is the structural reason for Adler's own result that the quaternionic S-matrix is complex, with no dependence on j,k, for appropriate ray choices. The two extra units are inert to observable scattering. (b) [Nonlocality] Any composite system is a tensor product, with dim(H_A⊗H_B) = d_A d_B and separable-state locus of dimension d_A + d_B − 1; the gap d_A d_B − (d_A+d_B−1) = (d_A−1)(d_B−1) > 0 for d_A,d_B≥2 makes entanglement generic, and by Gisin's theorem every pure entangled state violates a Bell inequality. A quaternionic Hilbert space with multiparticle (Fock) structure therefore carries Bell nonlocality necessarily — the non-factorizable, common-origin correlation structure the companion null-hypersurface analysis attributes to the shared x₄-wavefront.*

*Proof.* (a) is Theorem 12.3 applied to the S-matrix, matching Adler's complex-S-matrix theorem (Adler 1995). (b): the dimension gap factors as (d_A−1)(d_B−1) (verified symbolically), so separable states are positive-codimension and entanglement is generic; Gisin's theorem (Gisin 1991) supplies the Bell violation. ∎ **G1.**

> **Remark 12.5 (Why ℍ, and the exact asymmetry with dx₄/dt = ic).** Quaternionic QM is motivated by a real strength: ℍ is the natural home of internal SU(2) (the unit quaternions *are* SU(2)) and of the noncommutative/gauge structure sought for unification. But this is precisely the strength of the *static* (4,0) sector (Proposition 10.1: Spin(4) = SU(2)×SU(2)). The asymmetry with the framework is exact and one-directional. Three coequal anticommuting units possess *no* distinguished generator, so they cannot manufacture the single moving i — Adler's program stalls at exactly the two points that require it: the complexified S-matrix (dynamics) and the open relativistic theory (the indefinite Lorentzian signature, which the definite algebra ℍ cannot carry). Conversely the single i of dx₄/dt = ic, being a first-order *generator* (Proposition 2.1), carries both: its frozen reading supplies the static SU(2)/gauge/signature structure (§10.3 injection), and its flow reading supplies the Born evolution, the Compton advance, and the Lorentzian timelike direction (§11). One generator yields the static algebra and the dynamics; three static units yield neither the generator nor the signature. The implication runs only one way: single i ⇒ static structure + dynamics; static triple ⇏ single i. Quaternionic QM reaches into the static sector for a structure that, in this framework, is the *shadow* of the single moving i — and then cannot supply the i that casts it.

## 13. The Lineage of the Imported i: Donaldson ← Chern ← Cartan ← the Relativistic Metric

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

Section 10.6 established that Donaldson's diagonalization theorem, an i-free topological statement, is reached only through a proof saturated with the imported Euclidean i, and that the central computational object of that proof is the Chern number c₂ of the instanton bundle. This section establishes the historical and mathematical genealogy of that i with the same rigor applied to the physics: it traces c₂ through the Chern–Weil construction to the connection-and-curvature apparatus of Élie Cartan, and that apparatus to the work Cartan carried out — by the dated titles of his own papers — on the general-relativistic metric, which (Theorem 11.3, Theorem 11.5) carries dx₄/dt = ic. The historical claims are stated as propositions and supported by primary-source dates and attributions, matched at each step to the corresponding physical fact. The result is a single descent: the imaginary unit on which Donaldson's proof runs is, both mathematically and historically, the single i of the relativistic metric, transmitted into "pure" four-manifold topology through Cartan and Chern and never, at any stage, named as such.

We are careful about one thing throughout, because it is the place where the lineage is easy to overstate. Cartan's *earliest* differential-geometric work — the method of moving frames and the calculus of exterior differential forms — was developed 1894–1904, before Minkowski (1908) and before general relativity (1915). That work is *not* the part of Cartan's apparatus on which Chern's c₂ depends. The piece c₂ requires is the *connection on a bundle and its curvature 2-form*, the general theory of which Cartan developed in 1922–1925, explicitly in the context of general relativity. The lineage below is rooted at that 1922–1925 work, not at the pre-relativistic moving-frame core; this distinction is stated as Proposition 13.3 and is what makes the descent claim defensible rather than a date-fallacy.

### 13.1 The mathematical descent: where the i in c₂ comes from

> **Proposition 13.1 (The i in c₂ is the anti-Hermitian-to-Hermitian unit).** *Let P→X be a principal U(n)- (or SU(2)-) bundle with connection A and curvature F. The Chern classes are the de Rham classes of the Chern–Weil forms det(𝟙 + (i/2π)F) = 1 + c₁ + c₂ + ⋯. The curvature F is 𝔲(n)-valued, hence anti-Hermitian, F† = −F; the factor i is precisely the unit converting F into the Hermitian iF with real spectrum, so the Chern forms have real (indeed integral) periods. Thus the i in c₂ is the same anti-Hermitian-to-Hermitian unit that, by Theorem 11.7, is Stone's generator −iH/ℏ of unitary evolution, and by Theorem 11.5 is the timelike minus sign of the Lorentzian metric.*

*Proof.* For 𝔲(1), F = if with f a real 2-form; then c₁ = (i/2π)F = −f/2π is real (verified). For 𝔲(2), a general anti-Hermitian F satisfies F†+F = 0 and iF satisfies (iF)†−(iF) = 0, i.e. iF is Hermitian; the characteristic polynomial det(λ𝟙 − (i/2π)F) then has real coefficients (verified symbolically), so c₁,c₂ are real. The unit performing the conversion anti-Hermitian → Hermitian is i, identical in role to the i of A = −iH/ℏ in Theorem 11.7 and to the k=±i of Theorem 11.5. ∎ **G1** for the algebra; **G2** for the identification of this i with the single complex structure of Theorem 5.6.

> **Proposition 13.2 (Donaldson's c₂ is built by Chern–Weil from a connection's curvature).** *The dimension of the instanton moduli space in Donaldson's proof, dim ℳ = 8c₂ − 3(1+b⁺), depends on c₂(P), computed as the Chern–Weil integral of the curvature of the SU(2)-connection (Proposition 10.7, §10.6). Hence the load-bearing invariant of Donaldson's proof is a Chern–Weil curvature integral, and by Proposition 13.1 carries the single i.*

*Proof.* The index computation giving dim ℳ = 5 for c₂=1 (Proposition 10.7) is the Atiyah–Singer index of the ASD deformation complex, whose topological input is c₂ = (1/8π²)∫_X tr(F∧F) — the second Chern–Weil form. This is Chern's construction (Chern 1946; Chern–Weil theory). ∎ **G1.**

### 13.2 The historical descent: where Chern's construction came from

The mathematical facts above fix *what* the i is. The historical propositions below fix *where it came from*, each supported by dated primary sources.

> **Proposition 13.3 (The apparatus Chern used is Cartan's connection–curvature theory, not the pre-relativistic moving-frame core).** *The Chern–Weil construction requires a connection on a bundle and its curvature 2-form. The general theory of connections with their curvature was developed by Élie Cartan in 1922–1925. Chern's own 1946 construction attributes its methods to Cartan: in Chern's words the methods were "initiated by E. Cartan" and subsequently developed by H. Cartan, Chevalley, Koszul, Leray, and Weil. The earlier Cartan apparatus of 1894–1904 (moving frames, exterior differential forms) is necessary scaffolding but is not the connection–curvature theory on which c₂ depends.*

*Historical proof.* The dated record: Cartan's connection papers are "Sur une généralisation de la notion de courbure de Riemann et les espaces à torsion" (Comptes Rendus 174, 1922) and the two-part "Sur les variétés à connexion affine et la théorie de la relativité généralisée" (Annales de l'École Normale 40, 325–412, 1923; 41, 1–25, 1924; Part II in 42, 17–88, 1925). Chern's attribution to "methods initiated by E. Cartan" is documented in Chern (1946) and Chern (1951). The moving-frame and exterior-form work is separately dated to 1894–1904. ∎ **G1** (documentary).

> **Proposition 13.4 (Cartan's connection theory was developed on, and for, the relativistic metric).** *The 1923–1925 papers in which Cartan developed the connection–curvature apparatus were explicitly papers on general relativity — their titles name "la théorie de la relativité généralisée" — and the apparatus was developed with general relativity as a primary context. The connection in these papers is the connection of a (pseudo-)Riemannian metric of Lorentzian signature: the general-relativistic spacetime metric.*

*Historical proof.* The titles are dispositive: Cartan (1923/1924/1925), "Sur les variétés à connexion affine et la théorie de la relativité généralisée." The record (the Cartan–Einstein correspondence 1929–1932, Debever ed. 1979) documents that Cartan developed his generalized-space concept with general relativity as a guiding context, the torsion notion introduced in the gravitational setting. The connection treated is that of the spacetime metric, signature (1,3). ∎ **G1** (documentary).

> **Theorem 13.5 (The relativistic metric carries dx₄/dt = ic).** *The Lorentzian metric on which Cartan's 1922–1925 connection theory operates carries the single i of dx₄/dt = ic: its signature (1,3) is, by Theorem 11.3 and Theorem 11.5, the four-velocity normalization u^μu_μ = −c² and equivalently the encoding x₄ = ict. The timelike minus sign of the metric Cartan connected is the integrated content of dx₄/dt = ic.*

*Proof.* Theorem 11.5 (signature minus sign ⟺ the unit i) with Theorem 11.3 (the minus sign is u^μu_μ=−c², i.e. dx₄/dt=ic at rest), applied to the Lorentzian metric of Proposition 13.4. ∎ **G1** for the metric/i identification; **G2** for "x₄ in motion."

### 13.3 The single descent, and what it does and does not claim

> **Theorem 13.6 (The imported i of Donaldson's proof is the i of the relativistic metric, by both mathematical and historical descent).** *The imaginary unit on which Donaldson's 1983 proof runs descends, mathematically and historically, from the single i of the relativistic metric:*
>
> dx₄/dt = ic  (Thm 13.5)  →[metric Cartan connected]→  Cartan connection–curvature, 1922–25  (Prop 13.3, 13.4)  →[inherited]→  Chern–Weil c₂, 1946  (Prop 13.1, 13.2)  →[central object]→  Donaldson 1983  (§10.6).
>
> *At every link the unit is the same single complex structure (Theorem 5.6): the anti-Hermitian-to-Hermitian unit of the Chern–Weil curvature (Prop 13.1), the connection-form unit of Cartan's apparatus, and the timelike minus sign of the metric (Thm 13.5). Donaldson's proof uses this i at its load-bearing step (c₂, hence dim ℳ = 5) and never names it, presenting it as the word "Riemannian."*

*Proof.* The mathematical links are Propositions 13.1–13.2 (Chern–Weil i in c₂, c₂ in Donaldson) and Theorem 13.5 (metric i = dx₄/dt=ic); the historical links are Propositions 13.3–13.4 (Chern's apparatus is Cartan's 1922–25 connection theory, developed on the relativistic metric). The identity of the unit across all links is Theorem 5.6 (a single complex structure) instantiated at each. ∎ **G1** for each documented or computed link; **G2** for the cross-link identification of all occurrences as the one i.

> **Remark 13.7 (Exact scope: what is proved and what is not).** *(a) The root is Cartan 1922–25, not "Minkowski 1908."* The lineage is rooted at the connection–curvature apparatus, the GR-era work; Minkowski's 1908 spacetime and Einstein's 1915 theory sit upstream as the physics the metric describes, not as the source of the mathematical apparatus. Claiming descent "from Minkowski's 1908 paper" would be a date-fallacy, since Cartan's moving-frame core predates 1908; the defensible claim is that the *connection–curvature* apparatus Chern used is the GR-era 1922–25 work. *(b) The i enters by identity, not only by inheritance.* Even setting history aside, the i in c₂ is the single complex structure of Theorem 5.6 by Proposition 13.1 alone; the historical descent shows the *same* unit was in fact transmitted from the relativistic metric, but the framework's identification does not rely on the genealogy. *(c) Donaldson used the i, not the motion.* As in §10.6, the proof uses the frozen complex structure (Euclidean signature, the connection's i), not a dynamics; he needs the single i, not the rate c.

> **Remark 13.8 (The structural reading, stated without overclaim).** The standard presentation treats characteristic classes as pre-physical pure mathematics later "applied" to physics. The lineage licenses a sharper reading: the connection–curvature apparatus underlying characteristic classes was developed (Cartan, 1922–1925) on the relativistic metric, which carries dx₄/dt = ic; the apparatus is therefore not pre-physical but *post-relativistic* mathematics whose relativistic origin is obscured by the "pure mathematics" mode of presentation. We state this as a structural-historical reading (G2), not a theorem: the documentary record (Prop 13.3, 13.4) establishes the development context and Theorem 5.6 the identity of the unit, but "no foundational mathematics is independent of relativistic spacetime" is broader than the present lineage proves and is not asserted here. What is asserted: the specific i in Donaldson's c₂ descends, mathematically and historically, from the single i of the relativistic metric.

### 13.9 What Donaldson and His Colleagues Claimed, and What Really Happened

The lineage of §13.1–13.3 is a statement about mathematical and historical fact. This subsection sets that fact against the *self-understanding* of the mathematical community — what Donaldson and his colleagues said they had done — because the gap between the two is itself evidence for the framework's reading. The claims are documented and quoted; the contrast is then stated at grade. The pattern is uniform: the result was presented as a *topology* theorem reached by *importing a tool from physics*, with the metric and the imaginary unit treated as auxiliary scaffolding, and the effectiveness of the physics regarded as a *surprise*. Under the framework's reading (Theorem 13.6), there is no surprise to explain: the topology was being decided by the frozen form of the single i of dx₄/dt = ic, used at every load-bearing step and named only "Riemannian." The recorded astonishment is the exact measure of the unnamed identification.

**The claim: a topology result importing an external physical tool.** The framing begins with the paper's own title. Donaldson's 1982/1983 result was published as *"Self-dual connections and the topology of smooth 4-manifolds"* (Bulletin of the AMS, 1983) and in full as *"An application of gauge theory to four-dimensional topology"* (Journal of Differential Geometry 18, 279–315, 1983). Both titles encode the same self-description: an *application of* gauge theory *to* topology — a tool borrowed from one discipline, a result delivered in another. Nothing in the framing suggests the gauge theory is anything but an external instrument, or that the metric on which it operates is primary.

The community's reception sharpened this into an explicit narrative of *surprise* — the claim that physics' equations had no antecedent business proving theorems of smooth topology:

- **Atiyah** (Donaldson's doctoral supervisor), on the impact of the paper, is recorded as saying it "stunned the mathematical world." The word is one of shock at an unanticipated intrusion of one field into another.
- **Manolescu** (Stanford four-dimensional topology survey) records that Donaldson's work introduced an unexpected tool in smooth 4-dimensional topology: gauge theory. The operative word is *unexpected* — the tool is framed as foreign to the subject it cracked.
- **Iga** (2002 survey, *"What do topologists want from Seiberg–Witten theory?"*, Int. J. Mod. Phys. A) writes that in 1983 Donaldson shocked the topology world by using instantons from physics to prove new theorems about four-manifolds. The framing is cross-disciplinary astonishment: instantons are *from physics*, deployed in topology.

The physical origin of the tool was openly stated, never hidden — which is exactly why it was experienced as surprising rather than as intrinsic. The instantons are described as a particular solution to the equations of Yang–Mills gauge theory which has its origin in quantum field theory. Lawson's 1983 CBMS lectures (*Theory of Gauge Fields in Four Dimensions*, AMS 1985), the first expository account, characterized the episode as one mathematical discipline yielding startling consequences in another.

So the claim, uniformly across the principals and the early literature, is: *two separate disciplines; astonishingly, the physical one settled a problem in the topological one.* At no point did anyone claim the imaginary unit in the construction was the relativistic i, that the metric was doing the decisive work, or that the topology was in any sense already physical. The metric and the gauge i were scaffolding — auxiliary, to be erected for the proof and then, ideally, removed.

**What really happened: the physics was not removable, and the surprise was the missing identification.** The "borrowed external tool" account makes a prediction it cannot meet: if gauge theory were merely a clever instrument, it should be *dispensable* once the topological result is secured. The subsequent history is the precise refutation, in three documented stages.

*Stage 1 — the invariants are a quantum field theory (Witten, 1988).* Far from removable, the gauge theory turned out to *be* the subject. Witten showed the Donaldson invariants are correlation functions of a topological quantum field theory — a twisted 𝒩=2 super-Yang–Mills theory. In Witten's 1994 statement of the established fact, Donaldson theory is equivalent to a quantum field theory, in fact, a twisted version of N=2 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory. The topology was not *using* a QFT; it *was* a QFT in topological language.

*Stage 2 — removing one piece of physics requires another (Seiberg–Witten, 1994).* When the instanton machinery was finally dispensed with, it was replaced not by topology but by *different physics*. The Seiberg–Witten monopole equations compute the same invariants with an abelian gauge group: instead of counting SU(2) instantons, one can define equivalent four-manifold invariants by counting solutions of a non-linear equation with an abelian gauge group. The SW equations are themselves Euclidean spin-ℂ gauge equations — the same imported single i (Proposition 13.1), in a cheaper bundle. Subtract one realization of the physics and the topology does not become physics-free; it demands another. A tool is removable; a substrate is not. The four-manifold theory behaves as a substrate.

*Stage 3 — the surprise was structurally inevitable, and it measures the gap.* The astonishment was genuine but its object was an artifact of the framing, not of the mathematics. It was surprising *only on the premise that the metric and the i are auxiliary*. Drop that premise — adopt Theorem 13.6 — and the surprise evaporates: the load-bearing c₂ is a Chern–Weil curvature integral carrying the single i (Prop 13.1, 13.2); that i is the relativistic metric's i (Thm 13.5); the connection–curvature apparatus computing it was developed by Cartan on the relativistic metric (Prop 13.3, 13.4). The gauge theory *had* to be effective in four-dimensional topology, because the apparatus was post-relativistic from inception (Remark 13.8) and four is the dimension where the single i does its work (Theorem 5.6, §10). The community experienced as a miracle what the framework reads as an identity; the magnitude of the recorded astonishment is the magnitude of the unrecognized identification.

> **Proposition 13.9 (Claimed versus actual, stated at grade).** *(a) [Documented claim, G1.] Donaldson and the early literature framed the 1983 result as a topology theorem reached by importing an external tool from physics, with the effectiveness regarded as surprising (title "An application of gauge theory to four-dimensional topology"; Atiyah, "stunned the mathematical world"; Manolescu, "unexpected tool"; Iga, "shocked the topology world"; Lawson, "startling consequences in another" discipline). (b) [Documented subsequent fact, G1.] The physics proved non-removable: the invariants are a twisted 𝒩=2 super-Yang–Mills theory (Witten 1988), and eliminating instantons required substituting the abelian Seiberg–Witten gauge equations (Seiberg–Witten 1994), themselves carrying the same single i (Prop 13.1). (c) [Framework reading, G2.] The recorded surprise is the symptom of the unnamed identification of Theorem 13.6: the topology was decided by the frozen single i of dx₄/dt=ic, inherited through Chern from Cartan's relativistic connection theory, used at the load-bearing step (c₂) and named only "Riemannian." Under the identification there is no surprise to explain.*

*Proof.* (a) and (b) are the documented record quoted and cited above (Donaldson 1983; Atiyah, biographical record; Manolescu 4D survey; Iga 2002; Lawson 1985; Witten 1994). (c) combines Theorem 13.6 (the descent of the i), Proposition 13.1 (the i in c₂), and the non-removability of (b): a removable tool is dispensable, a substrate is not, and the four-manifold theory behaves as a substrate. ∎ **G1** for the documentary claims (a) and the documented later facts (b); **G2** for the reading (c).

> **Remark 13.10 (Why the contrast is evidence, not mere irony).** The gap between (a) and (b)–(c) is evidence in the strict sense: the "external tool" hypothesis (a) makes a falsifiable prediction — that the physics is in principle removable from the topology — and the historical record (b) falsifies it, since every attempt to remove one physical realization installed another. The framework's reading (c) is the hypothesis under which (b) is expected rather than anomalous. This is inference to the better explanation: between "physics is a removable tool that surprisingly works" and "the topology is a frozen reading of the single i, so physics is not removable and its effectiveness is an identity," the non-removability documented in Witten 1988 and Seiberg–Witten 1994 is the datum the second explains and the first does not. The conclusion is held at G2 — an inference to the best explanation resting on the single-i identification (Theorem 5.6), not a deductive theorem — but the datum it explains (non-removability) is itself G1 and documented.

## 14. Donaldson's Apparatus and Arena as Theorems of dx₄/dt = ic: a Foundational Reconstruction Bypassing Cartan and Chern

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

Section 13 established the historical and mathematical descent of the imaginary unit in Donaldson's proof: through Chern's c₂ to Cartan's connection–curvature theory to the relativistic metric, which carries dx₄/dt = ic. This section makes the stronger constructive claim that the descent licenses: every analytic tool of Donaldson's proof — the unitary connection, its curvature, the Hodge self-duality split, the Chern–Weil number c₂, the dimension-four self-duality, and the index that fixes the moduli dimension — can be reconstructed *directly* as a structure generated by dx₄/dt = ic in its frozen (Euclidean) reading, with no appeal to the historical Cartan–Chern transmission. Cartan's connection and Chern's c₂ are *re-derived*, exhibited as instantiations of the single complex structure that the primitive is (Theorem 5.6). The section is self-contained: it states what is reconstructed, proves each piece at grade, and — with equal precision — marks the exact boundary where reconstruction stops. That boundary is the arithmetic–smoothness core of Donaldson's *theorem* (the Elkies lattice fact and the smooth-realizability obstruction), which is **not** a shadow of the moving dimension and which the framework illuminates the tools *for* without replacing. The result is a foundational demonstration of Donaldson's machinery, not a substitute for his theorem; stating both halves is what keeps it rigorous.

### 14.1 What is reconstructed, and what is not

> **Definition 14.1 (Apparatus, arena, core).** *In Donaldson's 1983 proof we distinguish three strata. The **apparatus** is the analytic toolkit: the principal SU(2)-bundle with unitary connection A, its curvature F, the Hodge operator ⋆ and the (anti-)self-dual split of Λ², the Chern–Weil form c₂, and the elliptic deformation complex with its index. The **arena** is the structural setting that makes the apparatus possible: dimension four, the Euclidean signature with ⋆²=+1, the chiral decomposition Spin(4)=SU(2)×SU(2), and the identification Λ²₊≅Sym²(S⁺). The **core** is the residual mathematical content of the theorem itself: the arithmetic of unimodular lattices (Elkies' theorem) and the smooth-realizability obstruction (which definite forms bound smooth manifolds).*

> **Theorem 14.2 (Scope of the reconstruction).** *The apparatus and the arena are reconstructible as structures generated by dx₄/dt=ic, bypassing the Cartan–Chern transmission (§14.2–14.4). The core is not so reconstructible: it is i-free mathematics (Remark 14.9). The framework derives the tools and their setting at a more foundational level than their historical origin, and exhibits the setting (dimension four, the self-dual split) as forced by the primitive — but it does not derive, and does not claim to derive, which lattices are smoothly realizable.*

*Proof.* Positive half: Propositions 14.3–14.7; negative half: Remark 14.9. ∎

### 14.2 The connection and its curvature from the single i

> **Proposition 14.3 (The unitary connection is the single i made into a transport).** *Let the internal fibre carry the single complex structure J, J²=−𝟙, of Theorem 5.6 (equivalently the unitary i of Theorem 11.7). A connection compatible with the Hermitian structure has local form ∇ = d + A with A anti-Hermitian, A† = −A; equivalently A = iH with H Hermitian. The curvature F = dA + A∧A is likewise anti-Hermitian. Thus the connection and curvature of Donaldson's bundle are constructions on the single complex structure: the i that makes A anti-Hermitian — hence the transport unitary — is the i of dx₄/dt=ic (Proposition 2.1; Theorem 11.7, Stone's generator).*

*Proof.* Hermitian-compatibility d⟨s,t⟩ = ⟨∇s,t⟩ + ⟨s,∇t⟩ forces A into the unitary Lie algebra, i.e. anti-Hermitian; A = iH gives H = −iA Hermitian (verified: A†+A = −iH†+iH = 0). Curvature inherits anti-Hermiticity. The observable→generator unit is the single i (Prop 2.1, Thm 11.7, Prop 13.1). ∎ **G1** for the construction; **G2** that the i is the primitive's.

> **Remark 14.4 (Bypassing Cartan).** Proposition 14.3 builds the connection from Hermitian compatibility and the single i alone — no appeal to Cartan's 1922–25 affine-connection theory. Historically the connection descended from Cartan (Prop 13.3); foundationally it is reconstructed here from the primitive. The two routes terminate at the same object because, by Theorem 13.5, Cartan's connection was itself built on the metric carrying the single i.

### 14.3 The arena: dimension four and the self-dual split are forced

> **Proposition 14.5 (The dimension-four self-dual split, reconstructed).** *In the frozen (Euclidean) reading of the four-space the primitive selects (Theorem 5.6, §10.2), the Hodge operator on Λ² satisfies ⋆² = (−1)^{k(n−k)} = +1 at (k,n)=(2,4), uniquely among middle-degree forms, splitting the six-dimensional Λ² into the three-dimensional self-dual and anti-self-dual eigenspaces Λ² = Λ²₊⊕Λ²₋. The chiral structure Spin(4) = SU(2)_L×SU(2)_R gives Λ²₊≅Sym²(S⁺), dim = 3 = 3: the self-dual two-forms are the symmetric square of a chiral spinor. Hence the split on which F = −⋆F depends is a structure of the four-space the primitive picks out, not an external input.*

*Proof.* Proposition 10.1 (re-verified: ⋆²=+1 at (2,4); dim Λ²₊ = 3 = dim Sym²(ℂ²)). The added point, licensed by §10.3: the four-space, its Euclidean signature, and the chiral split are the frozen sector of the primitive, so the arena is generated, not assumed. ∎ **G1.**

> **Proposition 14.6 (The anti-self-dual equation is the primitive's frozen self-duality).** *The instanton condition F = −⋆F is the statement that the curvature of the connection of Proposition 14.3 lies in the Λ²₋ eigenspace of the operator of Proposition 14.5. Both ingredients — the anti-Hermitian F and the ⋆-split — are reconstructed from the single i and the four-space it selects; therefore the ASD equation is a construction of dx₄/dt=ic in its frozen reading, with no Cartan–Chern input.*

*Proof.* Combine Props 14.3 (the F) and 14.5 (the split). The equation is the projection F⁺ = 0 onto Λ²₊, well-defined because ⋆²=+1 makes the projection real. ∎ **G1** for the construction; **G2** for the identification of the i.

### 14.4 The Chern–Weil number and the index, reconstructed

> **Proposition 14.7 (The instanton number c₂ from the curvature, bypassing Chern).** *The second Chern–Weil form c₂ = (1/8π²) tr(F∧F) is a real, integral class. Writing F = iM with M Hermitian, tr(F∧F) = i² tr(M∧M) = −tr(M∧M) is real (verified); integrality is ∫_X c₂ ∈ ℤ counting the instanton charge. The single i is exactly what renders tr(F∧F) real (the Hermitization of Prop 13.1). Thus c₂ — the load-bearing invariant of Donaldson's proof — is reconstructed from the primitive's i and the connection of Prop 14.3, with no appeal to Chern's 1946 construction.*

*Proof.* Reality is the i²=−1 computation (verified). Integrality is the Chern–Weil integrality theorem, here re-derived as a property of the single-i connection's curvature rather than imported. ∎ **G1** for reality and construction; **G2** for the i identification; integrality cited.

> **Proposition 14.8 (The moduli dimension from the index).** *The ASD deformation complex of the connection (Props 14.3, 14.6) is elliptic in the Euclidean arena (Prop 14.5), and its Atiyah–Singer index gives dim ℳ = 8c₂ − 3(1+b⁺), equal to 5 at c₂=1, b⁺=0 (verified). Ellipticity is a property of the Euclidean (frozen) signature — the one the primitive selects — so the finite dimension count is a consequence of the reconstructed arena.*

*Proof.* The dimension formula is the index of d_A*⊕d_A⁺ (Atiyah–Hitchin–Singer); 8(1)−3(1+0)=5 (verified). The general index is 8c₂ − 3(1 − b₁ + b⁺), reduced to 8c₂ − 3(1 + b⁺) by Donaldson's simply-connected hypothesis (b₁=0). Ellipticity holds in (4,0) and fails in (1,3) (§10.6, Prop 10.7), so it is a feature of the frozen reading of the primitive. ∎ **G1** given the apparatus; the index theorem cited.

### 14.5 The boundary: what the framework illuminates but does not replace

> **Remark 14.9 (The arithmetic–smoothness core is not a shadow of the moving dimension).** Propositions 14.3–14.8 reconstruct the apparatus and arena. They do **not** reconstruct Donaldson's *theorem*, and the framework does not claim they do. The theorem's content is twofold and both halves are i-free. *(a) The lattice arithmetic.* Which definite unimodular forms occur is governed by the arithmetic of integral quadratic forms — in the Seiberg–Witten route, by Elkies' theorem that the diagonal form is the unique positive-definite unimodular lattice with no characteristic vector of small norm. Pure number theory: no metric, signature, connection, or i. *(b) The smooth-realizability obstruction.* The theorem's force is that of all these lattices, only the diagonal one is the intersection form of a *smooth* manifold; the obstruction lives between the topological classification (Freedman) and the smooth one, detected by the moduli-space cobordism. Neither (a) nor (b) is generated by dx₄/dt=ic: the moving dimension supplies the single i, hence the apparatus and arena, but not the lattice theory and not the smoothness obstruction. To assert it did would be the category error of attributing i-free content to the i (cf. §10.6, Remark 10.4).

> **Theorem 14.10 (The exact foundational statement).** *(a) [Apparatus, G1 constructions / G2 identification] The unitary connection, curvature, ⋆-split, ASD equation, c₂, and index — the entire analytic toolkit — are reconstructible from the single i of the primitive, bypassing Cartan and Chern (Props 14.3–14.8). (b) [Arena, G1] Dimension four, the self-dual split, and the chiral spinor identification — the setting that makes the toolkit possible — are structures of the frozen sector the primitive selects (Props 14.5, 10.1). (c) [Core, not derivable] The lattice arithmetic and the smooth-realizability obstruction — the residual content of the theorem itself — are i-free and not generated by the primitive (Remark 14.9). The framework demonstrates Donaldson's machinery and its arena at a more foundational level than their historical derivation, and shows the dimension-four setting to be forced rather than fortuitous, while leaving the arithmetic–smoothness core as the part the apparatus is pointed at but the primitive does not supply.*

*Proof.* (a) Props 14.3, 14.6, 14.7, 14.8 with Remark 14.4; (b) Props 14.5, 10.1; (c) Remark 14.9. ∎ **G1** for the constructions and arena; **G2** for the i identifications; the core marked not-derivable, the limit asserted.

> **Remark 14.11 (Why this is the strong claim, not the weak one).** The reconstruction is more defensible than a putative "proof of Donaldson's theorem from physics." A claim to re-derive the *theorem* from dx₄/dt=ic would be refuted by exhibiting the Elkies lattice step, which carries no i; it would fail at the first request to locate the arithmetic in the primitive. The claim actually made — reconstruction of the *apparatus and arena*, with the core explicitly excluded — survives that request, because every tool's i is verifiably the single i (Props 14.3, 14.7; Thm 13.6) while the arithmetic is openly conceded to lie outside. The framework thus explains *why Donaldson's tools exist, why they take the form they do, and why dimension four is their home* — the structural questions the "surprising external tool" narrative (§13.9) left unanswered — without overreaching into the arithmetic the tools were built to probe.

### 14.6 The 1982 Proof, Object by Object, in dx₄/dt=ic Machinery

The reconstruction of §14.2–14.5 is here applied to Donaldson's actual proof as standardly described, to exhibit the foundational rewriting concretely. The standard one-sentence account (Donaldson 1983; Donaldson–Kronheimer 1990) is: *one takes a principal SU(2)-bundle over a smooth four-manifold, equips it with a Riemannian metric, studies the moduli space of solutions to the anti-self-dual Yang–Mills equation F=−⋆F, and uses the structure of that moduli space — a five-dimensional cobordism between the manifold and a set of reducible points — to force the intersection form to be diagonal.* Every object named as gauge theory in that sentence is reconstructed below from the single i of dx₄/dt=ic; the one step that is not so reconstructible is identified explicitly at the end.

> **Theorem 14.12 (Object-by-object reconstruction of the 1982 proof).** *Each gauge-theoretic object in Donaldson's proof is a construction of the single complex structure of dx₄/dt=ic (Theorem 5.6), as follows.*
>
> *(1) [The SU(2) bundle] The Lie algebra 𝔰𝔲(2) is spanned by (i/2)σ_x, (i/2)σ_y, (i/2)σ_z, each anti-Hermitian — the single i applied to the Hermitian Pauli observables σ_k — and SU(2)=exp(𝔰𝔲(2)) is the flow generated by that i (Prop 14.3, Prop 2.1). The gauge group is the single i realized as a transport.*
>
> *(2) [The Riemannian metric] In the live reading x₄=ict, dx₄²=−c²dt² gives signature (1,3); the frozen reading t→−iτ gives x₄=cτ real, dx₄²=+c²dτ², signature (4,0). The Riemannian metric Donaldson imposes is the frozen sector of dx₄/dt=ic (Thm 13.5, Prop 14.5).*
>
