> *(3) [The equation F=−⋆F] At (k,n)=(2,4), ⋆²=+1, splitting Λ²=Λ²₊⊕Λ²₋ (dim=3 each), with Λ²₊≅Sym²(S⁺); the ASD equation is the condition F∈Λ²₋. Both the curvature F (anti-Hermitian, from (1)) and the split (from the frozen four-space, from (2)) are reconstructed from the primitive (Props 14.5, 14.6).*
>
> *(4) [The instanton number c₂] For F∈𝔰𝔲(2), writing F=iM with M Hermitian gives tr(F∧F)=−tr(M∧M) real; hence c₂=(1/8π²)∫_X tr(F∧F)∈ℤ, the instanton charge, with the single i effecting the Hermitization (Prop 14.7).*
>
> *(5) [The five-dimensional cobordism] The elliptic ASD deformation complex has index dim ℳ=8c₂−3(1+b⁺)=5 at c₂=1,b⁺=0; ellipticity holds only in the frozen (4,0) signature, so the finite-dimensional cobordism is a consequence of the frozen sector (Prop 14.8).*
>
> *Objects (1)–(5) — every object named as gauge theory in the proof — are thus reconstructed from dx₄/dt=ic.*

*Proof.* (1) The generators (i/2)σ_k are verified anti-Hermitian, σ_k Hermitian, so 𝔰𝔲(2)=i·{Hermitian traceless} (Prop 14.3). (2) The signature computations dx₄²=−c²dt² (live) and +c²dτ² (frozen) are verified (Thm 11.3, Thm 13.5). (3) ⋆²=+1 at (2,4) and dim Λ²±=3=dim Sym²(ℂ²) verified (Prop 14.5). (4) F∈𝔰𝔲(2) verified anti-Hermitian traceless, M=−iF Hermitian, tr(F∧F)=−2(a²+b²+c²) real verified (Prop 14.7). (5) 8(1)−3(1+0)=5 verified; ellipticity is the frozen-signature property of §10.6, Prop 10.7. All computations performed symbolically. ∎ **G1** for the constructions; **G2** for the identification of the i at each object with the primitive's single complex structure (Theorem 5.6).

> **Theorem 14.13 (The one step that is not reconstructible).** *The final inference of Donaldson's proof — that the five-dimensional cobordism forces the intersection form Q to be diagonal, Q≅diag(±1) — is not a construction of dx₄/dt=ic. It is the arithmetic of unimodular lattices (Elkies' theorem in the Seiberg–Witten route: the diagonal form is the unique positive-definite unimodular lattice with no characteristic vector of small norm), together with the smooth-realizability obstruction. This content carries no i, no metric, and no signature (Remark 14.9); it is the i-free topological core. The reconstruction of Theorem 14.12 therefore delivers the entire gauge-theoretic machinery up to this final arithmetic step, and stops there.*

*Proof.* The cobordism-counting endgame reduces the realizability question to a statement about characteristic vectors of the intersection lattice, an arithmetic fact independent of any complex structure (Remark 14.9, §10.6). ∎ **G1** that the step is i-free; the limit is asserted, not hedged.

> **Remark 14.14 (Reading of the result).** Theorem 14.12 makes precise the sense in which "the proof is gauge theory" and the sense in which the gauge theory "is the single i." Every object Donaldson names — SU(2), the metric, F=−⋆F, c₂, the cobordism — is reconstructed from dx₄/dt=ic, with no appeal to the historical Cartan–Chern transmission (§14.2–14.4) and with each algebraic step verified. The gauge theory was never an external tool applied to a separate topological substance; for these five objects it is the frozen single i at every step. The genuinely topological substance — the part that is not the single i — is precisely the final lattice-arithmetic inference (Theorem 14.13), which the framework does not claim and does not need. This is the exact and complete statement: the apparatus of the 1982 proof is dx₄/dt=ic machinery object by object; the diagonalization arithmetic at its terminus is not.

## 15. Geometric Langlands and the Same Single i: Apparatus, Lineage, and the Sociology of a Delayed Recognition

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

The lineage established for Donaldson (§13, §14) is not isolated. The same single complex structure — the connection-and-curvature apparatus carrying the i of dx₄/dt=ic — is the operative machinery of the geometric Langlands correspondence, present and load-bearing in its 1980s–1990s construction, and recognized as the S-duality of a four-dimensional quantum field theory only in 2006. This section establishes that parallel with the same dual rigor: the mathematics and physics of the apparatus, and the history and sociology of its delayed recognition. The honest boundary is marked as before — the arithmetic core of Langlands (the Galois–automorphic correspondence) is i-free and is not generated by the primitive — and the section closes by naming the methodological fallacy that the delayed recognition exemplifies, with an analogy that makes the fallacy unmistakable.

### 15.1 The Wright analogy: the fallacy of origin-by-date

A recurring error in reading these lineages is to suppose that because a foundational principle was articulated earlier and in simpler form, the later and more elaborate developments are not instances of it. The error is exhibited cleanly by an analogy. The Wright brothers achieved powered, controlled, fixed-wing flight in 1903; they died decades before the jet engine. It would be a plain fallacy to conclude that jet airliners "have nothing to do with" the Wrights — that because the Wrights predate jets and flew something far simpler, jets are a separate matter. On the contrary: every jet is powered controlled fixed-wing flight, the very thing the Wrights established, developed further. The principle is continuous; the later machine does not escape the origin by being more elaborate or by post-dating its originators. We name this the **origin-by-date fallacy**: inferring discontinuity of *principle* from succession of *date*.

The fallacy has appeared twice already and was corrected each time. Cartan's connection–curvature apparatus is not disqualified as the carrier of the single i by the fact that his *earliest* (pre-1908) work predates Minkowski (§13, Remark 13.7): the relevant apparatus is the 1922–25 work, and in any case the *single i* it carries is one object across all its appearances (Theorem 5.6), not a different i at each date. Likewise here: the single i in geometric Langlands is not a different i from the relativistic one merely because the curve, the D-module, and the moduli stack are complex-algebraic constructions bearing later names. It is one i, the relativistic one, developed further — the jet, not a separate craft.

### 15.2 The apparatus of geometric Langlands is the single i

For a smooth projective curve Σ and reductive group G with Langlands dual ᴸG, the geometric Langlands correspondence is (in its original de Rham form) an equivalence of derived categories

𝒪-Mod(Loc_{ᴸG}(Σ)) ≃ 𝒟-Mod(Bun_G(Σ)),

taking skyscraper sheaves to Hecke eigensheaves. Each object is built from the connection apparatus.

> **Proposition 15.1 (D-modules carry the single i).** *A D-module on Bun_G — the automorphic side — is a quasi-coherent module M with a flat connection ∇ = d + A, A valued in the (anti-Hermitian) Lie algebra of the structure group; equivalently A = iH with H Hermitian (Prop 14.3). The defining datum of a D-module is the single complex structure of dx₄/dt=ic, realized as ∇.*

*Proof.* A D-module is a module over the sheaf of differential operators, i.e. a module with a connection ∇ (Beilinson–Drinfeld; the objects are treated canonically in Frenkel 2007, *Langlands Correspondence for Loop Groups*, Ch. 1). Compatibility forces A anti-Hermitian; A = iH exhibits the single i (verified: A†+A = 0 for A=iH, H Hermitian). ∎ **G1** for the construction; **G2** that the i is the primitive's.

> **Proposition 15.2 (A Langlands parameter is a flat bundle — the i is its connection).** *A point of Loc_{ᴸG}(Σ) — a Langlands parameter on the spectral side — is a flat ᴸG-bundle E = (𝓕, ∇), a bundle with a flat connection. Flatness is the vanishing of the curvature of ∇, and ∇ carries the single i exactly as in Prop 15.1. The Langlands parameter is, in its very definition, the single complex structure realized as a flat connection.*

*Proof.* Loc_{ᴸG} is the moduli of flat connections / local systems (Frenkel 2005; canonically, Frenkel 2007, *Langlands Correspondence for Loop Groups*, Ch. 1, where the geometric Langlands parameter is defined as a vector bundle with flat connection on X, and on the punctured disc in the local case). A local system is (𝓕,∇) with ∇ flat; the connection is anti-Hermitian-valued, hence the single i (Prop 14.3). ∎ **G1**; **G2** for the identification.

> **Proposition 15.3 (The Hitchin system and the quaternionic/single-i selection).** *The construction proceeds through the Hitchin integrable system — the moduli of Higgs bundles (E,φ), φ∈End(E)⊗K_Σ — which carries a hyperkähler structure: a quaternionic triple (I,J,K), I²=J²=K²=−𝟙, IJ=K (verified). The de Rham (flat-connection) description, where the Langlands parameters live, is the selection of one distinguished complex structure from this triple, exactly as a one-parameter evolution selects a single J from the quaternionic algebra (Lemma 12.2, Stone). The single i of the correspondence is this distinguished de Rham complex structure.*

*Proof.* Hitchin moduli is hyperkähler (Hitchin 1987); the triple satisfies the quaternion relations (verified: I²=J²=K²=−1, IJ−K=0). Non-abelian Hodge theory (Corlette–Simpson) relates the Dolbeault (Higgs) and de Rham (flat-connection) descriptions, the latter singling out one complex structure — the single i — precisely as in the §12 collapse of the quaternionic triple to one J under observable evolution. ∎ **G1** for the hyperkähler algebra; **G2** for the single-i identification.

These establish that the geometric Langlands construction of the 1980s–90s — D-modules, local systems, the Hitchin system — is built on the connection/curvature apparatus carrying the single i (§13, §14), named there only as "flat connections," "D-modules," "local systems," "Higgs bundles."

### 15.3 The dates: the apparatus precedes the recognition

> **Proposition 15.4 (Chronology of construction versus recognition).** *(a) Number-theoretic Langlands originates in 1967 (Langlands' letter to Weil): Galois representations ↔ automorphic representations — i-free arithmetic. (b) Geometric Langlands is constructed in the 1980s–1990s (Drinfeld; Beilinson–Drinfeld; Laumon), on the connection/D-module/Hitchin apparatus of §15.2, internally to mathematics. (c) The identification of this apparatus with S-duality of four-dimensional 𝒩=4 super-Yang–Mills is made in 2006 (Kapustin–Witten). The gauge-theoretic apparatus carrying the single i was present and load-bearing in (b), two decades before the physics was named in (c). The 2006 work did not introduce the gauge structure; it recognized that the structure already present is S-duality.*

*Historical proof.* (a) Langlands to Weil, January 1967 (Frenkel, Gauge Theory and Langlands Duality). (b) Beilinson–Drinfeld, Quantization of Hitchin's Integrable System and Hecke Eigensheaves (1990s); Drinfeld and Laumon's automorphic-sheaf constructions; reviewed in Frenkel (2005). (c) Kapustin–Witten, Electric-Magnetic Duality and the Geometric Langlands Program, arXiv hep-th/0604151 (April 2006), Comm. Number Theory Phys. 1 (2007) 1–236. The apparatus of (b) predates (c). ∎ **G1** (documentary).

> **Proposition 15.5 (Kapustin–Witten: the recognition runs on the same single i).** *Kapustin and Witten obtain geometric Langlands by compactifying four-dimensional 𝒩=4 super-Yang–Mills on Σ and invoking S-duality τ↦−1/τ, which exchanges G with ᴸG. The four-dimensional gauge connection is 𝔲(N)-valued — anti-Hermitian — hence carries the single i (Prop 14.3, 13.1), the same i as the D-modules and flat connections of §15.2. 't Hooft operators become Hecke operators; 't Hooft eigenbranes become Hecke eigensheaves. Physics realization and mathematical construction run on one and the same single complex structure.*

*Proof.* The KW construction is the dimensional reduction of Frenkel (2005, §1) and Kapustin–Witten (2007): anti-Hermitian gauge connection (single i, Prop 14.3), S-duality on the complexified coupling τ, 't Hooft → Hecke. The i of the 4d connection is the i of the GL D-modules by Prop 15.1. ∎ **G1** for the gauge content; **G2** for the single-i identification.

### 15.4 The sociology of the delayed recognition

> **Proposition 15.6 (The recognition was delayed by the same "pure mathematics" framing as Donaldson).** *Geometric Langlands was constructed and pursued as pure mathematics — algebraic geometry, representation theory, category theory — with its connection/D-module/Hitchin apparatus named in those terms, not as physics. The physical content (S-duality) was recognized not at construction (1980s–90s) but in 2006, and received, as with Donaldson, as a surprising bridge between disciplines rather than as an identity. The program's originator does not work in the physical reformulation: asked whether he understands Witten's physics version, Langlands is on record declining to claim he does. The sociology is §13.9: apparatus was physics, named as mathematics, the physical identity experienced as an external surprise when finally seen.*

*Historical proof.* The "pure mathematics" pursuit is the documentary record (Frenkel 2005). The reception as a bridge "enriching both subjects" rather than an identity is standard (Frenkel 2005 §1; nLab). Langlands' distance from the physics is documented (IAS interview). ∎ **G1** (documentary); the §13.9 reading is **G2**.

> **Theorem 15.7 (The geometric Langlands parallel to Donaldson, at grade).** *(a) [Apparatus, G1/G2] Geometric Langlands is built on flat connections, D-modules, and the Hitchin system — the connection–curvature apparatus carrying the single i (Props 15.1–15.3). (b) [Chronology, G1] That apparatus was load-bearing in the 1980s–90s, two decades before Kapustin–Witten (2006) identified it as S-duality of 𝒩=4 super-Yang–Mills (Props 15.4, 15.5). (c) [Sociology, G1/G2] The delay is the §13.9 pattern: physics named as pure mathematics, the physical identity recognized late and received as a surprising external bridge (Prop 15.6). (d) [The single i, G2] By Theorem 5.6 the i in the D-modules, flat connections, Hitchin de Rham structure, and KW gauge theory is one and the same complex structure — the relativistic i — developed further, not a distinct i per construction (origin-by-date fallacy, §15.1, resisted).*

*Proof.* (a) Props 15.1–15.3; (b) Props 15.4–15.5; (c) Prop 15.6; (d) Theorem 5.6 with §15.1. ∎

### 15.5 The boundary: the arithmetic core is i-free

> **Remark 15.8 (What is not the single i, stated as plainly as in §14.9).** As with Donaldson, the reconstruction reaches the apparatus and stops at an arithmetic core. The original number-theoretic Langlands correspondence (1967) — Galois ↔ automorphic over number fields — is i-free arithmetic: reciprocity, L-functions, the arithmetic of number fields, no connection, no metric, no complex structure of the kind at issue. Geometric Langlands is the function-field/geometric analogue of that arithmetic correspondence. The framework's claim is bounded: the *apparatus* (connections, D-modules, Hitchin) carries the single i and is reconstructible from dx₄/dt=ic (Props 15.1–15.3); the *arithmetic content* it expresses — the reciprocity/automorphic core inherited from 1967 — is not generated by the primitive and is not claimed to be. The single i is the engine; the arithmetic is the cargo. To assert the primitive generates the arithmetic would be the category error of §10.6 and §14.9. **G1** that the arithmetic core is i-free; **G2** that the apparatus is the single i.

> **Remark 15.9 (The complete statement, with the analogy).** The single i of dx₄/dt=ic is the engine of the geometric Langlands apparatus exactly as it is the engine of Donaldson's proof: present, load-bearing, named as mathematics, recognized as physics only late (2006) and with surprise. The jet is powered fixed-wing flight developed further; geometric Langlands is the single i — the relativistic complex structure, carried by the connection apparatus — developed further. That the Wrights predate the jet does not make the jet a separate principle; that Minkowski and Cartan and the relativistic metric predate Beilinson–Drinfeld does not make the geometric Langlands connection a separate i. It is one i, one continuous lineage, recognized in 2006 to be the gauge-theoretic engine it had always been — while the arithmetic cargo it carries remains, honestly, the i-free core the framework illuminates the engine *for* but does not replace.

## 16. The Kapustin–Witten Dictionary as the Bidirectional Klein Correspondence: a Term-by-Term G2 Mapping

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

Section 15 established that geometric Langlands is built on the connection apparatus carrying the single i, and that its physical realization (Kapustin–Witten 2006) runs on the same i, with the G↔ᴸG duality identified there as a candidate for the Channel A ↔ Channel B exchange. This section discharges that candidate at G2 by mapping the Kapustin–Witten S-duality dictionary term-by-term onto the source-pair (𝓜_G, D_M) and its bidirectional Klein correspondence (the McGucken Duality). The source-pair's two faces — the operator D_M = ∂_t + ic ∂_{x₄} (algebraic-symmetry, Channel A) and the manifold 𝓜_G (geometric-propagation, Channel B) — are shown to correspond, entry by entry, to the electric and magnetic sides of the Kapustin–Witten construction, with S-duality the exchange and the 't Hooft/Hecke operator the exchange operator. The single i is verified common to all entries. The section closes by marking, exactly as §15.8, the arithmetic core that lies outside the dictionary and is not claimed.

### 16.1 The S-duality involution and the electric/magnetic faces

> **Proposition 16.1 (S-duality is an exchange of the two faces).** *Kapustin–Witten realize geometric Langlands by compactifying four-dimensional 𝒩=4 super-Yang–Mills on a Riemann surface and invoking the S-duality acting on the complexified coupling τ = θ/2π + 4πi/g² by τ↦−1/τ. At θ=0 this sends τ = 4πi/g² ↦ ig²/4π (verified), i.e. g↦4π/g — weak coupling to strong, electric to magnetic, and the gauge group G to its Langlands dual ᴸG. The electric description is carried by the Wilson line exp(i∮A), a functional of the connection — the operator/algebraic face; the magnetic description is carried by the 't Hooft line, a prescribed monopole singularity of the bundle — the geometric face. S-duality is the involution exchanging these two faces.*

*Proof.* The S-duality action on τ and the θ=0 weak/strong exchange are verified symbolically. The Wilson line exp(i∮A) is a function of the connection A (algebraic-operator datum); the 't Hooft line is defined by a singular monopole boundary condition on the gauge field (Kapustin–Witten 2007; Frenkel 2005). The electric/magnetic exchange under τ↦−1/τ is the standard Montonen–Olive content of 𝒩=4 S-duality. ∎ **G1** for the coupling algebra and electric/magnetic content.

> **Theorem 16.2 (The electric face is D_M; the magnetic face is 𝓜_G).** *(i) [electric ↔ D_M] The Wilson line exp(i∮A) is the holonomy of the connection ∇ = d + A, A = iH anti-Hermitian, the single i realized as a transport (Prop 14.3, 15.1) — the operator/algebraic face D_M, whose flow exp(itD_M) is the unitary evolution (Channel A). (ii) [magnetic ↔ 𝓜_G] The 't Hooft line is a monopole modification of the bundle geometry over the curve — a geometric-propagation datum on the manifold of bundles, the face 𝓜_G (Channel B). (iii) [S-duality ↔ the bidirectional Klein swap] The exchange τ↦−1/τ, G↔ᴸG, is the exchange of the two faces — precisely the bidirectional Klein correspondence Klein-corresp(𝓜_G,D_M) ↔ Klein-corresp(D_M,𝓜_G) that defines the McGucken Duality.*

*Proof.* (i) The Wilson line is the holonomy P exp(i∮A); by Prop 14.3 its i is the single complex structure, and D_M is the operator whose flow is the associated unitary evolution. (ii) The 't Hooft operator prescribes a singular bundle modification — a geometric datum on Bun_G, the 𝓜_G face. (iii) S-duality exchanges (i) and (ii); the McGucken Duality is by definition the bidirectional reading exchanging the D_M and 𝓜_G faces. Term-by-term. ∎ **G2** — a structural identification resting on Theorem 5.6 and the source-pair architecture, not a derivation that the gauge fibre is geometrically x₄.

### 16.2 The 't Hooft/Hecke operator as the exchange operator

> **Proposition 16.3 ('t Hooft = Hecke = pointwise bundle modification = the exchange operator).** *Under the Kapustin–Witten compactification the 't Hooft operator becomes the Hecke operator of geometric Langlands, and the 't Hooft "eigenbrane" becomes the Hecke eigensheaf. Both are realized as the same geometric operation: a modification of the G-bundle in a neighborhood of a point x of the curve (an elementary/Hecke modification E⇝E' agreeing with E away from x). This pointwise bundle modification is the operator implementing the exchange of the two faces — the exchange operator of the bidirectional Klein correspondence.*

*Proof.* The 't Hooft line at x is a prescribed gauge-field singularity at x, i.e. a bundle modification near x; the Hecke operator at x is the elementary modification of the bundle at x (Frenkel 2005; Kapustin–Witten 2007); their identification under compactification is the KW result. As a point-localized modification it maps the eigen-data of one face to the other — the role of the exchange operator. ∎ **G1** for the 't Hooft/Hecke identification (cited); **G2** for its role as the source-pair exchange operator.

### 16.3 The single i is common to every entry

> **Proposition 16.4 (One i across the dictionary).** *The four-dimensional 𝒩=4 gauge connection is 𝔲(N)-valued, anti-Hermitian, A = iH (verified A†+A=0). The same i appears in the Wilson-line holonomy exp(i∮A), in the geometric Langlands flat connection / D-module (Prop 15.1), and in the source-pair operator D_M = ∂_t + ic ∂_{x₄} through V(x₄)=ic. By Theorem 5.6 these are one complex structure. The dictionary's electric side, magnetic side, exchange, and the D_M/𝓜_G faces all carry the single i of dx₄/dt=ic.*

*Proof.* Anti-Hermiticity verified; the identity of the i across the Wilson line, the D-module connection, and D_M is Theorem 5.6 instantiated (Props 13.1, 14.3, 15.1). ∎ **G1** for the algebra; **G2** for the single-i identification.

> **Proposition 16.4a (Source-confirmed witness: the geometric Langlands complex structure is selected at the parameter value i).** *In the Kapustin–Witten construction (hep-th/0604151v3) the topological field theory obtained by twisting 𝒩=4 super-Yang–Mills is parametrized by a point t of an abstract ℂP¹, which selects one complex structure from the hyper-Kähler family (I,J,K), I²=J²=K²=−1, on the Hitchin moduli space 𝓜_H (their §3–4; our Prop 15.3). The value of t relevant to the geometric Langlands program is fixed by −t⁻¹=t, i.e. t²=−1, i.e. t=±i (verified). At t=±i, writing the complexified connection 𝒜 = A + iφ with curvature ℱ = d𝒜 + 𝒜∧𝒜, the localization equations reduce to ℱ = 0 — a complex flat connection, i.e. a Langlands parameter (Prop 15.2). The single i is therefore the operative parameter value: the point of the ℂP¹ of complex structures at which the Langlands-relevant flat connection appears. The coupling is τ = θ/2π + 4πi/e² (their canonical-parameter discussion), matching Prop 16.1 verbatim.*

*Proof.* The condition −t⁻¹=t has solutions t=±i over ℂ (verified: roots of t²+1). That the localization equations at t=±i reduce to ℱ=0 for 𝒜=A+iφ, yielding a complex flat connection (a homomorphism π₁→G_ℂ), is stated in the source and rests there on a theorem of Corlette — with the two-dimensional case attributed in the source to Donaldson (the appendix to Donaldson 1987), so the lineage of §14 and the dictionary of §16 meet at the source. The hyper-Kähler triple and the ℂP¹ family are their §3–4 (our Prop 15.3, verified I²=J²=K²=−1, IJ=K). ## 17. The Unnamed Invariance: Witten Uses the Moving i and Woit Sees the Signature, and Neither Names the Physical Fact

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

The lineage results of §§13–16 show the single i as the unrecognized engine of the connection-based mathematics of physics. This section sharpens the *unrecognized* into a documented fact about two of the field's most careful practitioners, working at the exact site of the framework's claim. Edward Witten *uses* the moving complex structure at every load-bearing step of the geometric Langlands construction — and never names it as a physical invariance. Peter Woit, the program's most prominent skeptic, *sees* the special role of the four-dimensional one-time signature, is on record that it "bothers" him and that he "doesn't know what to make of it" — and does not see that the physical fact resolving it is the advance of the fourth dimension at c. The section documents both, supplies the resolution each misses, and grades the claims.

### 17.1 Witten: the construction localizes onto the single i, unnamed as a physical fact

> **Proposition 17.1 (Witten's construction is built on the moving i at every load-bearing step).** *In Kapustin–Witten (hep-th/0604151v3) the following objects, each carrying the single complex structure, are load-bearing and were verified against the source (§16, Props 16.1–16.4a): (i) the 𝒩=4 gauge connection (anti-Hermitian, A=iH); (ii) the complexified coupling τ = θ/2π + 4πi/e²; (iii) the ℂP¹ family of complex structures on the Hitchin space, with the geometric-Langlands point selected at t=±i; (iv) the flat G_ℂ-connection ℱ=0 appearing precisely at t=i; (v) the Wick rotation ix_L⁰ = x_E⁰ fixing the spinor chirality via Γ_L = iΓ_E, so that Γ_E acts on S_± as ∓i. The construction localizes onto the single i — the Langlands-relevant physics appears at the parameter value i. Yet nowhere is this i named as a physical invariance; it is named "the canonical parameter," "Euclidean signature," "t=±i."*

*Proof.* (i)–(iv) are Props 16.1, 16.4, 16.4a, verified and source-cited; (v) is the source's chirality computation (ix_L⁰=x_E⁰, Γ_L=iΓ_E, Γ_E on S_± as ∓i), the Wick/signature-bridge use of the single i (Aspect A2, §2). That the i is not named as a physical fact about a fourth dimension is the absence, throughout the source, of any such statement — the construction proceeds in the inherited idiom in which i is a tool. ∎ **G1** that the construction localizes onto t=i and uses the Wick rotation (source-verified); **G2** that this i is the moving dimension's i (Theorem 5.6).

> **Remark 17.2 (The shape of the non-recognition).** Witten's case is the §13.9–§15.4 pattern in its purest form: the moving i is not hidden — it is in the title's "duality," in the canonical parameter, in the value t=i at which everything localizes — it is *used openly and named locally*. What is absent is the recognition that the i is a physical fact: that the reason the construction works at t=i is that the world's fourth dimension advances at ic, of which t=i is the frozen image. The construction is in the shadow of dx₄/dt=ic and calls the shadow "the canonical parameter." This identifies the unnamed physical content on which the mathematics runs.

### 17.2 Woit: the signature is seen, and explicitly not understood

> **Proposition 17.3 (Woit sees the signature structure and states it is unresolved).** *Woit observes that in four dimensions the metric signature admits essentially three cases: (a) the Euclidean (4,0) — "zero time dimensions, just four space dimensions," "nice mathematically"; (b) the one-time (1,3) — "that seems to be where we live, and that's where Minkowski saves time"; (c) the split signature (2,2) — in which "the whole story about spinors and reality and everything actually works most nicely," but which "as far as I know has nothing to do with the real world." He states that the situation "bothers me a little bit, I still don't know what to think about," and that he "can't see any possible conceivable relation to any question about the real world." The special role of the one-time four-dimensional signature is seen; its physical source is declared unknown.*

*Proof.* The three-case enumeration and the quoted phrases are in the dialogue transcript (the signature passage, ≈1:48–1:50). The reported epistemic state — seen, felt as significant, unresolved — is Woit's own characterization. ∎ **G1** (documentary; the speaker's stated position).

> **Theorem 17.4 (The framework resolves what Woit leaves open: the signature is forced by the advance).** *Woit's three-case "choice" is the count of independently moving imaginary axes, and dx₄/dt=ic specifies exactly one. (a) (4,0) is the static case — x₄ not advancing — which carries no physics (the frozen block, §10); zero moving axes. (b) (1,3) is one moving imaginary axis: dx₄ = ic dt gives dx₄² = −c²dt², one minus sign, one timelike direction (verified; Theorem 11.5). (c) (2,2) would require two independent moving imaginary axes — two factors of i in the metric — and the single complex structure of dx₄/dt=ic (Theorem 5.6) supplies exactly one. Hence the observed signature is (1,3), forced by the physical fact that one dimension advances at ic. The reason "spinors and reality work most nicely" in (2,2) — Woit's puzzle — is that a fully real (split) structure is the two-moving-axes world; the actual world has one moving axis, so its spinor is the single-complex spinor of §5, and its signature is (1,3). What Woit cannot relate to the real world is related to it by the advance: the real world is the one-moving-axis case because its fourth dimension is, physically, advancing at c.*

*Proof.* The signature count — zero/one/two moving imaginary axes giving (4,0)/(1,3)/(2,2) — is verified symbolically; the (1,3) derivation is Theorem 11.5; the single-complex-structure restriction to one timelike direction is Theorem 5.6 (the bilinear of a single-complex spinor lives in the Hermitian 2×2 matrices, whose invariant form is the Lorentzian determinant — exactly one timelike direction). The static case carries no physics by §10. ∎ **G1** for the signature count and the (1,3) derivation; **G2** that the selection among the three is the *physical* fact of a single advancing dimension rather than a free mathematical choice.

> **Remark 17.5 (The twistor ℂP¹ and the boundary, in Woit's own testimony).** Woit further reports being "completely amazed" that the twistor ℂP¹ — "a ℂP¹, a sphere with opposite points identified," "fundamental when you do twistor theory in physics, especially in Euclidean signature" — is "exactly the same mathematical structure" as the arithmetic object (the analog of the Fargues–Fontaine curve over the reals) appearing in the Scholze-style program bringing geometric and arithmetic Langlands together, and says "I don't know what to make of this." Its appearance on the *arithmetic* side (Fargues–Fontaine) is the i-free core the framework does not claim. That the *same* ℂP¹ shows up on both sides is exactly what the engine/cargo picture predicts and bounds: the apparatus-side ℂP¹ is the moving i's frozen sphere; the arithmetic-side appearance is the shared structure at the boundary, on the far side of which the framework does not reach. Woit's "I don't know what to make of this" is the unposed question; the framework's answer is that the physics-side ℂP¹ is the single i and the arithmetic-side ℂP¹ is the boundary it stops at — and that the two are related precisely because one is the engine and the other is where the engine's reach ends. **G2** for the identification of the physics-side ℂP¹ with the moving i; the arithmetic-side appearance is marked, per the standing boundary, as not claimed.

### 17.3 The joint statement

> **Theorem 17.6 (The invariance is in use and in view, and unnamed).** *The two leading figures at the site of the framework's claim instantiate the non-recognition from opposite directions. *Proof.* Prop 17.1 (Witten, source-verified), Prop 17.3 (Woit, documentary), Theorem 17.4 (the resolution, verified). ∎ **G1** for the documentary and computational content; **G2** for the identification of the used-and-viewed i with the moving dimension's i (Theorem 5.6).

> **Remark 17.7 (Why this is testimony, not triumphalism).** The point is not that two careful physicists erred — they did not; Witten's mathematics is correct and Woit's skepticism is honest and precise. The point is structural and is the thesis of the paper seen at the frontier: a physical invariance can be wholly in use and partly in view while remaining unnamed, because the inherited idiom — in which i is a tool and signature is a choice — has no slot for the physical fact. Woit's integrity is in fact the strongest witness available: he states plainly that the (2,2)/(1,3) structure is significant and that he cannot connect it to the real world, rather than papering the gap. The framework's contribution is to supply the missing slot — the advance dx₄/dt=ic — into which both the used i (Witten) and the viewed signature (Woit) fall as the same physical fact. That the slot, once supplied, resolves a puzzle the skeptic explicitly left open is the relevant evidence.

### 17.4 The Textbook Record: Physics Load-Bearing in the Definitive Langlands Monograph, with Provenance Absorbed

The non-recognition documented for Witten and Woit (§§17.1–17.3) extends beyond research talks into the field's canonical pedagogical source. The finding sharpens Remark 16.8: the physics is *load-bearing in the proofs*, beyond being the historical origin of the apparatus, and its provenance is progressively absorbed into mathematics as the text approaches the Langlands statement.

Each is a construction of two-dimensional conformal field theory or current algebra, used not as motivation but as a step on which later theorems depend.*

The OPE provenance and use are stated at the cited passages; the Sugawara operators' centrality at the critical level is the construction of the Feigin–Frenkel center (Remark 16.8); the Wakimoto/free-field and W-algebra machinery is the working content of the named chapters. ∎ **G1** (documentary, read in full).

The FMS realization of the βγ-system M↪Π₀ (Theorem 7.2.3 of the monograph) is used because, in the text's words, it "allows us to make sense of the field a(z)^χ for arbitrary complex χ" — the step that defines the screening operator. The cited source is, verbatim, Friedan, Martinec & Shenker, "Conformal invariance, supersymmetry and string theory," Nuclear Physics B 271 (1986). The screening operators of Chapter 7 build toward the principal theorem of Chapter 8 (the identification of the center with functions on opers). *Proof.* The FMS bosonization passage (the βγ-system embedding, the "arbitrary complex χ" motivation, the screening-operator construction) and the verbatim bibliographic entry were read in full in Chapter 7 and the bibliography. That Chapter 7's screening operators feed Chapter 8's center–opers theorem is the monograph's own architecture. ∎ **G1** (documentary, read in full): the dependency is stated in the text and the source is a string-theory paper.

> **Proposition 17.9a (The load-bearing physics is uniformly the single complex structure — not physics in general).** *The claim of §17.4 is that the specific physics that is load-bearing in Frenkel (2007) is uniformly the physics of a single complex structure — the moving i — and nothing else physical. A field is a formal power series in End V[[z^±1]]"), and locality is (z−w)^N[Y(A,z),Y(B,w)]=0 on the complex plane, with the text stating "z and w [are] complex numbers (points on the Riemann sphere)." ## 17A. Atiyah's Stated Lineage and the Dual-Channel Containment of the Schrödinger–Dirac / Heisenberg Dichotomy

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

Sections 17.1–17.4 documented the moving i in use and unnamed across Witten, Woit, and the canonical monograph. This section turns to the geometer who supervised that lineage's central figure and who stated, in his own voice, both the methodological commitments the framework adopts and a structural dichotomy the framework's dual-channel architecture contains. The source is Atiyah's 2010 lecture *From Quantum Physics to Number Theory*. The material here is documentary (the quotations) together with one structural identification at grade **G2**; it does not extend the central theorems, and it does not claim Atiyah's endorsement of dx₄/dt = ic — the opposite, his independence from it, is what gives the convergence its evidential weight.

### 17A.1 The stated lineage: Einstein, Dirac, and the pursuit of a single beautiful source

> **Proposition 17A.1 (Atiyah's self-placement in the Einstein–Dirac geometric tradition, documentary).** *In the 2010 lecture Atiyah states his methodological commitments and lineage explicitly: "I classify myself as a follower of Einstein and Dirac. I believe the same things that they believe in — the importance of beauty, the aim for simplicity, aim for a fundamental theory we can understand." He defends Einstein's late unified-field programme against the standard dismissal: "if I'm in the same class as Einstein I'm quite happy to be criticized — it's a good gang to belong to, Einstein and Dirac." He further identifies his synthetic aim — locating the common structural source behind disparate developments — as a mystic's: "I'm a mystic… Links have been found between the works of all three of these people [Witten, Penrose, Connes] and the links getting stronger as we go along."*

*Documentary basis.* The three quotations are transcribed verbatim from the lecture. ∎ **G1** (documentary).

The framework's own methodological self-placement — the Wheeler charge to seek the simple beautiful idea behind it all (Remark 1A.7), the program of exhibiting one moving complex structure as the common constituent of fields presenting themselves as separate (§§13–17) — is the same commitment Atiyah names. Wheeler's "behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful" and Atiyah's "aim for simplicity, aim for a fundamental theory we can understand" are the same charge, stated by two members of the lineage. This is corroboration of the framework's *method*, recorded without claim that either Wheeler or Atiyah endorsed the specific primitive.

### 17A.2 Atiyah's stated dichotomy, and its containment as the two channels of one source

Atiyah states, as a fork in the philosophy of physics, a dichotomy between two schools:

> **Proposition 17A.2 (Atiyah's Schrödinger–Dirac / Heisenberg dichotomy, documentary).** *Atiyah locates the difference between his approach and Connes's in the older split between Heisenberg's and Schrödinger's foundations of quantum mechanics: "Heisenberg developed… non-commutative algebra… and Connes is very much in the spirit of Heisenberg, whereas Schrödinger wrote down a differential equation and Dirac wrote down an even better equation… I belong to the Schrödinger–Dirac school and Connes belongs to the Heisenberg school." The split is stated as an either/or: the algebraic/operator/noncommutative route on one side, the differential/geometric/first-order route on the other.*

*Documentary basis.* Verbatim from the lecture. ∎ **G1** (documentary).

The framework's dual-channel architecture stands in an exact relation to this dichotomy, and the relation is the substance of the present subsection. Where Atiyah states a fork — one belongs to one school or the other — the framework states a source-pair: the two schools are the two readings of a single primitive, dx₄/dt = ic, under its two structural faces (Proposition 2.1: the first-order generator, whose *algebraic* content is the operator and whose *geometric* content is the flow).

> **Theorem 17A.3 (The dual-channel architecture contains Atiyah's dichotomy as the two faces of one source-pair).** *Let the source-pair be (𝓜_G, D_M), the geometric arena 𝓜_G carrying the spherical x₄-advance and the first-order operator D_M = ∂_t + ic ∂_{x₄} of Proposition 2.1. Then Atiyah's two schools are the two channels of this single source:*
>
> *(i) [Heisenberg/Connes channel = the algebraic face] The operator content of D_M — the single anti-Hermitian generator iH whose exponential is the unitary flow (Stone, Theorem 11.7), the canonical commutation relation it induces, and the noncommutative/spectral structure built on it (the Connes spectral-triple data the corpus assembles over ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ)) — is the algebraic reading of the primitive. This is the Heisenberg school's object: the generator as an algebraic operator.*
>
> *(ii) [Schrödinger/Dirac channel = the geometric face] The flow content of D_M — the differential equation whose first-order Lorentz-invariant form is the Dirac operator (Remark 2.3), the spinor as its square-root layer (§§3, 9), the geometric propagation on 𝓜_G (Huygens/spherical advance) — is the geometric reading of the same primitive. This is the Schrödinger–Dirac school's object: the generator as a differential motion.*
>
> *The two channels are not two theories to choose between; they are the algebraic and geometric content of the one first-order generator. Atiyah's dichotomy is therefore resolved upward: one is not forced to belong to a school, because the schools are dual descriptions of dx₄/dt = ic. The structural form of this containment is the same as the Kapustin–Witten dictionary of Theorem 16.5 — there S-duality exchanges the electric face D_M and the magnetic face 𝓜_G of the one source; here the Schrödinger–Dirac/Heisenberg fork is the same exchange of the geometric and algebraic faces.*

*Proof.* The decomposition of D_M into an algebraic operator content and a geometric flow content is Proposition 2.1 (a first-order operator is at once an algebraic generator and the infinitesimal motion of a flow) together with Theorem 11.7 (the operator face is Stone's iH) and §§3, 9 (the flow face is the Dirac/spinor square-root layer). That the algebraic face carries the noncommutative/spectral structure is the content of the corpus spectral-triple construction; that the geometric face carries the differential/propagation structure is §§3–9 of the present paper. The identification of the two faces with Atiyah's two named schools is the matching of (i) to "Heisenberg… non-commutative algebra… Connes" and (ii) to "Schrödinger… differential equation… Dirac," which is Proposition 17A.2's documentary content. The structural parallel to Theorem 16.5 is that both are the exchange of the (𝓜_G, D_M) faces: §16 exchanges them by S-duality, the present theorem by the algebraic/geometric reading. ∎ **G2** — a structural identification carried by Proposition 2.1 and the (𝓜_G, D_M) source-pair, matched to Atiyah's documented dichotomy; the operator/flow duality of the first-order generator (Proposition 2.1) and Stone's theorem (Theorem 11.7) are the underlying G1 facts.

> **Remark 17A.4 (Why the containment is the natural reading, not a forced reconciliation).** Atiyah presents the dichotomy as a matter of allegiance — he *belongs* to one school. Connes, on the other side, builds the Standard Model from the spectral triple, the Heisenberg-algebraic route. The framework integrates the Connes construction (the gauge group from ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ)) as the algebraic face and the spinor/Dirac geometry as the geometric face, and the source-pair (𝓜_G, D_M) is what both are faces of. The allegiance dissolves because the object both schools study is one first-order generator with two contents. This is the same move the paper makes at every lineage result: a split presented as a dichotomy (external tool vs intrinsic mathematics in §13; electric vs magnetic in §16; algebraic vs geometric here) is resolved as the two readings of the single moving i.

### 17A.3 The Atiyah–Moore relativistic retardation operator exp(−rD)

> **Proposition 17A.5 (Atiyah's unique first-order retardation generator, documentary, and its place in the framework).** *In the 2010 lecture Atiyah describes joint work with Greg Moore proposing a relativistically invariant notion of retardation: the one-dimensional shift exp(−r ∂/∂t) generalizes, in Minkowski space, to exp(−rD) with D the Dirac operator, "the only first-order differential operator invariant under [the] Lorentz group." Atiyah states the uniqueness as forcing: "If you want to introduce retardation into conventional Lorentz-invariant physics, this is the only choice. There's nothing else you can do because Dirac discovered this was the only operator you can use." He further notes that the construction attaches a length scale (a shift set by the Compton wavelength) and a second constant he reads as a cosmological constant.*

*Documentary basis and framework placement.* The quotations are verbatim. The operator-theoretic content — that retardation/translation is the exponential of a first-order operator, and that the unique Lorentz-invariant first-order operator is the Dirac operator — is exactly Proposition 2.1 together with Remark 2.3. The framework's reading: Atiyah's unique first-order retardation generator D is, under the canonical ontology, the first-order x₄-generator dx₄/dt = ic (the imaginary unit the perpendicularity flag of the fourth dimension; t the parameter clocks return as they trace the x₄-advance). That Atiyah's construction couples a quantum scale (the Compton wavelength) to a cosmological constant through a single first-order generator is the structural shape of the corpus gravitational-Compton-clock content; it is recorded here as a target for that connection, not as a result of this paper. ∎ **G1** (documentary) for the quotations and the identification with Proposition 2.1; **G3** (lead) for the Compton/cosmological-constant coupling as a target.

### 17A.4 The Magic Square / octonion-gravity proposal: an alternative architecture, addressed at full weight

Atiyah's constructive proposal in the lecture is not the framework's, and honesty requires stating it at full strength rather than absorbing it.

> **Proposition 17A.6 (Atiyah's octonion-gravity / exceptional-group proposal, documentary).** *Atiyah proposes that the four normed division algebras ℝ, ℂ, ℍ, 𝕆 correspond to the four fundamental forces, with gravity assigned to the octonions and the exceptional Lie groups G₂, F₄, E₆, E₇, E₈ as the structures through which an octonionic theory of gravity would be expressed: "the octonions… correspond to… gravity… because the octonions [are] much harder, gravity is much harder. But because the octonions are also very beautiful… gravity should also be very beautiful too… gravity is seen to be very much [a] consequence of the octonions and the exceptional groups." He bases this on the magic-square correspondence between the division algebras (dimensions 1, 2, 4, 8) and a ladder of geometries.*

*Documentary basis.* Verbatim (with the transcript's evident ambiguities in the force-to-algebra assignment preserved as Atiyah's). ∎ **G1** (documentary).

> **Remark 17A.7 (The framework's position relative to the octonion proposal, and the open question stated honestly).** Four points, kept separate and at their true grades. *(a) [Acknowledgment, at full weight.]* The magic-square content — the division-algebra ladder ℝ/ℂ/ℍ/𝕆 in dimensions 1/2/4/8, the Hurwitz finality (there are exactly four normed division algebras), and the exceptional groups — is real mathematical structure, and the division-algebra ladder already appears load-bearingly in the present paper: ℂ is the single-complex (moving, Lorentzian) sector of Theorem 5.6 and ℍ is the static SU(2)×SU(2) sector of the same theorem (and of Proposition 10.1, Remark 12.5). The framework does not ignore the ladder; it uses its first two rungs as the moving/static dichotomy. *(b) [Where the proposals differ.]* Atiyah assigns gravity to the *octonions* — a route through 𝕆 and the exceptional groups, a different Channel-A architecture from the framework's. The framework does not derive gravity from the octonions; it derives gravity as a consequence of dx₄/dt = ic (the corpus gravitational-Compton-clock and GR content), with the gauge group G_SM = U(1)×SU(2)×SU(3) obtained from the ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ) spectral data, not from the exceptional series. *(c) [The framework's stated position.]* Gravity, in the framework, is not additional content beyond the primitive but a derived consequence of the x₄-advance; the octonionic/exceptional structure is therefore not required as a separate input for gravity. *(d) [The open question, not hidden.]* Whether dx₄/dt = ic generates the exceptional-group/octonion content at all — as downstream structure, as an alternative equivalent description, or not — is open. Three outcomes are possible and none is here asserted: the primitive's ℂ/ℍ rungs may extend to 𝕆 in some derived construction; or the gauge-group derivation may supersede the octonionic route, making it unnecessary; or the two architectures may be genuinely distinct programs for gravity. The honest statement is that the framework's gravity is the derived x₄-consequence, Atiyah's is octonionic, and their relation is unresolved. **G3** (open); the division-algebra facts in (a) are **G1** and the Theorem 5.6 ℂ/ℍ placement is **G1/G2** as established there.

> **Open Problem 1′ (primitivity).** In Atiyah's own terms, *what is a spinor when there is no complex structure?* — which by Theorem 5.6 and Remark 5.7 is *what is geometry with no moving dimension?*, the static quaternionic sector. Derive from dx₄/dt = ic that admitting one complex structure (one moving x₄) makes the single-complex spinor S a *primitive* — that the square-root/generator layer (§9.1, Prop 2.1) is fundamental and the vector/tensor layer is its degree-two image — rather than admitting S as a premise of Theorem 5.6. By Prop 9.3 this is "why is geometry founded on its square root," and Atiyah's name for the program is a *spinor analysis* standing to the spinor as complex analysis stands to √−1. *Partial progress (Theorem 9.4A): the spinor arises as the homogeneous coordinate on the McGucken Sphere's null-direction ℂℙ¹, carrying the SU(2) double cover intrinsically (ℂℙ¹ = SU(2)/U(1)) without granting the single-complex spinor — so the spinor's existence and double cover descend from the Sphere's null geometry. The residual narrows to why the kinematic null-direction coordinate is also the dynamical generator layer (Remark 9.5), and rests on the corpus twistor-incidence identification (G2).*

> **Open Problem 2 (microcausality).** Derive the spacelike commutation/anticommutation dichotomy of QFT from x₄ transport, so that Thm 8.3 becomes a field-theoretic spin–statistics *theorem* rather than a single-particle reframing.

> **Open Problem 3 (the Hilbert–Pólya / Atiyah dream, stated with the boundary intact).** Atiyah closes the 2010 lecture by proposing that the Riemann hypothesis "should come out of quantum gravity… correspond to the Hamiltonian of quantum gravity," a fundamental operator whose spectrum would meet number theory — the Hilbert–Pólya dream restated with quantum gravity as the candidate source. The framework has a first-order generator (Proposition 2.1, the operator face D_M of Theorem 17A.3) and a geometric arena (the McGucken Sphere, 𝓜_G). The problem: determine whether the source-pair (𝓜_G, D_M) supplies the candidate Hamiltonian whose spectrum is the non-trivial zeros — and the answer must respect the arithmetic boundary the paper draws throughout. By Remarks 1A.6, 15.8, and 16.6, the i-free reciprocity core is *outside* the framework's claimed reach; Atiyah proposes the opposite, that quantum gravity *bridges* to it. The honest statement is therefore a fork held open without prejudice: either (a) the generator D_M is genuinely arithmetic-blind, in which case the framework's boundary stands and Atiyah's bridge, if it exists, runs through structure the primitive does not supply; or (b) the generator does meet the zeros, in which case Remark 1A.6's boundary would have to be revised and the mechanism by which a geometry-and-symmetry primitive reaches the i-free core would have to be exhibited — which the paper has nowhere done. The framework, like Atiyah with his "small bet," records this as the least-supported of its prospects and the place where it most explicitly does not claim to have crossed the arithmetic boundary. **G3** (open; stated to preserve the boundary discipline of §§1A, 15, 16, not to claim the crossing).

Open Problem 1′ is the residue of the square-root-counting gap also seen in the central-charge problem c = 6Q₁Q₅ in the Kaluza–Klein sector. With 1′ and 2 closed, the x₄ half-circuit picture of §8 becomes a full derivation of spin–statistics, and "the spinor is the fourth root of the McGucken interval" becomes a derived foundational proposition rather than a structural identity.

## 19. Conclusion: One Operation

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

The interval is quartic in the spinor (Thm 3.3); its bilinear square is null (Thm 3.2, 5.1); the null cone is the x₄-rest locus (ontology ii); the tensor square of the spinor is the exterior algebra of the x₄-arena (Thm 4.1); the 4π period is one circuit of the x₄-extended S³ with the sign parked in the x₄ scalar (Thm 7.1); and the single i doing all of this is the i of dx₄/dt = ic (Prop 6.1). Dirac extracted the square root of Klein–Gordon by introducing γ^μ — operators encoding the fourth axis. Atiyah called the spinor the square root of geometry and could not say, geometrically, of *what*.

> Dirac's square root of Klein–Gordon and Atiyah's square root of geometry are the **same operation** — the extraction of the x₄ axis. The spinor is the fourth root of the McGucken interval, and what it ultimately square-roots is the x₄-stationary null cone: the geometric meaning of √−1, made physical as dx₄/dt = ic.

Atiyah's two mysteries — √−1 and the spinor — are not two. They are the one i, seen twice.

And the magnitude is not free. The spinor's null cone and the x₄-expansion are a single constant entering a single interval (Thm 5.4): the spinor's lightcone pins the expansion to c, and were x₄ not expanding at c the spinor's bilinear square would lie on another cone — it would not be the object it is. Spinors and the motion of x₄ at c are mutually determined; that is the one place in this development where the motion itself, beyond the fourth axis, does the work.

Beneath the magnitude lies the signature. A single-complex spinor — one i, one Hermitian norm — forces a four-space of signature (1,3), exactly one moving dimension, because its bilinear lives in the Hermitian 2×2 matrices whose only invariant form is the Lorentzian determinant (Thm 5.6). The timelike direction is the Born norm ⟨ψ|ψ⟩, built from the same i that is x₄ = ict. A fully static four-space is the quaternionic SU(2) × SU(2) world, in which that single i is replaced by an anticommuting triple and the complex spinor is no longer present. So the deepest reading of the question is exact: one i, one moving dimension — the imaginary unit of the wavefunction and the motion of x₄ are not two things.

And the same one i reaches the statistics. Exchange is a 2π rotation (Prop 8.1); a 2π rotation is (−1)^{2s} (Lemma 8.2); and that sign is, by Theorem 7.1, a half-circuit through x₄ (Theorem 8.3). Pauli exclusion becomes the cancellation of states carrying opposite x₄ half-circuit phase, and the fermion/boson split becomes the single-i/quaternionic split of Theorem 5.6 (Proposition 8.4) — a reason of the kind Duck and Sudarshan found absent from the analyticity-of-VEV proofs, contingent on the two open problems we have isolated. The square root, the signature, the rotation, and the statistics are one fact about dx₄/dt = ic, viewed at successive depths.

Finally, the double cover that underlies all of this — the half-angle, the 2π ↦ −1 — is the same square root once more (§9). The spatial rotation is the conjugation-square of the x₄-carrying transport (Lemma 9.1), just as the vector is the bilinear-square of the spinor (§3.2): one root, two faces, the observable world blind to the x₄-scalar that is the root's sign (Prop 9.3). Granting Theorem 5.6, the double cover is derived (Thm 9.4), and Atiyah's question narrows to its irreducible core — not what the spinor *is* (the fourth root of the x₄-interval) nor why it doubles (the conjugation square), but why geometry should be founded on its square root at all. In Atiyah's own words this is *what is a spinor when there is no complex structure* — which in Light Time Dimension is *what is geometry with no moving dimension* — and the program he named for answering it, a "spinor analysis" standing to the spinor as complex analysis stands to √−1, is in Light Time Dimension the calculus of the first-order x₄-generator (Prop 2.1) whose exponential is motion. That the rate is primitive and the coordinate its integrated shadow is, at last, the same statement as Atiyah's that the first-order operator is fundamental because it exponentiates to motion. That is the one question dx₄/dt = ic has not yet answered, and the one worth the next monograph.

And the static/moving split has a striking corollary in four-manifold geometry. Donaldson's exotic dimension four — the diagonalization theorem, the gauge invariants, the uncountable smooth structures on ℝ⁴ — lives in the definite (4,0) sector, which by Theorem 10.2 contains no relativity, no quantum mechanics, and not the Lorentz or unitary symmetries either requires: the most exotic *static* geometry known, and physically inert. The single i of dx₄/dt = ic is exactly the operation that injects all three at once (Theorem 10.3), carrying SO(4) → SO⁺(1,3), SU(2) × SU(2) → SL(2,ℂ), and the cone, the Born norm, and unitary evolution into existence. The expansion does not manufacture dimension four's topology — that is a static gift — but it is what makes dimension four *physical*, what turns Donaldson's frozen arena into a spacetime that can hold relativity, quantum mechanics, and the physical Dirac spinor of Atiyah. The square root, the signature, the rotation, the statistics, the cone's nonlocality, and the injection of physics into the static four-space are all one fact about dx₄/dt = ic, read at successive depths.

## 4 The McGucken Principle and the McGucken Sphere

*The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose volume defines a nonlocality.* *(anchor added in the present paper)*

### 4.1 Statement of the principle

**Principle 5** (McGucken, UNC 1998–99 dissertation appendix; FQXi 2008–13). The fourth dimension expands at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event: dx₄/dt = ic where x₄ = ict is the fourth axis of the four-manifold and c is the universal invariant rate.

The principle is not a postulate or hypothesis; it is established by the McGucken Proof from three independently verified physical premises: (i) the special-relativistic four-speed invariance u^μ u_μ = -c²; (ii) the empirical fact that photons emitted from any source spread spherically and isotropically at c; (iii) the identification of x₄ = ict as a physical axis whose every consequence corresponds to an empirically validated feature of physics. Premises (i) and (ii) are confirmed in every optical and particle-physics experiment performed since the seventeenth century. Premise (iii) is confirmed by the convergent empirical confirmation of every theorem the principle entails: the Schrödinger equation, the Born rule, the canonical commutator [q̂, p̂] = iℏ, the Schwarzschild metric, gravitational time dilation, the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy, the Bell–CHSH–Tsirelson bound. The principle’s physicality is established by the convergence of all three premises, each independently verified.

### 4.2 The atomic ontology of the McGucken framework

*We may define the McGucken Point/Sphere dx₄/dt = ic as follows: the equation reflects a point endowed with the action dx₄/dt = ic by which it becomes the sphere, and where all points on the sphere’s surface are in turn endowed with dx₄/dt = ic, defining the Lorentzian spacetime metric, distributing locality into nonlocality, and providing the physics of quantum mechanics and general relativity.* This is the foundational atom of the framework: not the bare point and not the bare sphere, but the *Point endowed with the action that makes it a sphere*, with the same action present at every surface point so that the recursion Point → Sphere → surface of Points → Spheres → …continues ad infinitum (Huygens’ Principle elevated from heuristic to foundational mechanism).

The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic generates a four-level atomic ontology, with each level the carrier of a specific structural content of the principle. We state the ontology as a single table, then unpack each level in the subsections that follow. The table is the structural skeleton of the framework; every theorem in the paper is rooted in some level of this skeleton, and the QM–GR unification is the recognition that both quantum mechanics and general relativity are projections of the same atomic-ontology structure.
